### A note for the community

**Vector version:** 0.57.0

### Summary

The `loki` sink reports `component_sent_bytes_total` **after** compression. Other sinks, such as `datadog_logs`, report it **before** compression, which is what the [component spec](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/8832452f57afb536ea0de53a093f9fd1b669ccec/docs/specs/component.md#componentbytessent) and #20610 say it should be.

The result is that the same logs sent to two sinks show very different sizes. That makes the metric misleading for capacity planning and cost comparisons.

### What we see

We send the same log stream to both a `datadog_logs` sink and a `loki` sink (snappy compression). We compare `component_sent_bytes_total` to `component_sent_event_bytes_total` for each:

| Sink | `sent_bytes` ÷ `sent_event_bytes` |
|---|---|
| `datadog_logs` | ~1.0 |
| `loki` | ~0.2 |

- For `datadog_logs`, bytes sent roughly equals event bytes, which is what we expect.
- For `loki`, bytes sent is about 5× smaller, which fits the compressed payload size rather than the uncompressed one. Loki's own ingest metrics agree with the event-bytes figure.

### Why it happens

The `loki` sink uses the shared default `RequestBuilder::encode_events`. That function compresses the payload first, then passes the **compressed** length into the slot meant for the **uncompressed** size:

- [`src/sinks/util/request_builder.rs#L99-L101`](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/8832452f57afb536ea0de53a093f9fd1b669ccec/src/sinks/util/request_builder.rs#L99-L101): `compressed_byte_size = payload.len()` (already compressed) is passed as the `uncompressed_byte_size` argument of [`EncodeResult::compressed`](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/8832452f57afb536ea0de53a093f9fd1b669ccec/src/sinks/util/request_builder.rs#L41-L53).

That value then flows into the metric:

1. [`src/sinks/util/metadata.rs#L93-L99`](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/8832452f57afb536ea0de53a093f9fd1b669ccec/src/sinks/util/metadata.rs#L93-L99): `uncompressed_byte_size` becomes `request_encoded_size`.
2. [`lib/vector-common/src/request_metadata.rs#L270-L310`](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/8832452f57afb536ea0de53a093f9fd1b669ccec/lib/vector-common/src/request_metadata.rs#L270-L310): it is stored and returned as-is.
3. [`src/sinks/loki/service.rs#L56-L57`](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/8832452f57afb536ea0de53a093f9fd1b669ccec/src/sinks/loki/service.rs#L56-L57): `bytes_sent()` returns `request_encoded_size()`.

By contrast, `datadog_logs` has its own builder. It measures the size **before** compressing:

- [`src/sinks/datadog/logs/sink.rs#L302-L313`](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/8832452f57afb536ea0de53a093f9fd1b669ccec/src/sinks/datadog/logs/sink.rs#L302-L313): `uncompressed_size = buf.len()` is taken before compression and passed to `EncodeResult::compressed`.

### Expected

`component_sent_bytes_total` should report uncompressed bytes for every sink, including `loki`. Any other siult `encode_events` with compression turned on is probably affected too.

### Suggested fix

In the default `encode_events`, record the payload length before compression and pass that as `uncompressed_datadog_logs` does.

### Problem

`component_sent_bytes_total` for the `loki` sink reports compressed bytes, unlike other sinks

body_text:
### Problem

With `ignore_older_secs` and `remove_after_secs` both set, the `file` source deletes files it has never read. A file whose modification time is older than `ignore_older_secs` is opened at its end (`SeekFrom::End` for `too_old` in `FileWatcher::new`). The first read returns 0 bytes, and `last_read_success` is initialised from the file's mtime. If that mtime is older than `remove_after_secs`, the `remove_after` branch in the file server removes the file straight away. No event from the file is ever emitted.

The documentation describes neither the skipping nor the deletion this way:

- `ignore_older_secs`: "Ignore files with a data modification date older than the specified number of seconds."
- `remove_after_secs`: "After reaching EOF, the number of seconds to wait before removing the file, unless new data is written."

I expected an ignored file to be left alone, or at least not deleted unread. "Reaching EOF" here means seeking to the end, not reading to it.

### Reproduction

Every value is scaled down to seconds:

```yaml
# vector.yaml
data_dir: /data
sources:
  f:
    type: file
    include: [/logs/*.log]
    ignore_older_secs: 60
    remove_after_secs: 30
sinks:
  out:
    type: console
    inputs: [f]
    encoding:
      codec: text
```

```sh
mkdir -p logs data
printf 'unread line 1\nunread line 2\nunread line 3\n' > logs/old.log
touch -d '-90 seconds' logs/old.log
timeout 12 docker run --rm -v "$PWD/logs:/logs" -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
  -v "$PWD/vector.yaml:/etc/vector/vector.yaml:ro" timberio/vector:0.58.0-debian \
  --config /etc/vector/vector.yaml
ls logs
```

Output (0.58.0 and 0.49.0 behave the same):

```
INFO vector: Vector has started. debug="false" version="0.58.0" arch="x86_64" revision="2bcad9b 2026-08-26 13:37:07.557544670"
INFO ... Found new file to watch. file=/logs/old.log
INFO ... File deleted. file=/logs/old.log
```

No `unread line` event is printed and `logs/` is empty afterwards.

The file must be younger than the host's uptime to reproduce this. For an older file, `Instant::now().checked_sub(age)` underflows, and `last_read_success` falls back to "now".

### Impact

We hit this in production. Vector fell behind after a restart, and the backlog grew older than `ignore_older_secs`. On the next restart every backlog file was opened at its end, then deleted by `remove_after_secs` without being read, and data was lost for good. We now refuse any `ignore_older_secs` below `remove_after_secs` in our deploy tooling.

### Suggestion

Either never remove a file that was skipped by `ignore_older_secs` (one that was not read to its end), or document clearly that combining the two options deletes unread files.

### Version

0.58.0 (2bcad9b), also 0.49.0 (dc7e792). Docker images `timberio/vector:*-debian`, linux/amd64.

I expected an ignored file to be left alone, or at least not deleted unread. "Reaching EOF" here means seeking to the end, not reading to it.

### Reproduction

Every value is scaled down to seconds:

```yaml
# vector.yaml
data_dir: /data
sources:
  f:
    type: file
    include: [/logs/*.log]
    ignore_older_secs: 60
    remove_after_secs: 30
sinks:
  out:
    type: console
    inputs: [f]
    encoding:
      codec: text
```

```sh
mkdir -p logs data
printf 'unread line 1\nunread line 2\nunread line 3\n' > logs/old.log
touch -d '-90 seconds' logs/old.log
timeout 12 docker run --rm -v "$PWD/logs:/logs" -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
  -v "$PWD/vector.yaml:/etc/vector/vector.yaml:ro" timberio/vector:0.58.0-debian \
  --config /etc/vector/vector.yaml
ls logs
```

Output (0.58.0 and 0.49.0 behave the same):

```
INFO vector: Vector has started. debug="false" version="0.58.0" arch="x86_64" revision="2bcad9b 2026-08-26 13:37:07.557544670"
INFO ... Found new file to watch. file=/logs/old.log
INFO ... File deleted. file=/logs/old.log
```

No `unread line` event is printed and `logs/` is empty afterwards.

The file must be younger than the host's uptime to reproduce this. For an older file, `Instant::now().checked_sub(age)` underflows, and `last_read_success` falls back to "now".

### Impact

We hit this in production. Vector fell behind after a restart, and the backlog grew older than `ignore_older_secs`. On the next restart every backlog file was opened at its end, then deleted by `remove_after_secs` without being read, and data was lost for good. We now refuse any `ignore_older_secs` below `remove_after_secs` in our deploy tooling.

### Suggestion

Either never remove a file that was skipped by `ignore_older_secs` (one that was not read to its end), or document clearly that combining the two options deletes unread files.

### Version

0.58.0 (2bcad9b), also 0.49.0 (dc7e792). Docker images `timberio/vector:*-debian`, linux/amd64.

## Version
vector 0.58.0 (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl 2bcad9b 2026-08-26). The disk_v2 reader read path is unchanged on `master` as of 2026-10-05.

## Summary
After Vector restarts with history in a disk buffer, the reader's ledger position (`reader_last_record` in `buffer.db`) advances past records that the sink has read but not yet delivered: the request in flight and the next batch. If Vector is then killed with SIGKILL, the next start resumes after those records, and they are never delivered. The first crash after a start with no history behaves correctly: the ledger stays at the last delivered record and the in-flight batch is replayed.

## Minimal reproduction
Pipeline: `http_server` source, `http` sink with `buffer.type: disk`, `batch.max_events: 1000`, `batch.timeout_secs: 1`, `request.concurrency: 1`. A local HTTP destination holds request A, releases it while holding the next request B, Vector is SIGKILLed, and B is then counted as delivered. This mimics a database that commits B after the client died. Events are published continuously at 100/s with a unique `seq`. The script is below; `REMAP=0 HOLD=2 python3 repro.py 3` takes about 80 seconds.

Observed (`ledger_acked` is read from `buffer.db` immediately before SIGKILL):

```
cycle 1: A=410-510 B=511-611 ledger_acked=510 writer_next=763
  after restart: missing 0 []..; duplicate deliveries 101
cycle 2: A=2984-3084 B=3085-3185 ledger_acked=3186 writer_next=3336
  after restart: missing 1 [3186]..[3186]; duplicate deliveries 0
cycle 3: A=5559-5659 B=5660-5760 ledger_acked=5761 writer_next=5911
  after restart: missing 1 [5761]..[5761]; duplicate deliveries 0
```

In cycle 1, the ledger equals the last delivered record (510) and B is replayed. In cycles 2 and 3, the ledger is already past B (still held, never answered) and past the next batch (one record) at the moment of SIGKILL. After the restart, B is not replayed and the next batch is lost.

Bench confirmation with the `postgres` sink and the `mqtt` source on the same version: 5 of 6 consecutive SIGKILLs lost the batch queued after the in-flight request (1 or 99 events), and the in-flight batch was never replayed.

## Suspected cause (not confirmed)
`BufferReader::seek_to_next_record` replays already-acknowledged records through `next()` to reposition the reader. `next()` attaches a `BatchNotifier` and calls `self.finalizer.add(...)` for every record (`lib/vector-buffers/src/variants/disk_v2/reader.rs`, around lines 1220–1224). `track_read` skips marker registration while `!ready_to_read`. The records dropped during seek would then produce acknowledgements with no matching marker. Those unclaimed acknowledgements would credit later records as soon as they are read.

## Repro script

```python
#!/usr/bin/python3
"""Throwaway: mirror the fixture's two-gate handoff against a real Vector 0.58.0 binary.

Live 1-event posts at RATE/s -> remap(reroute_dropped) -> disk buffer -> http sink
(batch 1000/1s, concurrency 1). Destination holds request A ~20 s, releases it,
holds B, SIGKILL Vector, then "commits" B like the orphaned PostgreSQL backend.
"""

import glob
import http.server
import json
import os
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import urllib.request

VECTOR = "/tmp/vec058/vector-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/vector"
RATE = int(os.environ.get("RATE", "100"))
REMAP = os.environ.get("REMAP", "1") == "1"


def free_port():
    s = socket.socket()
    s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    p = s.getsockname()[1]
    s.close()
    return p


class Dest:
    def __init__(self):
        self.counts, self.lock = {}, threading.Lock()
        self.hold = False  # hold the next arriving request
        self.held = []  # [(event, seqs)]
        self.commit_on_release = {}
        dest = self

        class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *a):
                pass

            def do_POST(self):
                body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
                seqs = [json.loads(l)["seq"] for l in body.splitlines() if l.strip()]
                with dest.lock:
                    held = dest.hold
                    if held:
                        dest.hold = False
                        ev = threading.Event()
                        dest.held.append((ev, seqs))
                if held:
                    ev.wait()
                    with dest.lock:
                        commit = dest.commit_on_release.pop(id(ev), True)
                    if commit:
                        dest.commit(seqs)
                    try:
                        self.send_response(200)
                        self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
                        self.end_headers()
                    except OSError:
                        pass
                    return
                dest.commit(seqs)
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
                self.end_headers()

        self.port = free_port()
        self.srv = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", self.port), H)
        threading.Thread(target=self.srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    def commit(self, seqs):
        with self.lock:
            for s in seqs:
                self.counts[s] = self.counts.get(s, 0) + 1

    def wait_held(self, n, secs=30):
        end = time.time() + secs
        while time.time() < end:
            with self.lock:
                if len(self.held) >= n:
                    return self.held[n - 1]
            time.sleep(0.01)
        raise SystemExit(f"no held request #{n}")


def config(work, src, dst):
    path = os.path.join(work, "vector.yaml")
    remap = (
        """transforms:
  admit:
    type: remap
    inputs: [in]
    drop_on_error: true
    drop_on_abort: true
    reroute_dropped: true
    source: |
      assert!(is_integer(.seq), "seq")
"""
        if REMAP
        else ""
    )
    sink_in = "admit" if REMAP else "in"
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(f"""data_dir: {work}/data
sources:
  in:
    type: http_server
    address: 127.0.0.1:{src}
    decoding: {{codec: json}}
{remap}sinks:
  out:
    type: http
    inputs: [{sink_in}]
    uri: http://127.0.0.1:{dst}/
    encoding: {{codec: json}}
    framing: {{method: newline_delimited}}
    batch: {{max_events: 1000, timeout_secs: 1}}
    request: {{concurrency: 1, timeout_secs: 60}}
    healthcheck: {{enabled: false}}
    buffer: {{type: disk, max_size: 268435488, when_full: block}}
""")
    return path


def start(cfg, work):
    with open(os.path.join(work, "vector.log"), "a") as log:
        return subprocess.Popen(
            [VECTOR, "--config", cfg, "--quiet"], stdout=log, stderr=log
        )


class Publisher(threading.Thread):
    def __init__(self, src, first):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.src, self.next, self.stop = src, first, False

    def run(self):
        t0 = time.time()
        i = 0
        while not self.stop:
            body = json.dumps({"seq": self.next}).encode()
            try:
                urllib.request.urlopen(
                    urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.src}/", data=body),
                    timeout=2,
                ).read()
                self.next += 1
                i += 1
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(0.05)
                continue
            d = t0 + i / RATE - time.time()
            if d > 0:
                time.sleep(d)


def ledger(work):
    with open(glob.glob(f"{work}/data/buffer/v2/out/buffer.db")[0], "rb") as f:
        return struct.unpack_from("<QHH4xQ", f.read())


def main(cycles):
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="vecrepro2-")
    try:
        dest, src = Dest(), free_port()
        cfg = config(work, src, dest.port)
        p = start(cfg, work)
        pub = Publisher(src, 1)
        pub.start()
        for cycle in range(1, cycles + 1):
            first = pub.next
            time.sleep(5)
            dest.hold = True  # gate 1: next request is A
            ev_a, a = dest.wait_held(len(dest.held) + 1)
            time.sleep(float(os.environ.get("HOLD", "20")))
            dest.hold = True  # gate 2 queued for the next request
            ev_a.set()  # A commits
            ev_b, b = dest.wait_held(len(dest.held) + 1)
            time.sleep(0.5)
            wn, _, _, rl = ledger(work)
            p.kill()
            p.wait()
            ev_b.set()  # orphaned backend commits B after the kill
            print(
                f"cycle {cycle}: A={a[0]}-{a[-1]} B={b[0]}-{b[-1]} ledger_acked={rl} writer_next={wn}",
                flush=True,
            )
            time.sleep(3)
            p = start(cfg, work)
            time.sleep(15)
            last = pub.next - 1
            seen = {s for s, c in dest.counts.items() if first <= s <= last}
            missing = sorted(set(range(first, last + 1 - RATE * 3)) - seen)
            dups = sum(
                c - 1 for s, c in dest.counts.items() if first <= s <= last and c > 1
            )
            print(
                f"  after restart: missing {len(missing)} {missing[:3]}..{missing[-3:] if missing else ''}; duplicate deliveries {dups}",
                flush=True,
            )
        pub.stop = True
        p.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
        p.wait(30)
        dest.srv.shutdown()
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3)
```

```python
                        dest.commit(seqs)
                    try:
                        self.send_response(200)
                        self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
                        self.end_headers()
                    except OSError:
                        pass
                    return
                dest.commit(seqs)
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Length", "0")
                self.end_headers()

        self.port = free_port()
        self.srv = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", self.port), H)
        threading.Thread(target=self.srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    def commit(self, seqs):
        with self.lock:
            for s in seqs:
                self.counts[s] = self.counts.get(s, 0) + 1

    def wait_held(self, n, secs=30):
        end = time.time() + secs
        while time.time() < end:
            with self.lock:
                if len(self.held) >= n:
                    return self.held[n - 1]
            time.sleep(0.01)
        raise SystemExit(f"no held request #{n}")


def config(work, src, dst):
    path = os.path.join(work, "vector.yaml")
    remap = (
        """transforms:
  admit:
    type: remap
    inputs: [in]
    drop_on_error: true
    drop_on_abort: true
    reroute_dropped: true
    source: |
      assert!(is_integer(.seq), "seq")
"""
        if REMAP
        else ""
    )
    sink_in = "admit" if REMAP else "in"
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(f"""data_dir: {work}/data
sources:
  in:
    type: http_server
    address: 127.0.0.1:{src}
    decoding: {{codec: json}}
{remap}sinks:
  out:
    type: http
    inputs: [{sink_in}]
    uri: http://127.0.0.1:{dst}/
    encoding: {{codec: json}}
    framing: {{method: newline_delimited}}
    batch: {{max_events: 1000, timeout_secs: 1}}
    request: {{concurrency: 1, timeout_secs: 60}}
    healthcheck: {{enabled: false}}
    buffer: {{type: disk, max_size: 268435488, when_full: block}}
""")
    return path


def start(cfg, work):
    with open(os.path.join(work, "vector.log"), "a") as log:
        return subprocess.Popen(
            [VECTOR, "--config", cfg, "--quiet"], stdout=log, stderr=log
        )


class Publisher(threading.Thread):
    def __init__(self, src, first):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.src, self.next, self.stop = src, first, False

    def run(self):
        t0 = time.time()
        i = 0
        while not self.stop:
            body = json.dumps({"seq": self.next}).encode()
            try:
                urllib.request.urlopen(
                    urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.src}/", data=body),
                    timeout=2,
                ).read()
                self.next += 1
                i += 1
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(0.05)
                continue
            d = t0 + i / RATE - time.time()
            if d > 0:
                time.sleep(d)


def ledger(work):
    with open(glob.glob(f"{work}/data/buffer/v2/out/buffer.db")[0], "rb") as f:
        return struct.unpack_from("<QHH4xQ", f.read())


def main(cycles):
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="vecrepro2-")
    try:
        dest, src = Dest(), free_port()
        cfg = config(work, src, dest.port)
        p = start(cfg, work)
        pub = Publisher(src, 1)
        pub.start()
        for cycle in range(1, cycles + 1):
            first = pub.next
            time.sleep(5)
            dest.hold = True  # gate 1: next request is A
            ev_a, a = dest.wait_held(len(dest.held) + 1)
            time.sleep(float(os.environ.get("HOLD", "20")))
            dest.hold = True  # gate 2 queued for the next request
            ev_a.set()  # A commits
            ev_b, b = dest.wait_held(len(dest.held) + 1)
            time.sleep(0.5)
            wn, _, _, rl = ledger(work)
            p.kill()
            p.wait()
            ev_b.set()  # orphaned backend commits B after the kill
            print(
                f"cycle {cycle}: A={a[0]}-{a[-1]} B={b[0]}-{b[-1]} ledger_acked={rl} writer_next={wn}",
                flush=True,
            )
            time.sleep(3)
            p = start(cfg, work)
            time.sleep(15)
            last = pub.next - 1
            seen = {s for s, c in dest.counts.items() if first <= s <= last}
            missing = sorted(set(range(first, last + 1 - RATE * 3)) - seen)
            dups = sum(
                c - 1 for s, c in dest.counts.items() if first <= s <= last and c > 1
            )
            print(
                f"  after restart: missing {len(missing)} {missing[:3]}..{missing[-3:] if missing else ''}; duplicate deliveries {dups}",
                flush=True,
            )
        pub.stop = True
        p.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
        p.wait(30)
        dest.srv.shutdown()
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3)
```

## Version
vector 0.58.0 (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl 2bcad9b 2026-08-26), `postgres` sink with a disk buffer (`batch.max_events: 1000`, `request.concurrency: 1`), PostgreSQL 18.6.

## Problem
If PostgreSQL terminates the sink's session while an insert is running, the whole batch is dropped as a non-retriable error. This happens on a fast shutdown of the database (`57P01 admin_shutdown`), on the crash of any other backend (`57P02 crash_shutdown`), or on `pg_terminate_backend`. The disk buffer has already handed the batch to the sink, so it is lost even though the buffer is durable. The next request then fails on DNS or connection errors while the database is down, and *those* are retried, so everything after the dropped batch is delivered.

Observed when stopping the database container while ingesting 1,000 events/s (one batch exactly missing afterwards, 1,000 events):

```
ERROR sink{component_kind="sink" component_id=timescaledb component_type=postgres}:request{request_id=665}: vector::sinks::util::retries: Non-retriable error; dropping the request. error=Database error: error returned from database: terminating connection due to administrator command
ERROR ... vector_common::internal_event::service: Service call failed. No retries or retries exhausted. error=Some(Postgres { source: Database(PgDatabaseError { severity: Fatal, code: "57P01", message: "terminating connection due to administrator command", ... routine: Some("ProcessInterrupts") }) }) request_id=665 error_type="request_failed" stage="sending"
ERROR ... vector_common::internal_event::component_events_dropped: Events dropped intentional=false count=1000 reason="Service call failed. No retries or retries exhausted."
WARN  ... request{request_id=666}: vector::sinks::util::retries: Retrying after error. error=Database error: error communicating with database: failed to lookup address information: Try again
```

## Cause
`src/sinks/postgres/config.rs`, `PostgresRetryLogic::is_retriable_error`, only matches `sqlx::Error::Io(_) | sqlx::Error::PoolTimedOut`. Any `sqlx::Error::Database`, including session-termination errors, is treated as permanent.

## Proposal
Treat these SQLSTATEs as retriable:
- class `08` (connection exception);
- `57P01`, `57P02` and `57P03` (`admin_shutdown`, `crash_shutdown`, `cannot_connect_now`);
- optionally `40001` and `40P01` (serialization failure, deadlock).

This is no less safe than the `Io` case already retried. An `Io` error can arrive after the server committed, so an `Io` retry can duplicate rows. A `57P0x` raised while the statement runs means the transaction was rolled back, so a retry cannot duplicate anything.

### Problem

Unknown keys directly under a sink are rejected, but unknown keys under the `request` block of the `http` sink (and the `opentelemetry` sink with `protocol.type: http`) pass `vector validate` and are silently ignored. A typo such as `retry_atempts` leaves the default (effectively unlimited retries) in place with no error or warning.

Cause: `RequestConfig` in `src/sinks/util/http.rs` embeds `TowerRequestConfig` with `#[serde(flatten)]`, and serde does not support `deny_unknown_fields` together with `flatten`.

body_text:
## A note to the community

Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 reaction to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request.

## Problem

The `gcp_chronicle_unstructured` sink drops the whole batch on any request failure (HTTP 5xx from the Chronicle ingestion API, TLS/connection resets), without retrying. This happens with the default `request.*` settings, so `retry_attempts` / `retry_max_duration_secs` are never reached. Disk buffer (`type: disk`, `when_full: block`) does not help, because the failed batch has already left the buffer.

Observed on Vector 0.58.0 (Debian image, Kubernetes StatefulSet, 2 replicas) in a single day:

```
2026-10-13T07:54:56Z WARN  http_client: HTTP error. error=error trying to connect: unexpected EOF error_type="request_failed" stage="processing"
2026-10-13T07:54:56Z ERROR vector::sinks::util::retries: Unexpected error type; dropping the request. error=Failed to make HTTP(S) request: ... error trying to connect: unexpected EOF
2026-10-13T07:54:56Z ERROR vector_common::internal_event::service: Service call failed. No retries or retries exhausted. error=Some(HttpError { error: CallRequest { source: hyper::Error(Connect, ...ErrorCode(5)...) } })
2026-10-13T07:54:56Z ERROR component_events_dropped: Events dropped intentional=false count=627 reason="Service call failed. No retries or retries exhausted."

2026-10-13T09:16:12Z ERROR vector::sinks::util::retries: Unexpected error type; dropping the request. error=Server responded with an error: 503 Service Unavailable
2026-10-13T09:16:12Z ERROR service: Service call failed. No retries or retries exhausted. error=Some(ServerError { code: 503 })
2026-10-13T09:16:12Z ERROR component_events_dropped: Events dropped intentional=false count=622 reason="Service call failed. No retries or retries exhausted."
```

Both failures are transient on the Chronicle side and would normally succeed on retry. Note the message is `Unexpected error type`, i.e. the retry logic rejected the error type before applying any limit; it is not "retries exhausted".

## Likely cause (from reading the source, not confirmed by a patch)

In `src/sinks/gcp_chronicle/chronicle_unstructured.rs` (v0.58.0 and current `master`):

- The sink is built with `.settings(request, GcsRetryLogic::default())`.
- `GcsRetryLogic` (`src/sinks/gcs_common/config.rs`) declares `type Error = hyper::Error` and `is_retriable_error` is only consulted for that type. Its `should_retry_response` already maps 5xx, 408, 429 and 401 to `RetryAction::Retry`.
- But the sink's service returns its own error type `ChronicleResponseError` (`ServerError { code }`, `HttpError { error }`). In `call()`, any non-2xx response is turned into `Err(ChronicleResponseError::ServerError { .. })` instead of `Ok(GcsResponse)`, so `should_retry_response` never sees the status code. Connection errors are wrapped in `ChronicleResponseError::HttpError`, which is not a `hyper::Error` either.
- The generic retry layer then cannot downcast the error, logs "Unexpected error type; dropping the request", and gives up.

## Expected behavior

5xx / 408 / 429 responses and connection-level errors are retried according to `request.retry_*`, as they are in other GCP sinks, before events are dropped.

## Configuration

```yaml
sinks:
  chronicle_fortinet:
    type: gcp_chronicle_unstructured
    inputs: [fortinet_source]
    region: eu
    log_type: FORTINET_FIREWALL
    fallback_log_type: FORTINET_FIREWALL
    namespace: <redacted>
    customer_id: <redacted>
    compression: gzip
    encoding: { codec: text }
    buffer: { type: disk, max_size: 1000000000, when_full: block }
    healthcheck: { enabled: true }
    # no `request:` block -> defaults
```

## Version

Vector 0.58.0-debian. Same code path present on `master` at the time of writing.

## Impact

Silent loss (only visible via `component_events_dropped` with `intentional=false`) of ~600 events per failed request whenever the Chronicle API returns a transient error. Roughly 1,250 events lost in one day here, but any longer Chronicle degradation would drop everything sent during it.

## References

None found. I searched the issue tracker for this exact message with Chronicle and did not find a matching issue; please link if a duplicate exists.

#26770 (Tonic 0.12 upgrade) moved Vector's gRPC stack to Hyper 1. Hyper 1 sets the default HTTP/2 `max_header_list_size` to 16 KiB. The legacy `h2` stack that Hyper 0.14 used set it to 16 MiB.

To keep behavior unchanged during the transport upgrade, #26770 added one shared constant that keeps the old value:

```rust
// lib/vector-common/src/constants.rs
pub const GRPC_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE: u32 = 16 << 20;
```

These components use it:

| Side | Component | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Server | `vector` source, `opentelemetry` source (gRPC) | `src/sources/util/grpc/mod.rs` |
| Server | Observability API (`api.address`) | `src/api/grpc_server.rs` |
| Client | `vector` sink | `src/sinks/vector/config.rs` |
| Client | `gcp_pubsub` source | `src/sources/gcp_pubsub.rs` |
| Client | API client (`vector top`, `vector tap`) | `lib/vector-api-client/src/client.rs` |

Review discussion on #26770 ([thread](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/pull/26770#discussion_r4340166111)):

- Keeping the value preserves behavior, but it also keeps a value that the upstream default no longer uses.
- Keeping 16 MiB permanently only because it was the old default is not a good reason. Keeping it temporarily for the transport upgrade is acceptable.

This issue tracks that decision.

On the server side, the limit sets how many header bytes a peer can send for each request before the request is rejected. 16 MiB is approximately 1,000 times the Hyper 1 default.

### Attempted Solutions

NA. #26770 kept 16 MiB on purpose, so that the Tonic upgrade does not change behavior.

### Proposal

Select a permanent value, then remove or keep the shared constant:

1. **Use the Hyper 1 default (16 KiB).** Remove the `http2_max_header_list_size` calls. This can break peers that send large metadata. The #26770 checks sent 24 KiB of headers and trailers, which is more than 16 KiB.
2. **Use a smaller fixed value** (for example, 64 KiB or 1 MiB). This gives space for large gRPC metadata and decreases the per-request header budget on listeners.
3. **Make the value configurable** on the server components (`vector` source, `opentelemetry` source, API), with a smaller default. This adds configuration for a value that most users do not change.

The client and the server sides can use different values. A client limit applies only to responses from a peer that the user configured.

Changing the server default is a user-facing change and needs a changelog fragment.

### References

- #26770: Tonic 0.12 upgrade that added `GRPC_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE`
- #19179: Tonic upgrade tracking issue

body_text:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/pablodecm/next-optimistic-routing-prefetch-loop

### To Reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/pablodecm/next-optimistic-routing-prefetch-loop and run `npm install`.
2. Run `npm run build && npm run start`.
3. Open `http://localhost:3000/acme/dashboard` with the browser's Network panel open.
4. Do not click anything. Watch the RSC requests.

To count the requests without the Network panel, run `scripts/measure.sh http://localhost:3000/acme/dashboard out.har`.
It records the page for 10 seconds with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) and prints the
prefetch requests per URL and segment.

The reproduction has this route structure, with `cacheComponents: true`:

```
app/
  layout.tsx
  [workspace]/
    layout.tsx                      renders {children} and {modal}
    @modal/
      default.tsx                   returns null
      [...catchAll]/page.tsx        returns null (clears the slot on soft navigation)
    dashboard/page.tsx              six <Link>s to /[workspace]/items/<n>/view
    items/[itemId]/view/page.tsx
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** each visible link is prefetched once (a `/_tree` request and its segments).

**Current:** after the first links are prefetched, one link sends the same segment prefetch over and over, about
65 times a second, for as long as the page is open. Every response is HTTP 200:

```
GET /acme/items/5/view?_rsc=…
rsc: 1
next-router-prefetch: 1
next-router-segment-prefetch: /$d$workspace/@modal/(slot)/$c$catchAll/__PAGE__
→ 200 text/x-component
```

Prefetch requests in 10 seconds with the page idle:

| Variant | Requests |
|---|---|
| Reproduction as is (16.4.0) | 669, all for the `@modal/[...catchAll]/__PAGE__` segment of one link |
| Reproduction as is (16.5.0-canary.8) | 675, same segment |
| `experimental.optimisticRouting: false` | 10 |
| Without `cacheComponents` | 10 |
| Without `@modal/[...catchAll]` | 8 |
| One link only | 2 |

In a deployed app on Vercel, the responses were served from cache (`x-nextjs-cache: HIT`, `x-nextjs-prerender: 1`).
The repeated requests from real browsers matched the platform's bot detection, and real users were challenged.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #1 SMP Thu Oct  1 14:49:36 UTC 2026
  Available memory (MB): 16644
  Available CPU cores: 8
Binaries:
  Node: 24.19.0
  npm: 11.17.0
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 12.8.1
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.0).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

Also reproduces on `next@16.5.0-canary.8`.

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Linking and Navigating, Parallel & Intercepting Routes, cacheComponents

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

#### Relation to #97135

This is the same symptom as #97135 (closed, now locked), which #97128 fixed for a parallel-slot catch-all next to a
*dynamic* sibling (`@modal/[...catchAll]` next to `[username]`). That fix marks the level as conflicting when two
branches disagree about the dynamic child. In this reproduction the other branch has a *static* segment at that
level (`items`), so no conflict is recorded, matching prefers the static child, and the catch-all value is never
resolved. It still loops on 16.4.0 and 16.5.0-canary.8.

#### Cause (from reading `segment-cache/optimistic-routes`)

1. The first prefetch learns the route. Both slots are written into the known-route tree: `children` adds the
   static child `items`, and `@modal` adds the dynamic child `[...catchAll]` at the same level.
2. A later link is predicted by `matchKnownRoute`. Static children win, so the URL matches through
   `items/[itemId]/view`, and `resolvedParams` gets `workspace` and `itemId`. The catch-all value is only set on
   the catch-all branch, which is not taken.
3. `reifyRouteTree` reaches the `@modal` `[...catchAll]` segment with no resolved value. It keeps the original
   segment and inherits the parent vary path, at the existing
   `// TODO: This should never happen. Bail out with null.` The slot's `__PAGE__` vary path omits `catchAll`.
4. The server response is keyed with the real `catchAll` value, so it never fulfills the entry the prefetch task
   waits on. The task sees the entry as missing and fetches again, with no backoff.

The patch below stops the loop, which supports this reading. I did not step through it in a debugger.

#### Candidate fix

The patch is also in the reproduction repo as
[`optimistic-routes-bail-out.patch`](https://github.com/pablodecm/next-optimistic-routing-prefetch-loop/blob/main/optimistic-routes-bail-out.patch). It does what the `TODO`
describes: when a param is not resolved, `reifyRouteTree` returns `null` and
`matchKnownRoute` falls back to server resolution. Applied to the installed 16.4.0 package, the reproduction sends
10 prefetches, and clicking links still navigates client-side to the right page.

```diff
--- a/packages/next/src/client/components/segment-cache/optimistic-routes.ts
+++ b/packages/next/src/client/components/segment-cache/optimistic-routes.ts
@@ -795,6 +795,10 @@
     null, // Start with null partial vary path at the root
     acc
   )
+  if (reifiedTree === null) {
+    // A param could not be resolved from the URL. Fall back to the server.
+    return null
+  }
 
   // The metadata tree is a flat page node without the intermediate layout
   // structure. Clone it with the updated metadata vary path collected during
@@ -1034,7 +1038,7 @@
   search: NormalizedSearch,
   parentPartialVaryPath: PartialVaryPath | null,
   acc: ReifyAccumulator
-): RouteTree<null> {
+): RouteTree<null> | null {
   const originalSegment = pattern.segment
 
   // This segment's param (if any) is a root param iff the segment is at or
@@ -1063,9 +1067,14 @@
         isRootParam
       )
     } else {
-      // Param not found in resolvedParams - keep original and inherit partial
-      // TODO: This should never happen. Bail out with null.
-      partialVaryPath = parentPartialVaryPath
+      // The param was not resolved while matching the URL. This happens when a
+      // parallel route slot has a catch-all (e.g. `@modal/[...catchAll]`) and
+      // the URL matched through a static sibling in another slot, so the
+      // catch-all's value was never recorded. Keeping the original segment would
+      // produce a vary path that omits the param, and the server response would
+      // never fulfill the entry the prefetch task waits on. Bail out so the
+      // route is resolved by the server instead.
+      return null
     }
   } else {
     // Static segment: inherit partial vary path from parent
@@ -1078,16 +1087,17 @@
   if (patternSlots !== null) {
     newSlots = new Map()
     for (const [key, childPattern] of patternSlots) {
-      newSlots.set(
-        key,
-        reifyRouteTree(
-          childPattern,
-          resolvedParams,
-          search,
-          partialVaryPath,
-          acc
-        )
+      const reifiedChild = reifyRouteTree(
+        childPattern,
+        resolvedParams,
+        search,
+        partialVaryPath,
+        acc
       )
+      if (reifiedChild === null) {
+        return null
+      }
+      newSlots.set(key, reifiedChild)
     }
   }
 
```

Routes with this shape are then no longer predicted. A fuller fix could resolve catch-all values for parallel
slots while matching, so these routes can still be predicted.

#### Workarounds

- `experimental: { optimisticRouting: false }` in `next.config`.
- `prefetch={false}` on the affected links.

#### Related

- #97135 / #97128: see above.
- #98998 "Fix prefetch loop when a predicted route redirects" addressed another prefetch loop in the same module.
- #99988: same symptom with a raw `:` in a dynamic segment; a different trigger.

This one still reproduces on 16.5.0-canary.8, which includes those changes.

### To Reproduce

2. Run `npm run build && npm run start`.
3. Open `http://localhost:3000/acme/dashboard` with the browser's Network panel open.
4. Do not click anything. Watch the RSC requests.

To count the requests without the Network panel, run `scripts/measure.sh http://localhost:3000/acme/dashboard out.har`.
It records the page for 10 seconds with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) and prints the
prefetch requests per URL and segment.

The reproduction has this route structure, with `cacheComponents: true`:

```
app/
  layout.tsx
  [workspace]/
    layout.tsx                      renders {children} and {modal}
    @modal/
      default.tsx                   returns null
      [...catchAll]/page.tsx        returns null (clears the slot on soft navigation)
    dashboard/page.tsx              six <Link>s to /[workspace]/items/<n>/view
    items/[itemId]/view/page.tsx
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** each visible link is prefetched once (a `/_tree` request and its segments).

**Current:** after the first links are prefetched, one link sends the same segment prefetch over and over, about
65 times a second, for as long as the page is open. Every response is HTTP 200:

```
GET /acme/items/5/view?_rsc=…
rsc: 1
next-router-prefetch: 1
next-router-segment-prefetch: /$d$workspace/@modal/(slot)/$c$catchAll/__PAGE__
→ 200 text/x-component
```

Prefetch requests in 10 seconds with the page idle:

| Variant | Requests |

| Reproduction as is (16.4.0) | 669, all for the `@modal/[...catchAll]/__PAGE__` segment of one link |
| Reproduction as is (16.5.0-canary.8) | 675, same segment |

| Without `@modal/[...catchAll]` | 8 |

#### Relation to #97135

This is the same symptom as #97135 (closed, now locked), which #97128 fixed for a parallel-slot catch-all next to a
*dynamic* sibling (`@modal/[...catchAll]` next to `[username]`). That fix marks the level as conflicting when two
branches disagree about the dynamic child. In this reproduction the other branch has a *static* segment at that
level (`items`), so no conflict is recorded, matching prefers the static child, and the catch-all value is never
resolved. It still loops on 16.4.0 and 16.5.0-canary.8.

#### Cause (from reading `segment-cache/optimistic-routes`)

1. The first prefetch learns the route. Both slots are written into the known-route tree: `children` adds the
   static child `items`, and `@modal` adds the dynamic child `[...catchAll]` at the same level.
2. A later link is predicted by `matchKnownRoute`. Static children win, so the URL matches through
   `items/[itemId]/view`, and `resolvedParams` gets `workspace` and `itemId`. The catch-all value is only set on
   the catch-all branch, which is not taken.
3. `reifyRouteTree` reaches the `@modal` `[...catchAll]` segment with no resolved value. It keeps the original
   segment and inherits the parent vary path, at the existing
   `// TODO: This should never happen. Bail out with null.` The slot's `__PAGE__` vary path omits `catchAll`.
4. The server response is keyed with the real `catchAll` value, so it never fulfills the entry the prefetch task
   waits on. The task sees the entry as missing and fetches again, with no backoff.

The patch below stops the loop, which supports this reading. I did not step through it in a debugger.

#### Candidate fix

The patch is also in the reproduction repo as
[`optimistic-routes-bail-out.patch`](https://github.com/pablodecm/next-optimistic-routing-prefetch-loop/blob/main/optimistic-routes-bail-out.patch). It does what the `TODO`
describes: when a param is not resolved, `reifyRouteTree` returns `null` and
`matchKnownRoute` falls back to server resolution. Applied to the installed 16.4.0 package, the reproduction sends
10 prefetches, and clicking links still navigates client-side to the right page.

```diff
--- a/packages/next/src/client/components/segment-cache/optimistic-routes.ts
+++ b/packages/next/src/client/components/segment-cache/optimistic-routes.ts
@@ -795,6 +795,10 @@
     null, // Start with null partial vary path at the root
     acc
   )
+  if (reifiedTree === null) {
+    // A param could not be resolved from the URL. Fall back to the server.
+    return null
+  }
 
   // The metadata tree is a flat page node without the intermediate layout
   // structure. Clone it with the updated metadata vary path collected during
@@ -1034,7 +1038,7 @@
   search: NormalizedSearch,
   parentPartialVaryPath: PartialVaryPath | null,
   acc: ReifyAccumulator
-): RouteTree<null> {
+): RouteTree<null> | null {
   const originalSegment = pattern.segment
 
   // This segment's param (if any) is a root param iff the segment is at or
@@ -1063,9 +1067,14 @@
         isRootParam
       )
     } else {
-      // Param not found in resolvedParams - keep original and inherit partial
-      // TODO: This should never happen. Bail out with null.
-      partialVaryPath = parentPartialVaryPath
+      // The param was not resolved while matching the URL. This happens when a
+      // parallel route slot has a catch-all (e.g. `@modal/[...catchAll]`) and
+      // the URL matched through a static sibling in another slot, so the
+      // catch-all's value was never recorded. Keeping the original segment would
+      // produce a vary path that omits the param, and the server response would
+      // never fulfill the entry the prefetch task waits on. Bail out so the
+      // route is resolved by the server instead.
+      return null
     }
   } else {
     // Static segment: inherit partial vary path from parent
@@ -1078,16 +1087,17 @@
   if (patternSlots !== null) {
     newSlots = new Map()
     for (const [key, childPattern] of patternSlots) {
-      newSlots.set(
-        key,
-        reifyRouteTree(
-          childPattern,
-          resolvedParams,
-          search,
-          partialVaryPath,
-          acc
-        )
+      const reifiedChild = reifyRouteTree(
+        childPattern,
+        resolvedParams,
+        search,
+        partialVaryPath,
+        acc
       )
+      if (reifiedChild === null) {
+        return null
+      }
+      newSlots.set(key, reifiedChild)
     }
   }
 
```

Routes with this shape are then no longer predicted. A fuller fix could resolve catch-all values for parallel
slots while matching, so these routes can still be predicted.

#### Workarounds

- `experimental: { optimisticRouting: false }` in `next.config`.
- `prefetch={false}` on the affected links.

- #97135 / #97128: see above.
- #98998 "Fix prefetch loop when a predicted route redirects" addressed another prefetch loop in the same module.
- #99988: same symptom with a raw `:` in a dynamic segment; a different trigger.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/vjeux/next-rust-react-compiler-options-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install` (the repro pins `next@16.5.0-canary.9`, `react@19.3.0`, `babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0`).
2. `node scripts-show-compiled.mjs` — starts `next dev` with `reactCompiler: true` (the Babel loader path), fetches the client chunk of `app/counter.tsx` and prints the compiled `Counter`.
3. `RUST_COMPILER=1 node scripts-show-compiled.mjs` — the same with `experimental: { turbopackRustReactCompiler: true }` (the native Turbopack path).
4. Compare the two printouts (also in the repro's README).

### Current vs. Expected behavior

In development the two integrations hand the React Compiler different options, so the native path emits different code for the same component:

| option | Babel loader path | native path (`turbopackRustReactCompiler`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `environment.enableResetCacheOnSourceFileChanges` + the file's source text | on (the Babel plugin turns it on whenever `NODE_ENV=development`): the memo cache opens with `if ($[0] !== "<source hash>") { reset every slot }`, so after a Fast Refresh the component renders the edited code instead of values memoized by the old one | off: `source_code: None` and the environment left at its default, so no guard is emitted and the memo cache survives an edit of the file |
| `environment.enableNameAnonymousFunctions` | `isDev` (`packages/next/src/build/get-babel-loader-config.ts`, `crates/next-core/src/next_shared/webpack_rules/babel.rs`): memoized callbacks are named `"Counter[onClick]"`, `"Counter[(anonymous)()]"` for React DevTools and stack traces | never: anonymous arrows |
| `flowSuppressions` | the plugin default, `true` | `false` |
| compiler source type for `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts` | n/a (Babel parses TS) | `SourceType::from_program(program)` without `.with_typescript(..)`; `swc`'s own `jsc.transform.reactCompiler` integration sets it |

Current (native path, development), from the repro:

```js
const $ = _c(10);
const { step } = t0;
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
let t1;
if ($[0] !== count || $[1] !== step) {
    t1 = ()=>setCount(count + step);
```

Expected (what the Babel path emits for the same file, development):

```js
const $ = _c(11);
if ($[0] !== "5fc996b489ca5de79226075b42ff4eaa6b1a643ebf1eba25896c9393fb66454e") {
    for(let $i = 0; $i < 11; $i += 1){ $[$i] = Symbol.for("react.memo_cache_sentinel"); }
    $[0] = "5fc996b489ca5de79226075b42ff4eaa6b1a643ebf1eba25896c9393fb66454e";
}
const { step } = t0;
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
let t1;
if ($[1] !== count || $[2] !== step) {
    t1 = ({ "Counter[onClick]": ()=>setCount(count + step) })["Counter[onClick]"];
```

Production builds are not affected by the first two rows (both are development-only in the Babel plugin). The compiler itself is not the difference: comparing the TypeScript plugin and the Rust port at the same react/react commit over a 9,000-file app gives identical output for every compiled function once the options match.

The cause is `react_compiler_options` in `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript/src/transform/mod.rs`: `environment: Default::default()`, `source_code: None`, `flow_suppressions: false`, and `apply_rust_react_compiler` passing `SourceType::from_program(program)`.

A fix with unit tests is on a fork, ready to be turned into a PR: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/compare/canary...vjeux:next.js:react-compiler-native-parity?expand=1 (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p turbopack-ecmascript --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p turbopack-ecmascript --lib react_compiler_tests` pass on `nightly-2026-10-06`).

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #1 SMP Fri Jul 17 15:49:12 PDT 2026
  Available memory (MB): 229265
  Available CPU cores: 166
Binaries:
  Node: 24.18.0
  npm: 11.16.0
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 11.10.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.5.0-canary.9 // Latest available version is detected (16.5.0-canary.9).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, React

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

Also reproduced on `next@16.3.5` and `16.4.0`; the native transform's options have not changed since `turbopackRustReactCompiler` landed. Related, already fixed: #96820 (SSR scope and `fast_check`), swc-project/swc#12007 (the prefilter that skipped nested components).

This issue and the fork branch were written by Christopher Chedeau's (@vjeux) coding agent at his direction, from a measured comparison of the two integrations.

| `flowSuppressions` | the plugin default, `true` | `false` |
| compiler source type for `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts` | n/a (Babel parses TS) | `SourceType::from_program(program)` without `.with_typescript(..)`; `swc`'s own `jsc.transform.reactCompiler` integration sets it |

body_text:
**Summary.** On a large App Router application, leaving Next 16's filesystem cache for builds on (`experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`, the default) makes a cold `next build` — one that starts with an empty cache directory, which is every CI build that does not restore the cache and every first build — take 2.6× longer than the same build with the cache turned off (776.5 s vs 301.3 s on Next 16.3.5; 781.3 s vs 367.1 s on 16.5.0-canary.8), use 2.6× the memory (68.2 GB vs 26.0 GB) and 5.4× the CPU, and write a cache of 15–21 GB for about 3 GB of build output. The extra time is not the cache write, which takes 28–32 s. It is bookkeeping that Turbopack's task engine only does when the cache is on: when the tasks that flatten each chunk group's assets finish (one such task per chunk group, 262,000 chunk groups in this app, ~26,000 children each), propagating their "active" counts and follower/upper relations through the aggregation graph runs on a single thread for about six minutes while the other 165 cores idle. A one-commit change on my fork, https://github.com/vjeux/next.js/compare/canary...vjeux/turbo-tasks-skip-activeness-in-fresh-build, turns off activeness tracking for a build whose cache database starts empty (nothing is restored from an empty database, so no part of the graph can become active again, which is the only thing activeness tracking is for); it brings the cold cache-on build from 781 s to 515 s on that app, leaves warm builds and the persisted graph unchanged, and passes the backend and filesystem-cache test suites. I cannot share the application; the linked public repository reproduces the chunk-group fan-out and the cache size on a 1,106-file app (9–10 minute build, 7.4 GB cache), not the 2.6× wall-time ratio, and I can run any branch against the application and report traces and profiles.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/vjeux/turbopack-chunk-group-fanout-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `pnpm install` (installs `next@canary`; 16.5.0-canary.8 when these numbers were taken).
2. `rm -rf .next && /usr/bin/time -v pnpm next build` — filesystem cache on (the default).
3. `rm -rf .next && FS_CACHE=0 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm next build` — the same build with `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild: false` (the `next.config.ts` reads the variable).
4. Compare wall time, `Maximum resident set size`, `User time`, and the size of `.next/cache/turbopack`.

The repository is a generated App Router app: 300 routes (`app/r<i>/page.tsx`, server components) each render a sliding window of 100 of 200 shared `"use client"` components; each shared component lazily imports (`import()`) 3 of 600 leaf client components; each leaf lazily imports 2 other leaves. 1,106 files, 11 MB of source, no dependency besides `next`, `react` and `react-dom`. The generator and its parameters are in `tools/tpgen.rs`.

Why that shape: with nested async chunking (`turbopackClientSideNestedAsyncChunking`, on by default in `next build`), Turbopack creates one async chunk group per dynamic import *per parent chunk group*, so the number of chunk groups is routes × reachable dynamic imports. Two levels of lazy-inside-lazy is enough to turn a 1,106-file app into a 9-minute build. Without the second level (500 routes × 300 shared × 1,000 leaves, 1,806 files) the same generator builds in 234 s with a 2.7 GB cache.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** a cold build with the cache on costs about the cache write (28–45 s here) on top of the cache-off build; the cache directory is in the order of the build output; a rebuild after a one-line change costs that file's recompile plus a small write.

**Actual, public reproduction** (166 cores, 223 GB, Linux x64, next 16.5.0-canary.8):

| build | wall | `Compiled successfully in` | cache write | peak RSS | user CPU | `.next/cache` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cache on (default) | 635.1 s | 9.1 min | 43 s | 46.0 GB | 5,916 s | 7.4 GB, 773 files |
| cache off (`FS_CACHE=0`) | 609.8 s | 8.7 min | — | 32.0 GB | 4,370 s | — |

Here the cache costs +35 % CPU and +44 % memory and writes 7.4 GB for a 1,106-file app. The wall-time ratio stays near 1 because this app lacks the fan-in described below.

**Actual, large private application.** App Router; 280 `page.tsx` + 333 `route.ts` (613 endpoints); 12,391 first-party `.ts/.tsx` files; 1,079 `import()` sites in first-party code; `productionBrowserSourceMaps: true`; `output: "standalone"`. One cold build reads ~54,000 files, creates ~131,000 module instances across the server, client and edge environments, 279,804 chunk items and 262,463 async chunk groups (231,083 of them for the browser), executes 12.96 million tasks and persists 12,820,814 of them.

Next 16.3.5 (published binary), 192 cores, 235 GB, `next build` only (type check off), fresh `distDir` for each cold build:

| run | wall | `Compiled` | cache write / compaction | peak RSS | user CPU | cache dir after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cache off, cold | 301.3 s | 4.1 min | — | 26.0 GB | 4,583 s | — |
| cache on, cold | 776.5 s | 12.0 min | write 32.2 s (21.06 GB) | 68.2 GB | 24,831 s | 21.06 GB, 510 SST files |
| cache on, rebuild, nothing changed | 48.0 s | 9.3 s | write 0.7 s (157 MB); compaction 30.2 s (20.97 GB deleted, 20.92 GB rewritten) | 11.6 GB | 352 s | 21.16 GB |
| cache on, one line changed in one leaf client component | 169.0 s | 2.1 min | write 3.8 s (1.26 GB); compaction 24.1 s (13.97 GB deleted, 13.69 GB rewritten) | 51.4 GB | 4,700 s | 22.08 GB |
| cache on, a second one-line change in the same file | 155.6 s | 1.9 min | write 3.5 s (1.17 GB); compaction 18.0 s (11.64 / 10.80 GB) | 50.5 GB | 3,047 s | 22.36 GB |
| cache on, 20 components changed (one exported const appended to each) | 279.3 s | — | — | 71.2 GB | — | 31.87 GB (+9.8 GB) |

Next 16.5.0-canary.8 built from source, 166 cores, 223 GB: cache off cold 367.1 s, 25.2 GB; cache on cold 781.3 s (a second run 986.0 s), 66.8 GB, write 27.6 s for 15.41 GB (zstd); rebuild with nothing changed 65.0 s; one leaf file changed 208.8 s.

So on this app the cache turns a 5-minute cold build into a 13-minute one, and a one-line change costs a 2.6–2.8-minute rebuild of which 18–24 s is compaction rewriting half to all of the store.

**Where the time goes.** With `NEXT_TURBOPACK_TRACING=1` on the from-source canary build, the cache-on cold compile (934 s with tracing on) has these phases: `whole app module graph` 0.2–99.6 s; endpoints and chunking done at 124 s; **no span at all from 124 s to 487 s, with one tokio thread at 100 % and the other 165 idle**; `emitting` 487–897 s. The cache-off compile (331 s) has the module graph to 91 s, endpoints to 104 s, a 64 s span-less single-threaded gap, and `emitting` 168–303 s. The cache write itself is 28–32 s in both versions. The cost is in-memory tracking that is only enabled with the cache (`dependencyTracking: persistentCaching || hasDeferredEntries`), not I/O.

`perf` on the busy thread during the gap (release build with symbols): 36.0 % `DashMap<TaskId, Box<TaskStorage>>::_entry`, 20.5 % `AggregationUpdateQueue::decrease_active_count`, 12.8 % `AggregationUpdateQueue::process`, 9.2 % `AggregationUpdateQueue::increase_active_count`, 8.9 % `connect_child::resurrect_deleted`, 7.3 % `ExecuteContext::open_task`; later in the same gap 27.9 % `AggregationUpdateQueue::inner_of_upper_lost_followers`, 23.7 % the DashMap entry, 14.5 % `decrease_active_count`, 13.0 % `inner_of_upper_has_new_followers`. Callers: `TurboTasksBackend::task_execution_completed → connect_children::process_new_children`, i.e. a task finishing with ~26,000 new children, each child already having thousands of uppers, all processed by one `AggregationUpdateQueue` on the completing thread.

**What fills the cache.** Per task type, from `turbo-tasks-backend`'s `print_cache_item_size` feature (uncompressed; 28.43 GiB in total, 15.4 GB after zstd on canary, 21 GB after LZ4 on 16.3.5):

| task | bytes | tasks × average | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<BrowserChunkingContext as ChunkingContext>::chunk_group` | 5.17 GiB | 231,083 × 23.3 KiB | one per browser async chunk group |
| `OutputAssetsWithReferenced::all_assets` | 4.07 GiB | 35,538 × 101 KiB | 64.5 M children |
| `ChunkGroupResult::referenced_assets` | 3.28 GiB | 2,025 × 1.38 MiB | 52.8 M children |
| `ChunkGroupResult::all_assets` | 3.26 GiB | 1,411 × 1.99 MiB | |
| `ChunkGroupResult::output_assets_with_referenced` | 2.57 GiB | 262,382 × 10.2 KiB | |
| `FileContent::persist` | 1.94 GiB | 41,020 × 49.6 KiB | the emitted files |
| `AsyncLoaderModule::chunk_group` | 945 MiB | 262,463 | |
| `chunk_group_assets` | 896 MiB | | |
| `all_assets_from_entries` | 753 MiB | 283 × 2.2 MiB | |
| `module_factory_with_code_generation_issue` | 744 MiB | 279,804 × 2.7 KiB | |
| `EcmascriptModuleContent::new_merged` / `::new` | 375 / 286 MiB | | |
| `evaluate_webpack_loader` | 258 MiB | | |

About 65 % of the store is chunk-group results and their asset flattenings. Their MiB-sized values are mostly `cell_dependencies`: each flattening awaits a few cells for each of the ~26,000 `OutputAssetsReference`s it can reach, and their metadata is the children and follower sets. One task type alone, `<EcmascriptModuleChunkItem as OutputAssetsReference>::references` (279,478 tasks), has 13.4 million uppers and 182 million cache hits in one build. On 16.3.5 the store splits into TaskData 16.56 GB stored (25.28 GB raw, LZ4), TaskMeta 2.83 GB (12.8 M entries × ~221 B), TaskCache 147 MB and ~1.5 GB of `.meta`.

**My reading of the cause.**
1. `expand_output_assets` runs once per chunk group and walks the whole transitive async-reference graph each time, so dependency and child edges scale as chunk groups × reachable references, and with nested async chunking there is one async chunk group per (dynamic import × parent chunk group).
2. Connecting those children propagates active counts and reclassifies followers/uppers through the aggregation graph, on the one thread that completed the task.
3. The compaction after each build rewrites 50–100 % of the store (the new TaskData SSTs overlap the whole key range): 18–30 s per build and no space reclaimed for the 20-file change.

**The change on my fork.** https://github.com/vjeux/next.js/compare/canary...vjeux/turbo-tasks-skip-activeness-in-fresh-build — one commit, 21 lines. `TurboBackingStorage::is_fresh()` exposes whether the cache database held no data when it was opened (the key-value layer already tracks this for its shutdown compaction), and `create_turbo_tasks` builds the backend with `active_tracking: false` when a build (`is_short_session`) starts from such a database. A build persists only at shutdown, so with an empty database nothing is restored: every task is created, connected and scheduled during the session, and no subgraph can become active again with dirty tasks in it, which is the case activeness tracking exists for. #75899 already disables it when dependency tracking is off; this applies the same reasoning to the cache-on build whose cache is empty. Activeness is transient state, so the persisted graph is byte-identical and the next build (database no longer fresh) restores it with tracking on, exactly as today.

Measured on the application, canary vs. the branch, same box and binary build flags:

| build | canary | fork branch |
|---|---|---|
| cache on, cold | 781.3 s (986.0 s) · 66.8 GB · write 27.6 s / 15.41 GB | **514.9 s (530.0 s, 558.6 s)** · 66.5 GB · write 26.0 s / 15.44 GB |
| cache on, rebuild, nothing changed | 65.0 s · 13.4 GB | 64.8 s · 13.6 GB |
| cache on, one leaf file changed | 208.8 s · 51.5 GB | 214.9 s · 49.0 GB |
| cache off, cold | 367.1 s · 25.2 GB | — (unchanged code path) |

With tracing: compile 15.7 min → 7.9 min, the single-threaded gap 363 s → 27 s, `emitting` 410 s → 239 s, persisted bytes identical. `cargo test -p turbo-tasks-backend` (126 unit tests and all integration binaries) and `pnpm test-start-turbo test/e2e/filesystem-cache/*` (3 suites, 23 tests, including `warm-restart-task-stats`, which asserts zero task-cache misses on the warm build after the cold one) pass with the branch's binary. What remains after the change is the follower/upper reclassification (the 27 s gap) and a slower `emitting` (239 s vs 134 s cache-off). #91637 (batched N×M aggregation updates), rebased onto canary, changes nothing here: 972.9 s alone, 539.5 s on top of the branch.

If the direction is right I am happy for this to be taken over or told how it should be done; the branch is there to be used.

https://github.com/vjeux/turbopack-chunk-group-fanout-repro

2. `rm -rf .next && /usr/bin/time -v pnpm next build` — filesystem cache on (the default).
3. `rm -rf .next && FS_CACHE=0 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm next build` — the same build with `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild: false` (the `next.config.ts` reads the variable).

The repository is a generated App Router app: 300 routes (`app/r<i>/page.tsx`, server components) each render a sliding window of 100 of 200 shared `"use client"` components; each shared component lazily imports (`import()`) 3 of 600 leaf client components; each leaf lazily imports 2 other leaves. 1,106 files, 11 MB of source, no dependency besides `next`, `react` and `react-dom`. 1. `expand_output_assets` runs once per chunk group and walks the whole transitive async-reference graph each time, so dependency and child edges scale as chunk groups × reachable references, and with nested async chunking there is one async chunk group per (dynamic import × parent chunk group).

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/pauksztello/locale-slot-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`, `npm run build`, `npm run start`
2. Open http://localhost:3000/en and do a hard refresh
3. Click "People (catch-all slot)" in the nav (client navigation to /en/about/people)
4. Click the "Slot: EN ▾" button, then "Switch to FR" (a `<Link replace>` to /fr/about/people)

Every server component reads the locale with `rootParams.locale()` from `next/root-params`. `app/[locale]` is the root layout, with `generateStaticParams` for en and fr. The `@localeSwitch` slot is matched by `@localeSwitch/[...catchAll]/page.tsx` for this URL.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current (`next build` + `next start`): after switching, the layout and the page show FR, but the `@localeSwitch` slot still shows "EN" in both places it's rendered (header and footer). Reloading the page fixes it.

Current (`next dev`): the slot switches to FR correctly, but the browser console logs:

    Error: This library called use() to suspend in a previous render but did not call use() when it finished. This indicates an incorrect use of use(). Learn more: https://react.dev/warnings/conditional-use-of-use

Expected: the slot is re-rendered for the new locale, like the layout and the page.

body_text: ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/gauravsinghlive/cache-components ### To Reproduce Steps to reproduce 1. Deploy a Next.js application through OpenNext to Cloudflare Workers. 2. Enable Cache Components in `next.config.mjs`: ```const nextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, }; export default nextConfig; ``` 3. Build and deploy the generated Worker to Cloudflare and request an affected route. 4. Observe the HTTP 500 response and Cloudflare Error 1101. 5. Set `cacheComponents: false`, rebuild, and redeploy using the same dependencies. 6. Request the same route again and compare the results. The failure is reproducible with Cache Components enabled, while disabling it restores normal operation. ### Current vs. Expected behavior Expected behavior : The application should respond successfully with Cache Components enabled. Actual behavior : Requests return HTTP 500 with Cloudflare Error 1101 when cacheComponents: true. Setting it to false restores normal operation. ### Provide environment information ```bash Environment : Next.js: 16.3.8 (also tested 16.4.0) React / React DOM: 19.3.0 @opennextjs/cloudflare: 1.20.10 Wrangler: 4.149.0 Runtime: Cloudflare Workers (workerd) Node.js: 24.19.0 pnpm: 12.10.1 OS: Windows 11 x64 ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Runtime ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Other (Deployed) ### Additional context I'm experiencing a runtime failure when deploying Next.js through OpenNext to Cloudflare Workers with Cache Components enabled. With cacheComponents: false, the deployment works. Setting cacheComponents: true causes requests to fail with HTTP 500 and Cloudflare Error 1101. Downgrading Next.js from 16.4.0 to 16.3.8 did not resolve the issue. Related issue : [#94880 — Concurrent requests hang the worker with Cache Components](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/94880) [OpenNext PR #1318](https://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-cloudflare/pull/1318) Could you clarify whether this behavior indicates a remaining Next.js issue or an incompatibility with the OpenNext/Cloudflare Workers runtime integration?

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/HardMax71/next-turbopack-stderr-panic

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repo and run `npm install`
2. Run `npm run dev`
3. Open http://localhost:3000
4. Stop the server and run `npm run dev` again

### Current vs. Expected behavior

The repo has a small PostCSS plugin that prints a stack trace to stderr when it loads (`console.error(new Error("logged by a PostCSS plugin").stack)`). When the CSS is compiled, the dev server prints:

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' (51144598) panicked at turbopack/crates/turbo-tasks/src/manager.rs:2215:17:
cannot access a task-local storage value without setting it first
```

The plugin's output never shows up. The page still loads. On the next start:

```
⚠ Turbopack's filesystem cache has been deleted because we previously detected an internal error in Turbopack. Builds or page loads may be slower as a result.
```

I expected the stack trace to be printed (source-mapped or as is), with no panic and the cache kept.

A plain line without a stack frame prints fine. The same stack printed inside the plugin's `Once()` hook (during the transform, not at load) also prints fine.

How I ran into it: on Node 26, `@tailwindcss/node` 4.2 prints a deprecation warning when it loads, and with `NODE_OPTIONS=--trace-deprecation` that warning has a stack. Then `next dev` panics every time.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0
  Available memory (MB): 24576
  Available CPU cores: 15
Binaries:
  Node: 26.0.0
  npm: 11.12.1
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.5.0-canary.9 // Latest available version is detected (16.5.0-canary.9).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

CSS, Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

Also happens on 16.4.0 (`manager.rs:2172:17`) and on Node 22.23.2. `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` shows no frames.

I think the PostCSS worker is pre-warmed from a plain `tokio::spawn` ([process_pool/mod.rs#L773-L779](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/f10699476a2655fbf562849c64cc132ac2036b8c/turbopack/crates/turbopack-node/src/process_pool/mod.rs#L773-L779)), so it has no turbo-tasks context. Its startup stderr is read there ([#L448](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/f10699476a2655fbf562849c64cc132ac2036b8c/turbopack/crates/turbopack-node/src/process_pool/mod.rs#L448)) and goes to `apply_source_mapping` ([#L156-L175](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/f10699476a2655fbf562849c64cc132ac2036b8c/turbopack/crates/turbopack-node/src/process_pool/mod.rs#L156-L175)), that reads turbo-tasks values once the text has an `    at file:line:col` line ([source_map/mod.rs#L37-L43](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/f10699476a2655fbf562849c64cc132ac2036b8c/turbopack/crates/turbopack-node/src/source_map/mod.rs#L37-L43)). 

That would explain why only output at load panics. Not confirmed with a backtrace.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/JalilArfaoui/repro-next-js-hoisting/

### To Reproduce

```bash
npm install
NODE_ENV=production npm run build     # Turbopack production build (Next 16 default)
NODE_ENV=production npm run start
```

Open `http://localhost:3000/`. The page crashes during hydration, on every load. The browser console shows the instrumentation warning from `source/design-system/root.tsx` proving the duplicate evaluation:

```
[repro] theme module evaluated 2 times: module-level singletons are duplicated
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'main')
    at o$.theme (chunks/….js)
    at e.generateAndInjectStyles (chunks/….js)   <- styled-components reads a theme
                                                    instance the ThemeProvider never saw
```

A `./check.sh` script in the repo automates the full verdict (build with hoisting → crash; build without → renders) using headless Chromium.

**Control:** add `experimental: { turbopackScopeHoisting: false }` to `next.config.mjs` and rebuild — the page renders and the theme module is evaluated exactly once. Building with webpack also renders.

### Current vs. Expected behavior


**Expected.** A module evaluates once. Module-level singletons (a styled-components theme object, a `createContext` result) exist once, shared by every importer.

**Current.** One scope-hoisted (merged) module factory is executed **twice** in the browser, so every module-scope singleton it contains exists twice. In this repro the styled-components theme object is duplicated: the `ThemeProvider` provides one instance while styled components resolve fonts from the other → `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'main')` during hydration.


### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #1-NixOS SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC
  Available memory (MB): 64208
  Available CPU cores: 16
Binaries:
  Node: 24.11.1
  npm: 11.6.2
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0 (also reproduced on 16.2.6, 16.3.4 and 16.5.0-canary.9)
  react: 19.2.0
  react-dom: 19.2.0
  styled-components: 6.0.7
  typescript: 5.9.3
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), next build (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

- Only reproduces in **production builds**; `next dev` is fine (scope hoisting is disabled in dev).
- Reproduces on 16.2.6, 16.3.4, **16.4.0** (latest stable) and **16.5.0-canary.9** — i.e. also after #96697 ("Raise registration calls in hoisted modules to the top", which closed #96648) and its 16.3 backport #97308.
- Same bug family as #96648 and as the duplicated-WebSocket-singleton case analyzed in https://yceffort.kr/en/2026/08/turbopack-scope-hoisting-singleton-split — in both of those, 16.3.1+ fixes it; this variant still reproduces on 16.4.0.
- Distinct from #99109 (partial-namespace snapshot inside one evaluation of a merged factory) and from #98099 (same module id emitted with different factory bodies, first-wins registration): here a single factory body is **evaluated twice**, through two different top-level require chains.
- Workaround we ship in production: `experimental: { turbopackScopeHoisting: false }`.

```
    at e.generateAndInjectStyles (chunks/….js)   <- styled-components reads a theme
                                                    instance the ThemeProvider never saw
```

A `./check.sh` script in the repo automates the full verdict (build with hoisting → crash; build without → renders) using headless Chromium.

**Control:** add `experimental: { turbopackScopeHoisting: false }` to `next.config.mjs` and rebuild — the page renders and the theme module is evaluated exactly once. Building with webpack also renders.

### Current vs. Expected behavior


**Expected.** A module evaluates once. Module-level singletons (a styled-components theme object, a `createContext` result) exist once, shared by every importer.

**Current.** One scope-hoisted (merged) module factory is executed **twice** in the browser, so every module-scope singleton it contains exists twice. In this repro the styled-components theme object is duplicated: the `ThemeProvider` provides one instance while styled components resolve fonts from the other → `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'main')` during hydration.

```bash
Binaries:

  npm: 11.6.2
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0 (also reproduced on 16.2.6, 16.3.4 and 16.5.0-canary.9)
  react: 19.2.0
  react-dom: 19.2.0
  styled-components: 6.0.7
  typescript: 5.9.3
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), next build (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

- Only reproduces in **production builds**; `next dev` is fine (scope hoisting is disabled in dev).
- Reproduces on 16.2.6, 16.3.4, **16.4.0** (latest stable) and **16.5.0-canary.9** — i.e. also after #96697 ("Raise registration calls in hoisted modules to the top", which closed #96648) and its 16.3 backport #97308.
- Same bug family as #96648 and as the duplicated-WebSocket-singleton case analyzed in https://yceffort.kr/en/2026/08/turbopack-scope-hoisting-singleton-split — in both of those, 16.3.1+ fixes it; this variant still reproduces on 16.4.0.
- Distinct from #99109 (partial-namespace snapshot inside one evaluation of a merged factory) and from #98099 (same module id emitted with different factory bodies, first-wins registration): here a single factory body is **evaluated twice**, through two different top-level require chains.
- Workaround we ship in production: `experimental: { turbopackScopeHoisting: false }`.
