### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/shward/next-repro-100150

### To Reproduce

1. App Router app with any middleware matching `/api/x` that returns `NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } })`.
2. `app/api/x/route.ts`: read `request.body` with `getReader()`, concatenate, log the total, then call `formData()`.
3. Post a ~150 KB multipart body slowly, several times:
   `curl --limit-rate 150k --data-binary @body.bin -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...' http://host/api/x`
4. The logged length is sometimes the full body and sometimes the last chunk only.
5. Exclude the path from the middleware matcher: 8 of 8 pass.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: with middleware in front, a body that arrives in several socket reads can reach the route as the last chunk only. A 150,671 byte multipart POST reached `request.body.getReader()` as one 19,599 byte chunk, the last 19,599 bytes. `new Response(bytes, { headers }).formData()` then throws "Failed to parse body as FormData". 4 of 6 slow posts failed on the same server.

Expected: the route gets the whole body however many reads it took.

### Provide environment information

```
Next.js 15.5.27
output: "standalone"
Node.js 22.23.3
Middleware on the Node runtime (15.5 default), matcher covering the route
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Middleware, Route Handlers, Server Actions

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), Other (standalone server in a container)

### Additional context

Where it looks like it lives:
- `server/next-server.js` ~line 1259 calls `requestData.body.finalize()` in a `finally` without `await`. `finalize()` in `server/body-streams.js` is what waits for `end` before `replaceRequestBody(readable, buffered)`.
- `server/app-render/action-handler.js` ~line 637 pipes `req.body` straight into busboy for multipart server actions, so those read the same stream.
- `cloneBodyStream()` ran twice for one request in my logs; the second call attaches a new `data` listener to the already swapped request.

Line numbers are from 15.5.27; my local copy is 15.5.24 with the same calls at 1257 and 648.

Workaround: exclude the route from the matcher and resolve inside the route whatever middleware used to provide. `experimental.middlewareClientMaxBodySize` is not involved; these bodies are well under 10 MB.

### Versions checked

15.5.27 and 16.0.0 reproduce. 16.1.7, 16.2.0, 16.3.0, 16.4.0 and canary do not: they await `requestData.body.finalize()`. LTS backport with an e2e test: #100153.

### Inline copy of the repro

No standalone repro yet; description below. A stripped-down app did not reproduce it for me. The real app in a container did, where the handler awaits database work before reading and the body arrives as 65,079 / 457 / 65,536 / 19,599 byte reads. The extra condition is not isolated.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/dgomez-orangeloops/next-dev-restart-reload-loop

### To Reproduce

Automated (Chromium through Playwright):

```bash
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
npm run repro
```

`scripts/repro.mjs` starts `next dev` from a clean `.next` and opens `/`. Each attempt navigates client-side to `/other` and `/third`, loads `/` again, restarts `next dev` with the tab still open, and requests the route handler `/api/ping` before the tab reconnects. It then counts the tab's document loads and HMR `restart` messages for 15 s. The loop does not start on every restart (in my runs it started on the 3rd or 4th), so the script tries up to 8 times and exits with code 1 when it reproduces.

By hand:

1. `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:3000.
2. Click **Other**, then **Third** (client-side navigations), then load http://localhost:3000 again.
3. Stop `next dev` (Ctrl+C) and leave the tab open.
4. `npm run dev:ping`: it starts `next dev` and requests `/api/ping` as soon as the server answers, before the tab reconnects.
5. If the tab reloads only once, repeat from step 2 without deleting `.next`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** after the restart the tab reloads non-stop (337 to 466 document loads in 15 s in my runs) until every tab on that origin is closed. While one tab loops, a new tab on the same origin loops too. On every reload, right after the page sends `turbopack-subscribe`, the HMR socket receives a `restart` for the main client chunk list, and the browser reloads on it:

```json
{"type":"turbopack-message","data":[{"resource":{"path":"static/chunks/_1anvha4rlo79g._.js","headers":null},"type":"restart","issues":[],"diagnostics":[]}],"hmrVersion":"N"}
```

The terminal repeats `✓ Compiled in 1–40ms` and `GET / 200` for as long as the tab is open.

**Expected:** one reload after the restart (the server session changed), then the page stays, as with 16.3.6.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.2.0
  Available memory (MB): 49152
  Available CPU cores: 15
Binaries:
  Node: 24.19.0
  npm: 11.17.0
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.5.0-canary.13 // Latest available version is detected (16.5.0-canary.13).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.0
  react-dom: 19.2.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

- **Regression in 16.4.0.** 16.3.6 does not loop (8 attempts). 16.4.1 and 16.5.0-canary.13 do.
- **Likely introduced by #98385** ("Fix initial Turbopack HMR update handling"). In `subscribeToClientHmrEvents` (`packages/next/src/server/dev/hot-reloader-turbopack.ts`), the first emission of `project.clientHmrEvents(id)` used to be dropped as the initial computation. Since #98385 it is forwarded unless it only carries issues. In the failing state that first emission is `restart` for every new subscription, so the forwarded `restart` reloads the page and the reload gets another one.
- **What the loop needs** (controls in the repro, 8 attempts each):
  - Client-side navigations in the session before the restart: `NAV=0 npm run repro` does not loop.
  - A route handler compiled by the restarted server before the tab reconnects: `PING=0 npm run repro` does not loop.
  - `proxy.ts` is not required, but the loop starts more often with it. The React Compiler made no difference.
- **Persistent dev cache:** with `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: false` it does not loop (8 attempts). In a larger app, the chunk files under `.next/dev/static/chunks` were byte-identical before and after the restart. So it does not look like a real content change; more like the version restored from the persistent cache not comparing with the new one.
- **#99963** (included in canary.13) touches the same code and does not fix it.
- **Local workaround:** also ignoring a `restart` as the first emission (`initial.value.type !== 'restart'`) stops the loop, and later HMR updates still apply. It is probably not the right fix upstream.
- **How we hit it:** our dev script polls a route handler while `next dev` starts, to know when the server is ready. So restarting the dev server with a tab open could leave that tab reloading forever.

### To Reproduce

Automated (Chromium through Playwright):

```bash
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
npm run repro
```

`scripts/repro.mjs` starts `next dev` from a clean `.next` and opens `/`. Each attempt navigates client-side to `/other` and `/third`, loads `/` again, restarts `next dev` with the tab still open, and requests the route handler `/api/ping` before the tab reconnects. It then counts the tab's document loads and HMR `restart` messages for 15 s. The loop does not start on every restart (in my runs it started on the 3rd or 4th), so the script tries up to 8 times and exits with code 1 when it reproduces.

By hand:

1. `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:3000.
2. Click **Other**, then **Third** (client-side navigations), then load http://localhost:3000 again.
3. Stop `next dev` (Ctrl+C) and leave the tab open.
4. `npm run dev:ping`: it starts `next dev` and requests `/api/ping` as soon as the server answers, before the tab reconnects.
5. If the tab reloads only once, repeat from step 2 without deleting `.next`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** after the restart the tab reloads non-stop (337 to 466 document loads in 15 s in my runs) until every tab on that origin is closed. While one tab loops, a new tab on the same origin loops too. On every reload, right after the page sends `turbopack-subscribe`, the HMR socket receives a `restart` for the main client chunk list, and the browser reloads on it:

```json
{"type":"turbopack-message","data":[{"resource":{"path":"static/chunks/_1anvha4rlo79g._.js","headers":null},"type":"restart","issues":[],"diagnostics":[]}],"hmrVersion":"N"}
```

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

In `subscribeToClientHmrEvents` (`packages/next/src/server/dev/hot-reloader-turbopack.ts`), the first emission of `project.clientHmrEvents(id)` used to be dropped as the initial computation. In the failing state that first emission is `restart` for every new subscription, so the forwarded `restart` reloads the page and the reload gets another one.

  - Client-side navigations in the session before the restart: `NAV=0 npm run repro` does not loop.

- **Persistent dev cache:** with `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: false` it does not loop (8 attempts). In a larger app, the chunk files under `.next/dev/static/chunks` were byte-identical before and after the restart. So it does not look like a real content change; more like the version restored from the persistent cache not comparing with the new one.
- **#99963** (included in canary.13) touches the same code and does not fix it.

- **How we hit it:** our dev script polls a route handler while `next dev` starts, to know when the server is ready. So restarting the dev server with a tab open could leave that tab reloading forever.
- **Not tested:** `next dev --webpack`, browsers other than Chromium and Chrome, Windows, Linux.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/nextor2k/next164-manifest-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `bun install` (npm or pnpm work the same)
2. Pin `next@16.3.8`, `react@19.2.6`, `react-dom@19.2.6`, then run `rm -rf .next && next build` (the app uses `output: "standalone"`).
3. Record the size of each `.next/server/app/**/page_client-reference-manifest.js` and the number of `.next/server/chunks/**/*.js` files.
4. Pin `next@16.4.1`, `react@19.3.0`, `react-dom@19.3.0` (16.4.0 behaves the same), then rebuild and compare.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** the client-reference manifests and the number of server chunks stay about the same, because the client-reference graph does not change between the two versions.

**Current**, on the minimal app (Turbopack, `next build`):

| File | 16.3.8 | 16.4.x |
|---|---|---|
| `app/page_client-reference-manifest.js` | 8,094 B | 8,785 B (+8.5%) |
| `app/faq/page_client-reference-manifest.js` | 6,771 B | 7,292 B (+7.7%) |
| `_global-error` manifest | 3,727 B | 4,239 B (+13.7%) |
| server chunk files | 28 | 38 (+36%) |

The number of manifest entries is unchanged. The growth is in the `ssrModuleMapping` chunk lists: each module now references more, smaller server chunks.

In a larger App Router app (several hundred client components, about 55 pages) the effect multiplies. Each module's `ssrModuleMapping` entry goes from about 2 server chunk paths to dozens, which means:
- `page_client-reference-manifest.js` grows about 330 KB per page (+48–65%);
- the server build emits 564 server chunks instead of 409;
- the `standalone` output grows 4–13%;
- the standalone server's warm RSS grows 26–28 MB after loading the same routes (3 runs per side, spreads well below the delta).

Client JS shrinks in the same builds, so the change looks like finer server-side chunking that is listed per module in every manifest.

Things tried:
- `experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime: false` does not change the manifests.
- `experimental.turbopackMangleExportNames: false` removes only part of the extra chunk references.
- The `turbopackChunking` options affect client chunks only.

I found no supported option that restores the 16.3 server chunk granularity.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Available memory (MB): 32019
  Available CPU cores: 16
Binaries:
  Node: 26.5.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.1
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
Next.js Config:
  output: standalone
```

### Which area(s) are affected?

Turbopack, Output (export/standalone)

### Which stage(s) are affected?

`next build` (local), `next start` (local), Other (self-hosted deployment)

### Additional context

We self-host with `output: "standalone"` in containers, so image size and per-container memory are the costs that matter to us. Reproduced on 16.4.0 and 16.4.1; 16.3.8 is the baseline.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/samuelcole/next-hmr-reload-repro

### To Reproduce

1. pnpm install
2. pnpm exec playwright install chromium
3. node repro.mjs

repro.mjs starts next dev three times on the same .next, so Turbopack's dev cache survives between sessions. Session 1 loads /a, does router.push("/b"), then loads /c. Sessions 2 and 3 each start with a different NEXT_PUBLIC_VALUE, POST to a route handler, then load /a and count page loads for 6 seconds. /a renders a client component that reads process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VALUE.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

 Expected: /a loads once per session.
Current (16.4.1): sessions 2 and 3 reload /a about 240 times in 6 seconds. This happened in 6 of 6 runs. The dev server logs GET /a 200 and ✓ Compiled on every reload. 16.3.8 doesn't loop (2 of 2 runs), and 16.5.0-canary.11 looped in 1 of 2.
Evey part is required: the loop goes away if you keep the env value the same, skip the POST, skip the router.push, skip the full load after it, or set experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: false.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0
  Available memory (MB): 49152
  Available CPU cores: 18
Binaries:
  Node: 24.14.1
  pnpm: 10.33.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.1
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

I logged inside `hot-reloader-turbopack.js` during a looping session. On every load, the main client entry's chunk list sends `restart` as its first message instead of `issues`. `subscribeToClientHmrEvents` forwards that through `sendTurbopackMessage`, which bumps `clientHmrVersion`. The page's next `turbopack-subscribe` then carries a stale `hmrVersion` and gets `RELOAD_PAGE` "HMR hash mismatch". That check looks like it came in with #97966. The entry's chunk files are byte-identical between the session that built the cache and the looping one.

From reading the source, without instrumenting it: `update_chunk_list` returns `Update::Total` when the baseline is a `NotFoundVersion`. So `VersionedContentMap::raw_get` may be coming back empty for the entry chunk list after the cache is restored.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/ysfsarikaya/next-turbopack-loadable-manifest-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `git clone https://github.com/ysfsarikaya/next-turbopack-loadable-manifest-repro && cd next-turbopack-loadable-manifest-repro`
2. `./reproduce.sh canary` (or `./reproduce.sh` for the pinned `next@16.3.4`). It installs, runs `next build`, runs `check-manifest.mjs` (compares every route's `react-loadable-manifest.json` with `.next/static/chunks`), starts `next start` on port 3999 and prints the script preloads of `/a` and `/b` with their HTTP status.

Or manually: `pnpm install && npx next build && npx next start`, open http://localhost:3000/b and look for a 404 on `/_next/static/chunks/*.js` in the Network tab.

Setup (App Router, no config, no dependencies besides next/react):

```
app/layout.tsx        renders <Gate />
app/a/page.tsx        nothing route-specific
app/b/page.tsx        renders <OnlyB /> and <Gate /> again
components/Gate.tsx   'use client'; const Heavy = dynamic(() => import('./Heavy').then(m => ({ default: m.Heavy })))
components/OnlyB.tsx  'use client'; import { Heavy } from './Heavy'   // static import of the gate's async target
components/Heavy.tsx  'use client'; ~30 KB inert payload so it gets its own chunk
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current** (16.5.0-canary.15): the per-route manifest of `/b` names a chunk that is never emitted, so the SSR HTML of `/b` preloads a 404:

```
ok       app/_not-found/page  40884  static/chunks/0ux4-jlr--gck.js
ok       app/a/page           40884  static/chunks/0ux4-jlr--gck.js
MISSING  app/b/page           40884  static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js

-- /b
<link rel="preload" href="/_next/static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js" as="script" fetchPriority="low"/>
404  /_next/static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js
```

The only emitted loader for `import('./Heavy')` lives in the layout's chunk and points at the chunk `/a` lists (16.3.4 build):

```js
83467,e=>{e.v(t=>Promise.all(["static/chunks/2legknbp6gahp.js"].map(t=>e.l(t))).then(()=>t(40884)))}
```

In the browser, `/b` logs `Failed to load resource: 404` for `1nahbtiww_lu9.js`; after hydration the loader fetches `2legknbp6gahp.js` (200), which was not preloaded. The page renders and works; the cost is a 404 on every SSR of that route and a later-resolving `next/dynamic` island.

**Expected:** the manifest of `/b` lists the chunk the emitted loader requests (as it does for `/a`), so every preloaded chunk exists.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0
  Available memory (MB): 16384
  Available CPU cores: 8
Binaries:
  Node: 25.0.0
  npm: 11.11.0
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 10.33.2
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.5.0-canary.15
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, Lazy Loading

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), next start (local)

### Additional context

Also reproduces on 16.3.4 and 16.4.2. Does not reproduce with `next build --webpack` (its manifest names an emitted chunk).

All three ingredients are needed; removing any one gives consistent output:

| Gate rendered by layout | Gate also reached from page `/b` | `/b` statically imports `Heavy` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | yes | manifest names an unemitted chunk |
| yes | yes | no  | consistent |
| yes | no  | yes | consistent (manifest = layout's chunk) |
| no  | yes | yes | consistent (`/b` gets its own loader and emitted chunk) |

This looks like the App Router counterpart of the Pages Router `/_app` case discussed in #99149 and fixed by #100091: the loader of `import('./Heavy')` is created in the layout's chunk group with the layout's availability, while the page's manifest resolves the same import with the page's availability, where `Heavy` is already in the entry, so it names a facade-only variant that is never emitted. #100091 says App Router is untouched, and canary.15 (which contains it) still reproduces. #99150 targets the `in_async_module()` mismatch, which is a different path.

components/Gate.tsx   'use client'; const Heavy = dynamic(() => import('./Heavy').then(m => ({ default: m.Heavy })))
components/OnlyB.tsx  'use client'; import { Heavy } from './Heavy'   // static import of the gate's async target
components/Heavy.tsx  'use client'; ~30 KB inert payload so it gets its own chunk
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current** (16.5.0-canary.15): the per-route manifest of `/b` names a chunk that is never emitted, so the SSR HTML of `/b` preloads a 404:

```
ok       app/_not-found/page  40884  static/chunks/0ux4-jlr--gck.js
ok       app/a/page           40884  static/chunks/0ux4-jlr--gck.js
MISSING  app/b/page           40884  static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js

-- /b
<link rel="preload" href="/_next/static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js" as="script" fetchPriority="low"/>
404  /_next/static/chunks/1nahbtiww_lu9.js
```

The only emitted loader for `import('./Heavy')` lives in the layout's chunk and points at the chunk `/a` lists (16.3.4 build):

```js
83467,e=>{e.v(t=>Promise.all(["static/chunks/2legknbp6gahp.js"].map(t=>e.l(t))).then(()=>t(40884)))}
```

In the browser, `/b` logs `Failed to load resource: 404` for `1nahbtiww_lu9.js`; after hydration the loader fetches `2legknbp6gahp.js` (200), which was not preloaded. The page renders and works; the cost is a 404 on every SSR of that route and a later-resolving `next/dynamic` island.

**Expected:** the manifest of `/b` lists the chunk the emitted loader requests (as it does for `/a`), so every preloaded chunk exists.

### Provide environment information

```bash

  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0
  Available memory (MB): 16384
  Available CPU cores: 8
Binaries:
  Node: 25.0.0
  npm: 11.11.0
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 10.33.2
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.5.0-canary.15
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, Lazy Loading

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), next start (local)

### Additional context

Also reproduces on 16.3.4 and 16.4.2. Does not reproduce with `next build --webpack` (its manifest names an emitted chunk).

All three ingredients are needed; removing any one gives consistent output:

| Gate rendered by layout | Gate also reached from page `/b` | `/b` statically imports `Heavy` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | yes | manifest names an unemitted chunk |
| yes | yes | no  | consistent |
| yes | no  | yes | consistent (manifest = layout's chunk) |
| no  | yes | yes | consistent (`/b` gets its own loader and emitted chunk) |

This looks like the App Router counterpart of the Pages Router `/_app` case discussed in #99149 and fixed by #100091: the loader of `import('./Heavy')` is created in the layout's chunk group with the layout's availability, while the page's manifest resolves the same import with the page's availability, where `Heavy` is already in the entry, so it names a facade-only variant that is never emitted. #100091 says App Router is untouched, and canary.15 (which contains it) still reproduces. #99150 targets the `in_async_module()` mismatch, which is a different path.

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repo

The only non-default config:

  experimental: {

  },

ReferenceError: Cannot access 'e' before initialization
    at a.s.e [as b] (lib/addListener.js:1:41)
    at module evaluation (lib/store.js:6:13)
    at module evaluation (lib/addListener.js:1:41)

    at module evaluation (lib/store.js:6:13)
  4 | const INITIAL_STATE = { open: false };
  5 |
> 6 | let state = INITIAL_STATE;
    |             ^
```

**Expected:** the build succeeds, as it does with `turbopackModuleFragments: false`.

`lib/store.js` has no circular imports. In the build output it is split into two fragments that import each other. ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/wodka-bot/next-wasm-trace-regression

### To Reproduce

1. `pnpm install`
2. `pnpm --filter web build`
3. Inspect `apps/web/.next/server/app/api/x/route.js.nft.json` (a one-line script is in the README).
4. Change `next` in `apps/web/package.json` to `16.3.8`, `pnpm install`, rebuild, compare.

The workspace has one App Route handler, `app/api/x/route.ts`, that imports a workspace package `foxlike` whose `index.js` does `import * as wasm from "./tiny.wasm"` (the shape wasm-bindgen emits; `tiny.wasm` is the 8-byte empty module). `apps/web` also declares `dayjs`, `zod` and the devDependency `typescript`, none of which the route imports.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

| next | `api/x/route.js.nft.json` entries | trace contains `dayjs` / `zod` / `typescript` |
|---|---|---|
| 16.3.8 | 124 | no |
| 16.4.1 | 5388 | yes |
| 16.5.0-canary.14 | 5400 | yes |

`app/page.js.nft.json`, whose graph has no wasm, stays at about 130 entries on every version.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/theravengroup/turbopack-stale-tailwind-css

### To Reproduce

1. `pnpm install`
2. `./repro.sh`

Each run cold-builds v1, keeps only `.next/cache`, switches to v2 (the stylesheet **and** a page change), and warm-builds with `TURBO_ENGINE_READ_CONCURRENCY=1`. It then checks which stylesheet version the emitted CSS was compiled from. Setup: `@tailwindcss/turbopack` as a `turbopack.rules` loader for `*.css`, with `turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild` left at its default (on).

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Expected: the warm build emits CSS compiled from the v2 stylesheet.

Current: many warm builds emit v2's utilities compiled against the **v1** stylesheet. Results on an M-series Mac:

| next | `TURBO_ENGINE_READ_CONCURRENCY=1` | `=4` (Vercel's value) |
|---|---|---|
| 16.5.0-canary.15 | 7/10 stale | 2/10 stale |
| 16.4.2 | 4/10 | 4/10 |
| 16.4.1 | 18/33 | 2/10 |

None were seen in 5 runs at the default of 64. In production on Vercel this shipped a stylesheet built from the previous commit's `globals.css`. The deployment logged "Restored build cache from previous deployment", and the build finished with no errors or warnings.

What happens, from tracing every loader call (pid, hash of `source`):

```
pid A  loader(source = v1 globals.css)   <- previous build's content, from the restored cache
pid A  loader(source = v2 globals.css)   <- current content; same worker
emitted CSS = result of call 2 = compiled from v1 (the loader reused in-process state)
```

1. Restoring the cache marks every file read dirty for this session (`session_dependent`). Reading a dirty task's cell returns the previous session's value (`try_read_task_cell`). When `app/page.jsx` is re-read, its change invalidates the loader task. The loader task then runs before the `globals.css` read has been redone, so `WebpackLoadersProcessedAsset::process` hands the loader the **previous build's** `globals.css` as `source`.
2. When the `globals.css` read completes, the loader task is invalidated and runs again with the current content. That part is correct.
3. Both calls can land in the same pooled Node worker. `@tailwindcss/turbopack` keeps a compiler per resource in the worker and rebuilds it only when the file's mtime changes. The mtime didn't change between the two calls, so the second call returns output built from the first `source`. (Filed separately as tailwindlabs/tailwindcss#20584; `@tailwindcss/postcss` already guards against this.)

Step 3 is a loader bug, but steps 1 and 2 are what expose it. webpack only runs a loader on a file's current content, and loaders are written with that assumption. Persistent workers allow in-process caches, and plenty of loaders keep them. Running a loader on content that is about to be replaced is wasted work at best. With any loader that caches per resource, it turns into wrong output that Turbopack accepts as current.

Possible directions (for maintainers to judge):

- Make sure the resource's own content is current before evaluating a webpack loader or PostCSS transform for it. For example, read `self.source.content()` with strong consistency in `WebpackLoadersProcessedAsset::process`, or wait until a session-dependent read of the resource has been redone this session.
- At least document that a loader may be called again for the same resource with different `source` and an unchanged mtime, and must not cache by path or mtime alone.

The window widens when reads are throttled. Vercel's Next.js adapter (`@vercel/next` `dist/adapter/index.js`, `modifyConfig`, still there in 23.0.2) sets `process.env.TURBO_ENGINE_READ_CONCURRENCY = "4"` for every production build where `CI` is set. That's why this showed up on Vercel and not in local builds at the default 64.

Also reproduced on 16.4.2 and 16.4.1, with `@tailwindcss/turbopack` 4.3.3 and `tailwindcss` 4.3.3.

Production: Vercel build machine "4 cores, 8 GB" (iad1), Vercel CLI 64.0.2, `next build` with Turbopack, build cache restored from the previous production deployment.

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, CSS

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

- `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild: false` makes it go away (0/5), at the cost of the warm-cache speedup.
- If only the stylesheet changes, it never goes stale (0/8). The loader task has to be invalidated by another file it depends on before the stylesheet is re-read.
- Possibly the same family as #99163 (SWC plugins running with another configuration after a persistent-cache restore), where a cache restore also leads to work running with inputs that don't belong together.
- Code read at v16.4.1: `turbo-tasks-fs/src/disk.rs` (`read` is `session_dependent`, gated by `TURBO_ENGINE_READ_CONCURRENCY`, default 64), `turbo-tasks-backend/src/backend/mod.rs` (`try_read_task_cell` returns stored data for dirty tasks), `turbopack-node/src/transforms/webpack.rs` (`process` passes `self.source.content()` as the loader's `source`), `turbopack-node/src/process_pool/mod.rs` (idle-worker reuse).

```

1. Restoring the cache marks every file read dirty for this session (`session_dependent`). Reading a dirty task's cell returns the previous session's value (`try_read_task_cell`). When `app/page.jsx` is re-read, its change invalidates the loader task. The loader task then runs before the `globals.css` read has been redone, so `WebpackLoadersProcessedAsset::process` hands the loader the **previous build's** `globals.css` as `source`.
2. When the `globals.css` read completes, the loader task is invalidated and runs again with the current content. That part is correct.
3. Both calls can land in the same pooled Node worker. `@tailwindcss/turbopack` keeps a compiler per resource in the worker and rebuilds it only when the file's mtime changes. The mtime didn't change between the two calls, so the second call returns output built from the first `source`. (Filed separately as tailwindlabs/tailwindcss#20584; `@tailwindcss/postcss` already guards against this.)

Step 3 is a loader bug, but steps 1 and 2 are what expose it. webpack only runs a loader on a file's current content, and loaders are written with that assumption. Persistent workers allow in-process caches, and plenty of loaders keep them. Running a loader on content that is about to be replaced is wasted work at best. With any loader that caches per resource, it turns into wrong output that Turbopack accepts as current.

Possible directions (for maintainers to judge):

- Make sure the resource's own content is current before evaluating a webpack loader or PostCSS transform for it. For example, read `self.source.content()` with strong consistency in `WebpackLoadersProcessedAsset::process`, or wait until a session-dependent read of the resource has been redone this session.
- At least document that a loader may be called again for the same resource with different `source` and an unchanged mtime, and must not cache by path or mtime alone.

The window widens when reads are throttled. Vercel's Next.js adapter (`@vercel/next` `dist/adapter/index.js`, `modifyConfig`, still there in 23.0.2) sets `process.env.TURBO_ENGINE_READ_CONCURRENCY = "4"` for every production build where `CI` is set. That's why this showed up on Vercel and not in local builds at the default 64.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/shunkakinoki/next-use-cache-short-lived-rdc-marker

### To Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/shunkakinoki/next-use-cache-short-lived-rdc-marker
cd next-use-cache-short-lived-rdc-marker
npm install
npm run verify
```

`verify.mjs` builds twice from a clean `.next`. The first build uses `cacheLife("seconds")` and the second uses a `cacheLife("hours")` control. It exits 0 only when the short-lived build warns and the control is clean.

The app is a root layout that renders a zero-arg cached read inside `<Suspense>`, plus six static pages:

```tsx
async function readShared() {
  "use cache";
  cacheLife("seconds");
  return "shared";
}
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current.** With `cacheComponents: true`, every prerendered route that reads the short-lived entry logs:

```
Error: Route "/a": Unexpected cache miss after cache warming phase during prerendering. This is likely caused by non-deterministic arguments that differ between the cache warming phase and the final prerender phase (e.g. unstable array order). Ensure that arguments passed to cached functions are deterministic.
```

```
cacheLife("seconds"): build exit 0, 6 warning(s): /a, /b, /c, /d, /e, /
cacheLife("hours"): build exit 0, 0 warning(s)
```

The function takes no arguments, so the key is deterministic. The build exits 0 and the read still becomes a dynamic hole, but through the anomaly path (`makeUnknownRuntimeDataHangingPromise`) rather than as session data. A real app whose layout reads one short-lived entry on hundreds of routes gets hundreds of these warnings per build, with `"use cache"` and `"use cache: remote"` alike.

**Expected.** A short-lived entry is omitted from the static shell quietly, as it is when the entry is generated during the build or joined from another invocation. No unexpected-miss warning.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Available memory (MB): 48175
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 24.21.0
  npm: 11.19.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.5.0-canary.17 // Latest available version is detected (16.5.0-canary.17).
  react: 19.2.0
  react-dom: 19.2.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

Also reproduces on `16.4.2` and `16.4.0`.

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Use Cache, cacheComponents

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local)

### Additional context

In `use-cache-wrapper.ts`, the leader that finds a short-lived entry in the cache handler during the prospective prerender returns a session-data hanging promise and resolves the shared result as `prerender-dynamic`. It never writes the `SESSION_DATA` marker into the mutable Resume Data Cache:

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/bb63c72077ad7b81b2319f74a7ef3b00c1751483/packages/next/src/server/use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.ts#L3363-L3383

The sibling paths all save the reason. These are the intra-request joiner ([L2991-L2999](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/bb63c72077ad7b81b2319f74a7ef3b00c1751483/packages/next/src/server/use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.ts#L2991-L2999)), the cross-request joiner ([L3222-L3227](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/bb63c72077ad7b81b2319f74a7ef3b00c1751483/packages/next/src/server/use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.ts#L3222-L3227)), and the generation path ([L3560-L3570](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/bb63c72077ad7b81b2319f74a7ef3b00c1751483/packages/next/src/server/use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.ts#L3560-L3570)). Without the marker, the final prerender (no cache signal) misses the RDC and reaches the `UnexpectedCacheMissError` branch ([L2932](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/bb63c72077ad7b81b2319f74a7ef3b00c1751483/packages/next/src/server/use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.ts#L2932)).

Saving the marker in that branch fixes the repro. I applied the equivalent change to the compiled `dist/server/use-cache/use-cache-wrapper.js` and `dist/esm/...` in the repro's `node_modules`, and the `seconds` build dropped to 0 warnings:

```ts
if (resumeDataCache?.mutable) {
  resumeDataCache.cache.set(serializedCacheKey, SESSION_DATA)
}
```

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/roqqq3/turbopack-lazy-glob-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run build`
3. `npm run check`

`components/GlobLoader.tsx` loads `widgets/*.tsx` with a lazy (default) `import.meta.glob`. `components/ImportLoader.tsx` loads `control/WidgetC.tsx` with a plain `import()` as a control. `check.mjs` reads `.next/server/app/page_client-reference-manifest.js` and reports whether each widget's code is in the page's entry scripts.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Running `npm run check` after a production build reports:

WIDGET_A_SIGNATURE: EAGER (in the page entry scripts)
WIDGET_B_SIGNATURE: EAGER (in the page entry scripts)
WIDGET_C_SIGNATURE: lazy (async chunk only)

Current: the modules matched by the lazy (default) `import.meta.glob` in `GlobLoader` are bundled into the page's entry scripts, so they load with the page even though nothing calls their thunks until a button is clicked. The same happens on 16.4.1.

Expected: lazy glob entries are split into async chunks and loaded when their thunk is called, the same as the plain `import()` control (WIDGET_C). The `import.meta.glob` docs describe the default mode as lazy loading.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/yunsii/turbopack-async-race-repro

### To Reproduce

```bash
npm install
npx next build
node repro.cjs race        # n FAILED: (0 , d.D) is not a function   (a later import of n fails the same way)
node repro.cjs sequential  # n evaluated OK
```

`repro.cjs` loads the Turbopack server runtime and chunks produced by `next build` and drives two loaders deterministically. Module graph:

```
lib/root.mjs   top-level await                         -> async, hasAwait=true  (has its own queue)
lib/m.js       imports root, no top-level await         -> async, hasAwait=false (no queue of its own)
lib/n.js       imports m and calls m's export at module scope
```

1. Loader 1 instantiates `m`; `m` awaits `root`. Its exports are registered only after that await (`a.s([...])` comes after `[d]=e.then?(await e)():e`).
2. Loader 2 awaits `root` and, as soon as `root` resolves, instantiates `n` for the first time.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `n` throws `TypeError: (0 , d.D) is not a function` during module evaluation. The error is cached in the module cache, so every later import of `n` (and of everything that depends on it) fails for the lifetime of the process.

**Expected:** `n` waits until `m` has finished evaluating (as it does when the loads are sequential), or more generally: a module must never observe the exports of a dependency that has not finished evaluating unless they are part of an actual import cycle.

Why it happens (`turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/src/shared/runtime/async-module.ts`): `m` was compiled with `hasAwait=false`, so it has no queue and only forwards its dependencies' queues. When `n` is instantiated, `root`'s queue is already `Resolved`, so `fnQueue` does not count it, `fn.queueCount` stays `0` and `handleAsyncDependencies` returns `getResult()` synchronously — but `m`'s continuation that registers its exports is still pending in the microtask queue.

```ts
function fnQueue(q) {
  if (q !== queue && !depQueues.has(q)) {
    depQueues.add(q)
    if (q && q.status === QueueStatus.Unresolved) {  // root is already Resolved -> not waited on
      fn.queueCount++
      q.push(fn)
    }
  }
}
currentDeps.map((dep) => dep[turbopackQueues](fnQueue)) // m (hasAwait=false) only forwards root's queue
return fn.queueCount ? promise : getResult()            // reads m's still-empty exports
```

Reproduces on `next@16.3.0`, `next@16.4.2` and `next@16.5.0-canary.17` (export name differs only because of mangling: `d.sizeFor` on 16.3.0, `d.D` on 16.4+).

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Available memory (MB): 44142
  Available CPU cores: 20
Binaries:
  Node: 22.23.1
  npm: 10.9.8
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.2
  react: 19.2.0
  react-dom: 19.2.0
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, Pages Router, Runtime

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

How this shows up in a real app: with `next start` / standalone, `experimental.preloadEntriesOnStart` (on by default) loads all pages in the background without blocking requests. Requests that arrive right after the server starts load page modules concurrently with the preload. In our app ~68% of server modules are async (because of ESM externals such as `zod/v4`, imported via `await a.y(...)`), and a module that calls a dependency's export at module scope occasionally lands in the window described above. That server process then returns 500 for every page depending on it until it is restarted; whether a process is affected depends on request timing, so the same build produces some healthy and some broken pods (we saw several per day on Kubernetes rolling deploys, error at module evaluation: `TypeError: (0 , d.G) is not a function`).

Workaround: set `experimental.preloadEntriesOnStart: false` and, in the custom server, await `require('next/dist/server/lib/render-server').propagateServerField(dir, 'unstable_preloadEntries', [])` before listening, so module initialization happens on a single loader before any request is accepted.

Open `https:///a/b/c` in a browser: React throws minified error #418 (hydration text mismatch), then the client re-renders with `/a/b/c`. ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current (Vercel):** for a catch-all path that `generateStaticParams` did not return, the on-demand server render puts the whole catch-all value into one percent-encoded canonical segment (`"c":["","a%2Fb%2Fc"]`), so server-side `usePathname()` returns `/a%2Fb%2Fc`. Values derived from it in the server HTML are wrong (`encodeURIComponent(pathname)` gives `%2Fa%252Fb%252Fc`), the wrong HTML is cached until revalidation, and hydration fails with #418. `params` is correct: `{"slug":["a","b","c"]}`. **Expected:** server-side `usePathname()` returns `/a/b/c`, as it does for prerendered paths, under `next start`, and on the client. Separate routes in one Vercel deployment, each requested at a path that was not prerendered: | Route | Request | Server `usePathname()` | |---|---|---| | `[[...slug]]` + `generateStaticParams` + `revalidate` | `/m/n/o` | `/m%2Fn%2Fo` (wrong) | | `[...slug]` + `generateStaticParams` + `revalidate` | `/req/m/n/o` | `/req/m%2Fn%2Fo` (wrong) | | `[[...slug]]` + `generateStaticParams`, no `revalidate` | `/ssg/m/n/o` | `/ssg/m%2Fn%2Fo` (wrong) | | `[[...slug]]` + `revalidate`, no `generateStaticParams` (built as dynamic) | `/isr/m/n/o` | `/isr/m/n/o` (correct) | | `[[...slug]]` + `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` | `/dyn/m/n/o` | `/dyn/m/n/o` (correct) | | `[a]/[b]` + `generateStaticParams` + `revalidate` | `/one/m/n` | `/one/m/n` (correct) | ### Provide environment information ``` Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0: Tue Aug 11 21:06:40 PDT 2026; root:xnu-13432.1.9~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050 Available memory (MB): 49152 Available CPU cores: 18 Binaries: Node: 26.5.1 npm: 11.17.0 Yarn: N/A pnpm: 10.26.2 Relevant Packages: next: 16.4.2 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.2). eslint-config-next: N/A react: 19.3.1 react-dom: 19.3.1 typescript: 7.0.2 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` Deployed on Vercel (Node.js 24.x, default Turbopack build). Also reproduces with `next@16.5.0-canary.17` deployed to Vercel. ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Dynamic Routes, Navigation, Runtime ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Vercel (Deployed) ### Additional context - Local `next build && next start` is correct for every path above, including the RSC response. - Related but separate: #95648 (on Vercel, the root route's server-side `usePathname()` is `/index`; fix in #95973). That fix normalizes only the root `/index` case. In this repro the root `/` is correct (`"c":["",""]`). - Guess (unverified): on Vercel the fallback render receives the catch-all value as one string (`a/b/c`) and builds the canonical URL by encoding it as a single segment. `"c"` has one element for three path segments.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/akirilyuk/next-link-commit-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Production build (`next build`, `next start`, Turbopack), Next 16.2.6, without `cacheComponents`.
2. Open a list page whose rows are `<Link>`s with default prefetch to a dynamic detail page. The detail page shares every layout with the list, and the only loading boundary is above both.
3. Click a row right after the page loads, on a CPU-constrained host (Docker, 2 CPUs), so the click lands while the target's metadata-only prefetch is in flight.
4. About 1 click in 100 never navigates.

**Shape**

```
app/(app)/layout.tsx                    async, reads the session on every request
app/(app)/loading.tsx                   the only loading boundary on the path
app/(app)/admin/layout.tsx              force-dynamic, awaits connection()
app/(app)/admin/users/page.tsx          list of <Link href="/admin/users/[id]">, default prefetch
app/(app)/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx     dynamic, static `metadata`, no loading.tsx of its own
```

Navigating from the list to a detail page keeps every layout, so there's no loading boundary under the segment that changes.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** the URL changes to the detail page and it renders.

**Current:**

**A failing run (Playwright trace, times from the document request)**

- 144 ms: `/_tree` prefetches for the visible links, the target included.
- 304 ms: a metadata-only prefetch of the target starts (`Next-Router-State-Tree: ["",{},null,"metadata-only"]`). It finishes at 321 ms.
- 317 ms: the click's navigation request starts, with `refetch` on `[id]`. It returns 200 with the full payload, and the page's chunks load with 200.
- After that there's no `history.pushState`, no render, no console error, no page error and no further request for that URL. The URL stays on the list until the test times out at 15 s.

An init-script probe saw the same thing: in failing runs the navigation body arrives and then nothing happens, while in passing runs `pushState` follows the body by 10 to 20 ms. The page was hydrated and the `<Link>` click handler had run.

**Rates**

It needs CPU contention. In Docker (Linux arm64, 2 CPUs, Playwright 1.62.1, Chromium, one worker) it failed 1/165, 3/300 and 2/300 times. On a 14-core Mac it failed 0 times in about 500 runs. It also failed three times on GitHub-hosted Linux runners in CI.

**Where I think it waits**

In 16.2.6, `createCacheNodeForSegment` in `router-reducer/ppr-navigations.js` uses `waitForSegmentCacheEntry(metadataEntry).then(...)` as the head when the metadata entry is still `Pending`. In the failing trace, the navigation starts 13 ms after the metadata-only prefetch of the same URL, while it's pending, and the transition has no boundary to show while it waits. From the outside I can't tell whether that promise never settles or React never pings the lane (the #98303 fingerprint). I don't have lane bits from a failing run of the real app.

**What didn't reproduce it**

I built a small app with the same tree (50 links, `(app)/loading.tsx`, an async layout, a dynamic detail page) and ran it in the same 2-CPU Docker setup:

| variant | failures / runs |
|---|---|
| base | 0 / 600 |
| plus a sidebar of 12 prefetched links | 0 / 600 |
| plus `generateMetadata`, a ~10 KB page, and the load event 150 ms after hydration, so the click lands inside the target's metadata-only prefetch in about 1 of 3 runs | 0 / 600 |

The request trees match the failing run (the same metadata-only second stage, the same `refetch` marker), so the overlap alone isn't enough in a small app. Ours has a much busier main thread at that moment (a 53 KB document and many client components), which fits the contention pattern described in #98305 and #98303.

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: arm64
  Available memory (MB): 3921
  Available CPU cores: 2
Binaries:
  Node: 24.18.1
  npm: 11.16.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.6
  react: 19.2.8
  react-dom: 19.2.8
Next.js Config:
  output: standalone
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Linking and Navigating, Metadata

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), next start (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

About the reproduction: this app copies the failing app's route shape and request sequence, but it has not failed yet (0 failures in 1,800 runs, table below). The failing app is private. The repo has the harness and an init-script probe (`pushState`, RSC request timings, React root lane bits) that dumps everything on a failure. Related: #98684 (open, same race with a `loading.tsx`), #99651 (same signature on 16.3.6, closed for lacking a reproduction), #98303 (same lane fingerprint, fixed in 16.3).

This replaces #100433 and #100434, which the bot closed because of how I filled in the link field.

Not yet tested on 16.3 or later. #95391 and a React bump in 16.3.0 fixed the #98303 variant of this lane fingerprint, so this may already be fixed. If that would help, we can measure our app on 16.4.2.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/CodingDiego/next-client-hook-dynamic-bun

### To Reproduce

1. `bun install`
2. `bun --bun next build` (Bun runs `next`): one `CLIENT_HOOK_DYNAMIC` error with its stack is printed per prerendered page (4 in the reproduction, 18 in the app it was cut from); the build exits 0.
3. `bun run build` (Node runs `next` through its shebang): nothing is printed; the build exits 0.

Count with `bun --bun next build 2>&1 | grep -c CLIENT_HOOK_DYNAMIC`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current.** With `cacheComponents: true`, a client component calling `usePathname()` rendered inside `<Suspense>` in `app/[locale]/layout.tsx`, and a route with fallback params (`/[locale]/projects/[slug]`), `next build` under Bun prints, per prerendered page:

```
Error: Route "/[locale]/projects/[slug]": Next.js encountered URL data `usePathname()` in a Client Component outside of `<Suspense>`.
...
  digest: 'CLIENT_HOOK_DYNAMIC'
}
```

The component *is* inside `<Suspense>`; the build succeeds and the output is correct (the route is `◐ Partial Prerender`). The same build under Node prints nothing. `useSelectedLayoutSegments()` instead of `usePathname()`, or `export const instant = false`, change nothing.

**Expected.** The same output as under Node: no rejection reported for work spawned inside an aborted prerender.

**Where it comes from.** `packages/next/src/server/dynamic-rendering-utils.ts` creates the error with digest `CLIENT_HOOK_DYNAMIC` and rejects a promise with it when a client hook reads URL data during a prerender; the prerender then aborts on purpose, so nobody awaits that promise. Next silences such rejections with the process-wide `unhandledRejection` listener installed by `server/node-environment-extensions/unhandled-rejection.external.js` (`filteringUnhandledRejectionHandler`): the filter calls `workUnitAsyncStorage.getStore()` and returns without reporting when the store is a prerender whose `renderSignal` is aborted. Under Bun the listener runs outside the async context of the code that created the rejected promise, so `getStore()` returns `undefined`, the filter never recognises the prerender and the rejection is reported. Under Node the listener keeps the context and the rejection is swallowed. The filter could avoid depending on the listener's async context, for instance by marking the rejected promise or error (the digest is already there) and checking that, or by attaching a no-op catch where the promise is created.

### Provide environment information

```

  Platform: win32
  Arch: x64
  Version: Windows 11 Pro
  Available memory (MB): 32437
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 26.5.0

  Yarn: 1.22.22

  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.1
  react-dom: 19.3.1
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/mgoodfellow/turbopack-sw-guard-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `pnpm install`
2. `pnpm build` (Turbopack), then `pnpm check`. It prints `guard MISSING`.
3. `pnpm start` and open `http://localhost:3000/?nosw`. The `?nosw` query deletes `Navigator.prototype.serviceWorker` before hydration, which simulates a browser without service worker support.
4. Repeat with `pnpm build:webpack` for comparison.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current (Turbopack):** the `if (!navigator.serviceWorker)` branch is removed from the client bundle. On a browser without service workers, the code after it runs and throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'addEventListener')`.

```js
(0,t.useEffect)(()=>{try{navigator.serviceWorker.addEventListener("message",()=>{}),s("service worker supported")}catch(e){...
```

**Expected (what webpack emits):** the check stays in the bundle and runs.

```js
(0,a.useEffect)(()=>{try{if(!navigator.serviceWorker)return void r("guard ran: no service worker support");navigator.serviceWorker.addEventListener(...
```

Only truthiness checks on `navigator.serviceWorker` are folded:

| Check | Survives |
| --- | --- |
| `if (!navigator.serviceWorker)` | no |
| `const sw = navigator.serviceWorker; if (!sw)` | no |
| `navigator.serviceWorker === undefined` | yes |
| `typeof navigator.serviceWorker === 'undefined'` | yes |
| `!('serviceWorker' in navigator)` | yes |
| `!navigator?.serviceWorker` | yes |
| `!window.navigator.serviceWorker` | yes |
| `!navigator.clipboard` (control) | yes |

`navigator.serviceWorker` is undefined in iOS in-app browsers (WKWebView, the Google app, Chrome on iOS) and in insecure contexts, so this is a common feature check. In our production app it sent 145 iOS users to the error boundary within five days after we switched from `next build --webpack` to Turbopack. The same check had shipped safely with webpack for months. Libraries such as `@serwist/window` and `workbox-window` call `navigator.serviceWorker` in their constructors and expect the app to check support first.

This looks related to Turbopack's well-known-object handling of `navigator.serviceWorker.register(new URL(...))` worker references: the modelled object seems to be treated as compile-time truthy.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #38~24.04.4-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon Sep 14 16:37:11 UTC 2
  Available memory (MB): 31828
  Available CPU cores: 24
Binaries:
  Node: 24.12.0
  npm: 11.6.2
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 10.34.5
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.2 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.2).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

Also reproduces on `16.5.0-canary.19`.

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Workaround: `'serviceWorker' in navigator` or `Reflect.get(navigator, 'serviceWorker')`.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/herman72/nextjs-fetch-request-no-store-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`, then `npm run dev`.
2. Open http://localhost:3000/request and read the terminal of `next dev`: it logs the error below.
3. Open http://localhost:3000/request-and-init: the same error.
4. Open http://localhost:3000/init and http://localhost:3000/request-no-option: no error.

The four pages differ only in their fetch. Each one reads `headers()` first, then fetches `https://api.vercel.app/blog`, and each one shows "25 posts", so each fetch works:

| Page | The fetch | Error |
|---|---|---|
| `/request` | `fetch(new Request(url, { cache: "no-store" }))` | yes |
| `/request-and-init` | `fetch(new Request(url), { cache: "no-store" })` | yes |
| `/init` | `fetch(url, { cache: "no-store" })` | no |
| `/request-no-option` | `fetch(new Request(url))` | no |

`next.config.mjs` sets `cacheComponents: true` and `partialPrefetching: true`. Without `partialPrefetching`, no page logs the error.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: on each visit of `/request` and `/request-and-init`, `next dev` logs:

```text
Error: Route "/request": Next.js encountered the unstable value `Date.now()` while prerendering.

This value can change between renders, so it must be either prerendered or computed later.
...
Learn more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-current-time
    at Page (app/request/page.js:14:7)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/TrevorBurnham/nextjs-instanceof-api-error

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repo and run `npm install && npm run build`
2. Inspect the build output:

```bash
grep -c "class e extends d.ServiceException" .next/server/app/api/*/route.js
```

Output shows each route has its own class definition:
```
.next/server/app/api/test/route.js:1
.next/server/app/api/test2/route.js:1
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** When multiple routes import the same class from an external package, Turbopack inlines a separate copy of the class definition into each route's bundle. This causes `instanceof` checks to fail across routes because each route has a different class object.

**Expected:** The class should be bundled once in a shared chunk and imported by all routes, preserving `instanceof` behavior.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 24.2.0
  Available memory (MB): 36864
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 20.18.1
  npm: 10.8.2
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 15.5.10
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.0.0
  react-dom: 19.0.0
  typescript: 5.7.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), Other (Deployed), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

I noticed this when working with AWS SDK clients: I had some logic that checked

```
if (error instanceof AccessDeniedException) { ... }
```

where `AccessDeniedException` was imported from one of those client packages. In local dev, the condition was `true` as expected. But in production (with the Turbopack build), it'd return `false`!

As a workaround, I've added all of my AWS SDK clients to `serverExternalPackages` for now.

body_text: ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/OblikStudio/test-nextjs/tree/issue-excessive-renders ### To Reproduce Here's the issue: 1. Put a `use client` component inside `layout.tsx` 2. Put another `use client` component inside `page.tsx` 3. Make sure that the page JS chuck takes longer to load 4. The layout child will excessively render until the page chunk loads This is reproducible with a fresh installation of Next.js 16.1.6: 1. Clone [the repo](https://github.com/OblikStudio/test-nextjs/tree/issue-excessive-renders) 1. `npm run build` 1. `npm run start` 1. Open Chrome DevTools 1. Disable Cache 1. Navigate to http://localhost:3000 1. You'll see a bunch of logs "rendering LayoutChild" 1. The logs stop only after seeing "rendering PageChild" 1. If you enable network throttling, the issue gets worse Here's what happens: And here's a video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfc1ffaa-0617-4e4f-ac31-5d644a76eb7d ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current behavior** is that Next.js re-renders any client components inside a `layout.tsx` until the JS chunk for the corresponding route is downloaded. If for some reason this never happens (like blocking the request URL), Next.js **gets stuck in an infinite loop**. **Expected behavior** is to render the layout child once and when the route chunk is downloaded — to render the page child. ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 24.6.0: Wed Nov 5 21:34:00 PST 2025; root:xnu-11417.140.69.705.2~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T8132 Available memory (MB): 16384 Available CPU cores: 10 Binaries: Node: 22.21.0 npm: 10.9.4 Yarn: N/A pnpm: 10.19.0 Relevant Packages: next: 16.1.6 // Latest available version is detected (16.1.6). eslint-config-next: N/A react: 19.2.3 react-dom: 19.2.3 typescript: 5.9.3 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) React ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) next start (local) ### Additional context This is reproducible on Next.js 15.4.10 too. It's where I initially spotted the issue, in my actual app. I thought I was doing something wrong and was going crazy, until I stripped everything down to a couple of files and reproduced it in a fresh installation, and even on the latest version of Next as well. It seems like there's some sort of race condition that makes React go crazy until the rest of the JS gets loaded. It was tricky to debug because the issue is affected by network conditions, so if you test locally and your JS chunk is small, the layout child will render just once, as expected. But if you turn on network throttling (or you put crap in your JS chunk to make it larger), you'll start seeing the issue.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/quiet-tdd-rzgf2d

### To Reproduce

1. Open Safari browser
2. Make sure Safari resumes with last session tabs when opening
     - On MacOS: configure the "Safari opens with" setting to "All windows from last session" or "All non-private windows from last session" (Safari > Settings > General > "Safari opens with")
     - On iOS this should be default behavior, haven't found a specific setting related to it
3. Open the reproduction codesandbox standalone preview (https://rzgf2d-3000.csb.app/)
4. Click the "Route 1" link
5. Quit Safari browser 
    - On MacOS via Toolbar > Right click Safari browser icon > Select "Quit"
    - On iOS:
         - Swipe up from the bottom to the middle of your screen and hold until you see the App Switcher
         - Swipe the Safari iOS browser app screen up and out of your screen to quit it
6. Re-open Safari browser
    - Assert the "Route 1" codesandbox preview page is shown (or select that tab after reopening)
    - Assert the back button seems interactable and is not disabled
    - Assert the address bar ends with: `/route-1`
7. Click the back button
    - Assert the "Route 1" page content is still showing (scroll position might change)
    - Assert the address bar actually points at `/`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Following the steps of reproduction, I would expect the content of the "Home" route to be shown after using the back button on the "Route 1" route, but the content of the "Route 1" route is persisted.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.2.0: Tue Nov 18 21:07:05 PST 2025; root:xnu-12377.61.12~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6020
  Available memory (MB): 16384
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 20.19.5
  npm: 10.8.2
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 10.11.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.0-canary.48 // Latest available version is detected (16.2.0-canary.48).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.4
  react-dom: 19.2.4
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Linking and Navigating, Pages Router

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

General description: Opening a Next.JS site in Safari browser, navigating to different pages, quitting Safari browser and reopening it (resuming from that Next.JS site) and then trying to use the browser back button results in the actual route in address bar to update correctly, scroll might be updated (assumed restoration), but the contents of the latest page that was visited is persisted - never showing the actual previous pages content.

This mainly impacts users on iOS as just swiping away the browser app, while later reopening it, while you keep a Next.JS powered site open in a tab will result in this situation (assumed common browsing behavior) - With reported confusion and frustration for users as a result.

Reproducible on operating systems (including, but unknown if limited to):
- MacOS Sequoia (15)
- MacOS Tahoe (26)
- iOS 26

Reproducible on browser(s):
- MacOS: Safari browser
- iOS: Any browser (assumed because of safari under the hood)

Reproduction steps tested on Chrome and Firefox on MacOS and behavior is as expected: pages back in history show as expected after quit and reopening of the browser.

I've not as of yet been able to pinpoint a specific Next.JS version that introduced this behavior, but it does affect both the Pages and App router in various Next.JS versions. It happens both when using `next/link` and regular anchor tags.

Versions / routers of Next.JS in projects where I've reproduced this issue:
- Next.JS `^12.2.0` - Pages router - Hosted on vercel
- Next.JS `^14.2.3` - Pages router - Hosted on vercel
- Next.JS `^14.2.35` - App router - Hosted on vercel
- Next.JS `15.5.9` - Pages router - Hosted on vercel 
    - Tested local dev / build + start of this version, same behavior
- Next.JS `^16.1.6` - App router - Hosted on vercel

Note: Similar behavior has anecdotally been reported to also apply when leaving a Next.JS site in iOS Safari browser tab open for long in the background and returning to it - reported duration was 3 hours, not reproduced yet, but assumed to be caused by similar underlying issue.

Note: So far this affects any Next.JS powered site I've tried to reproduce with, including https://vercel.com/ (tested through https://vercel.com/blog and navigating to blog post)

Reproduction steps tested on Chrome and Firefox on MacOS and behavior is as expected: pages back in history show as expected after quit and reopening of the browser.

I've not as of yet been able to pinpoint a specific Next.JS version that introduced this behavior, but it does affect both the Pages and App router in various Next.JS versions. It happens both when using `next/link` and regular anchor tags.

Versions / routers of Next.JS in projects where I've reproduced this issue:
- Next.JS `^12.2.0` - Pages router - Hosted on vercel
- Next.JS `^14.2.3` - Pages router - Hosted on vercel
- Next.JS `^14.2.35` - App router - Hosted on vercel
- Next.JS `15.5.9` - Pages router - Hosted on vercel 
    - Tested local dev / build + start of this version, same behavior
- Next.JS `^16.1.6` - App router - Hosted on vercel

Note: Similar behavior has anecdotally been reported to also apply when leaving a Next.JS site in iOS Safari browser tab open for long in the background and returning to it - reported duration was 3 hours, not reproduced yet, but assumed to be caused by similar underlying issue.

Hello dear Next maintainers,  

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/garronej/turbopack-emotion-dual-module

### To Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/garronej/turbopack-emotion-dual-module
cd turbopack-emotion-dual-module
pnpm install
pnpm run dev-turbopack
```

Open console, see hydration error.

Run again with `pnpm run dev-webpack`, no hydration error.  

### Current vs. Expected behavior

## Observed logs

Turbopack:

```txt
tss-react CJS
@emotion/react loaded: dist/emotion-react.cjs.js
@emotion/react loaded: _isolated-hnrs/dist/emotion-react-_isolated-hnrs.cjs.js
tss-react/next/pagesDir CJS
@emotion/react loaded: _isolated-hnrs/dist/emotion-react-_isolated-hnrs.development.esm.js
@emotion/react loaded: dist/emotion-react.development.esm.js
tss-react/mui CJS
```

Webpack:

```txt
tss-react CJS
@emotion/react loaded: dist/emotion-react.cjs.js
@emotion/react loaded: _isolated-hnrs/dist/emotion-react-_isolated-hnrs.cjs.js
tss-react/next/pagesDir CJS
@emotion/react loaded: dist/emotion-react.cjs.mjs
tss-react/mui CJS
```

## Expected behavior

Turbopack should not load both of these as separate live implementations in the same server graph:

- `dist/emotion-react.cjs.js`
- `dist/emotion-react.development.esm.js`

Webpack does not hit that split because `dist/emotion-react.cjs.mjs` is only a thin ESM re-export of `dist/emotion-react.cjs.js`.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.0.0: Wed Sep 17 21:35:32 PDT 2025; root:xnu-12377.1.9~141/RELEASE_ARM64_T6020
  Available memory (MB): 65536
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 22.12.0
  npm: 11.4.1
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 10.13.1
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.0-canary.99 // Latest available version is detected (16.2.0-canary.99).
  eslint-config-next: 15.5.7
  react: 19.0.0
  react-dom: 19.0.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

## Why this looks like a Turbopack bug

`@emotion/react` exposes distinct conditional export targets for:

- `default` -> `dist/emotion-react.cjs.js`
- `import` -> `dist/emotion-react.cjs.mjs`
- `development.module` -> `dist/emotion-react.development.esm.js`

Turbopack appears to resolve both the CJS target and the separate development ESM target in one server render path. That creates a dual-module situation and leads to hydration / SSR issues.

## Additional context

The repro uses `tss-react/next/pagesDir`, but the suspected root cause is not `tss-react` itself. The relevant signal is that Turbopack resolves `@emotion/react` to both the CJS implementation and a separate development ESM implementation in the same graph, while webpack effectively collapses to a single implementation.

@emotion/react loaded: dist/emotion-react.cjs.mjs
tss-react/mui CJS
```

## Expected behavior

Turbopack should not load both of these as separate live implementations in the same server graph:

- `dist/emotion-react.cjs.js`
- `dist/emotion-react.development.esm.js`

Webpack does not hit that split because `dist/emotion-react.cjs.mjs` is only a thin ESM re-export of `dist/emotion-react.cjs.js`.

next dev (local)

### Additional context

## Why this looks like a Turbopack bug

`@emotion/react` exposes distinct conditional export targets for:

- `default` -> `dist/emotion-react.cjs.js`
- `import` -> `dist/emotion-react.cjs.mjs`
- `development.module` -> `dist/emotion-react.development.esm.js`

Turbopack appears to resolve both the CJS target and the separate development ESM target in one server render path. That creates a dual-module situation and leads to hydration / SSR issues.

## Additional context

The repro uses `tss-react/next/pagesDir`, but the suspected root cause is not `tss-react` itself. The relevant signal is that Turbopack resolves `@emotion/react` to both the CJS implementation and a separate development ESM implementation in the same graph, while webpack effectively collapses to a single implementation.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/chandra2607/nextjs-webpack-turbopack-issue.git ### To Reproduce ```bash git clone https://github.com/chandra2607/nextjs-webpack-turbopack-issue.git cd nextjs-webpack-turbopack-issue # Turbopack (next build) docker build --build-arg BUILD_CMD=build -t repro-turbo . 2>&1 | tee out-turbo.txt # Webpack (next build --webpack) docker build --build-arg BUILD_CMD=build:webpack -t repro-webpack . 2>&1 | tee out-webpack.txt # Compare grep "not-found\|Retrying\|Generating static\|ƒ" out-webpack.txt grep "not-found\|Retrying\|Generating static\|ƒ" out-turbo.txt ``` ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current behavior:** - `next build --webpack`: webpack's static generation worker **executes not-found.tsx** at build time (side effects fire, fetches run) and logs `Retrying 1/3...` for transient Google Font download failures - `next build` (Turbopack): static generation worker **never enters not-found.tsx** and emits no retry logs — the component is silently skipped - Both produce the same final output: `ƒ /_not-found (Dynamic)` **Expected behavior:** Both bundlers should behave identically for `/_not-found` during the build. If the route is dynamic, neither should probe-render it. If one does, both should — so build-time side effects are predictable regardless of which bundler is used. ### Provide environment information ```bash Next.js: 16.2.1 Node: 22-alpine3.20 (Docker) React: 19.0.0 OS: Linux x86_64 ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Webpack, Turbopack, Font (next/font) ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) next build (local) ### Additional context Hi everyone — I've been digging into some weird build log differences between `next build --webpack` and `next build` (Turbopack) and wanted to write up what I found in case others have run into the same thing or can add context. There are two separate observations below. I'm not 100% sure whether either of these is a bug, a regression, or intentional — just sharing the data. --- ## Observation 1 — `not-found.tsx` component body appears to run at build time with webpack, but not with Turbopack ### What I noticed When I run `next build --webpack`, I can see the body of my `not-found.tsx` getting executed during "Generating static pages" — even though `/_not-found` ends up classified as `ƒ (Dynamic)` in the build output. When I switch to `next build` (Turbopack), nothing in `not-found.tsx` runs at build time at all. Both builds show the same final route table. Both produce: ``` Route (app) ┌ ƒ / └ ƒ /_not-found ƒ (Dynamic) server-rendered on demand ``` ### Repro component (`not-found.tsx`) To keep things simple I stripped it down to a fully synchronous, no-async, no-fetch component: ```tsx export default function NotFound() { console.log("[not-found] component evaluated"); console.log("[not-found] rendering"); return (

404 - Page Not Found

); } ``` ### Webpack build output ``` Generating static pages using 1 worker (0/1) ... [not-found] component evaluated [not-found] rendering ✓ Generating static pages using 1 worker (1/1) in 320ms ``` The component body runs during build. ### Turbopack build output ``` Generating static pages using 1 worker (0/1) ... ✓ Generating static pages using 1 worker (1/1) in 230ms ``` No logs at all — the component wasn't touched. ### What happens when `not-found.tsx` has a network call With a `fetch("http://missing-service:4005/test", { cache: "no-store" })` inside: ``` [not-found] component evaluated [not-found] fetching remote data [fetchRemoteData] about to fetch http://missing-service:4005/test [fetchRemoteData] fetch failed (expected): Dynamic server usage: Route /_global-error ... ``` Turbopack: nothing. No logs, no fetch attempt. ### Why this matters If your `not-found.tsx` (or any component it imports) has side effects — reading env vars during module init, opening a DB connection, making a health-check request — those things appear to silently fire at build time under webpack but not under Turbopack. Code that's only been tested with `next build` could behave differently in environments that use `next build --webpack`. I also tried `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` — it didn't change the behavior for either bundler. **Has anyone else seen this, or can confirm whether this is expected behavior?** --- ## Observation 2 — `Retrying 1/3...` shows up in webpack builds but not Turbopack when using `next/font/google` ### What I noticed When `next/font/google` is in `layout.tsx`, I mostly see this during the webpack compilation phase: ``` Creating an optimized production build ... Retrying 1/3... ✓ Compiled successfully in 10.9s ``` This log never shows up in Turbopack builds. ### Full example from a Docker build (`node:22-alpine3.20`) **Webpack:** ``` ▲ Next.js 16.2.1 (webpack) Creating an optimized production build ... Retrying 1/3... ✓ Compiled successfully in 10.9s ``` **Turbopack:** ``` ▲ Next.js 16.2.1 (Turbopack) Creating an optimized production build ... ✓ Compiled successfully in 5.7s ``` **due to this issue , the overall build time takes longer to complete.** **Has anyone else seen `Retrying 1/3...` in their webpack builds, especially in Docker or CI environments?** --- ## Comparison with Next.js 14.2 Neither of these behaviors appeared in `next build --webpack` on Next.js 14.2. The `[not-found] component evaluated` logs were absent and `Retrying 1/3...` was not reliably reproducible under the same Docker setup (`node:22-alpine3.20`). Both started showing up after upgrading to 16.x. Not sure if this is a regression or an intentional change in how the static generation worker handles `/_not-found` and how the font fetcher is implemented — mentioning it in case it helps narrow things down. --- ## Environment - Next.js: 16.2.1 - Node: 22 (Alpine 3.20 in Docker, native for local) - React: 19.x - OS: Linux (Docker) / macOS (local) ## Related issues - [#76473](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/76473) — Next.js build in GitHub Actions fails due to failed Google Fonts fetching - [#91653](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/91653) — Turbopack Google Fonts `http2 feature is not enabled` on some platforms (16.2) - [#86390](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/86390) — Turbopack crashes when Route Handler calls `notFound()` - [#62228](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/62228) — `not-found.tsx` SSR differences
