### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/chooblarin/next-prebuilt-skew-protection-repro

### To Reproduce

Full step-by-step instructions are in the repro's README (Skew Protection is a Vercel platform feature, so reproduction requires a Vercel Pro project with Skew Protection enabled — it cannot run in a sandbox).

Summary: deploy the repro twice via `vercel build` + `vercel deploy --prebuilt` with different `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID` values, then (1) observe the served HTML emits `data-dpl-id="dpl_..."` instead of the custom ID, and (2) compare pinning with curl: `x-deployment-id: dpl_<old>` is NOT pinned while `x-deployment-id: <old custom id>` IS pinned to the old deployment.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:**

When building via `vercel build` with `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID` set, Next.js auto-enables `experimental.runtimeServerDeploymentId` (`packages/next/src/server/config.ts`, gated on `hasNextSupport` — true because `vercel build` sets `NOW_BUILDER=1`). At runtime, `base-server.ts` then reads `process.env.NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID` from the **runtime** environment, where Vercel injects the platform `dpl_...` ID.

As a result, dynamically rendered HTML emits `data-dpl-id="dpl_..."`, and clients attach that ID to Server Actions / RSC requests. But Vercel's Skew Protection for **prebuilt** deployments pins only by the build-time custom deployment ID (the one in `routes-manifest.json`). The two never match, so Skew Protection is silently inoperative: every cross-deployment Server Action from a stale tab fails with `UnrecognizedActionError` — exactly the failure Skew Protection exists to prevent.

**Expected:**

Clients should be handed a deployment ID that the platform's skew routing can actually resolve. Either:
- the runtime override should not replace the custom ID when the custom ID is the documented pinning key for prebuilt deployments, or
- `runtimeServerDeploymentId` should not be auto-enabled in this scenario, or
- at minimum, the flag and this interaction should be documented (it currently appears in no Next.js or Vercel docs).

**Verified workaround:** explicitly setting `experimental: { runtimeServerDeploymentId: false }` makes the served HTML carry the build-time custom ID, and prebuilt Skew Protection then pins correctly end-to-end.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 10
Binaries:
  Node: 24.16.0
  npm: 11.13.0
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 10.30.3
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.6
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.6
  react-dom: 19.2.6
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A

(Deployed environment: Vercel Pro, `vercel` CLI 51.x, `vercel build` + `vercel deploy --prebuilt --archive=tgz` from GitHub Actions, Node.js 24)
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Runtime, Server Actions, Output

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

- The auto-enable logic is present on canary today: `packages/next/src/server/config.ts` (search for `runtimeServerDeploymentId`), and the runtime override is in `packages/next/src/server/base-server.ts` (`this.deploymentId = process.env.NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID` when the flag is enabled).
- `runtimeServerDeploymentId` is not documented anywhere; we found this by reading the source after weeks of debugging a production incident.
- The Vercel CLI error for over-long deployment IDs links to `https://vercel.com/docs/skew-protection#custom-skew-protection-deployment-id`, but that section does not exist on the current Skew Protection docs page.
- Related (but distinct): #88496 / #88941 (automatic deploymentId for prebuilt skew protection and its revert), #88327 (docs request for `deploymentId` / `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID`), #92154 (`generateBuildId` not respected in v16.2.0+ — possibly the same refactor area).
- Confirmed with Vercel support at the time: "the request reached our edge with the deployment ID attached, but Skew Protection did not end up pinning the request to that deployment."

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/dakini10/next-loading-stall-repro

### To Reproduce

```sh
npm install
npx next build
ITEM_COUNT=200 BLURB_REPEAT=6 PAGE_DELAY_MS=200 ./run-probe.sh mine 144 8 2
```

`run-probe.sh` clicks the Server Action button and watches whether the list ever reflects the
new order, over N parallel Playwright runs with two busy-loop processes competing for CPU, then
prints a tally. The failure is stochastic — a single run proves nothing, so please budget
n ≥ 150 on 16.3.4.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** the Server Action writes a cookie, calls `revalidatePath`, and the page
re-renders with the new order.

**Current:** intermittently the page never updates. The action's `POST` returns `200` with a
correct payload, nothing is left in flight, no error is logged, and the old DOM stays
indefinitely (observed out to 60s). A later `router.refresh()` does not recover it — the new
lane suspends the same way.

Read off the `FiberRoot` after the action has settled:

```
pendingLanes=512  suspendedLanes=512  warmLanes=512  entangledLanes=512  pingedLanes=0
```

A transition lane is suspended and was **never pinged**, although the thenables the boundary
parked on have already fulfilled. `actionQueue.pending` is `null` (the router has finished);
the page's RSC chunk sits at `resolved_model` and is never rendered.

### Rates measured

Same machine, same knobs. A run is only counted when the lane signature above is present — a
run that merely missed the 15s window on a loaded machine ends with lanes back at `0` and is
tallied separately, not as this bug.

| config | stalls / runs |
|---|---|
| 16.2.6 | 5 / 72, and 16 / 72 in an earlier batch |
| **16.3.4** | **2 / 192** |
| 16.4.0-canary.19 | 0 / 141 |
| 16.2.6, `app/(app)/loading.jsx` deleted | 1 / 132 |

#95391 (shipped in 16.3.0) clearly took a large bite out of this, but 16.3.4 still reproduces.

Three caveats, so the table is not over-read:

- **`loading.js` raises the rate but is not strictly required.** I expected removing it to take
  this to zero — related reports describe it as necessary — and it did not: 1 / 132 still
  carried the exact lane signature. Note the no-`loading.js` arm ran at a *higher* load (1-min
  load average 61 → 168) than the arm that produced 5 / 72 (13 → 58), so load does not explain
  the reduction; if anything it understates it.
- **The rate moves a lot with machine load.** The same 16.2.6 build measured 22% starting from
  a load average around 31 and 7% starting from around 13, so batches taken hours apart are not
  comparable to each other. The table establishes *that* 16.3.4 still reproduces, not by how
  much the rate differs between versions. (A properly interleaved comparison is running; I will
  add it as a comment.)
- **0 / 141 on canary is not evidence that canary fixed it.** At a ~1% rate, 141 runs cannot
  distinguish "fixed" from "not seen yet".

### What the shape needs

Four things are present in the reproduction:

1. `loading.js` on a segment (the `<Suspense>` it creates) — see the caveat above.
2. The page sits one segment **below** that boundary (`(app)/loading.jsx` + `(app)/decks/page.jsx`).
3. The layout at that boundary is `async` and awaits on every request, so a `RefreshAll`
   re-suspends the layout too.
4. The Server Action writes a cookie **and** calls `revalidatePath` (either alone is enough to
   put Next on the `RefreshAll` path, via `isCookieRevalidated` in
   `server/app-render/action-handler.js`).

Also required: a **production build**. `next dev` never reproduced it here.

I first tried the obvious minimal shape — page directly in the boundary's own segment, plain
synchronous layout — and got **0 / 24 on 16.2.6** across four variations (plain click; a
concurrent navigation; an 800ms server delay; a 200-row payload of client components). Adding
(2) and (3) produced 5 / 24 immediately, with the lane signature above. **I changed those two
together, so I have not isolated which of them matters** — only that the naive shape did not
reproduce and this one does. `run-ablations.sh` in the repo separates them.

### Additional context

This came out of a real app where the same lane signature shows up at 23.1% on 16.2.6 and 2.6%
on 16.3.4 (n = 117 each), so the reduction is not an artifact of the reduction itself.

Every probe run asks the server which Next version answered it (`/api/version`) and fails if
that disagrees with the version under test. That check is in the repo because it caught a real
error in my own measurements: with Playwright's `reuseExistingServer` enabled, a killed server
outlived the port check on a loaded machine, and a whole batch got measured against the previous
version under the new label.

Related: #86151 / #95391 (fixed the bulk of this), #84299, #86055, #97036, #96233.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/dennisat/nextjs-call-stack-size-exceeded-2026-09 ### To Reproduce ```bash pnpm install ./repro.sh deep # cold start, request /deep/a/b/c/d/e/f/g (8 segments) first ./repro.sh shallow # cold start, request /shallow/a/b/c/d/e/f (7 segments) first ``` The app is a bare `create-next-app` with `cacheComponents: true`, a root layout that wraps `children` in a trivial `"use client"` pass-through component, and two pages that return `

ok

`: one at 8 URL segments, one at 7. ### Current vs. Expected behavior `./repro.sh deep` (Node 20.16.0): ``` first /deep/a/b/c/d/e/f/g -> 500 RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded second /deep/a/b/c/d/e/f/g -> 500 third /shallow/a/b/c/d/e/f -> 200 fourth /deep/a/b/c/d/e/f/g -> 200 ← works as soon as any shallower route has compiled ``` `./repro.sh shallow`: `200 200`. The 8-segment route never fails if a shallower route compiled first, and any HMR recompile also "fixes" it for the rest of the process. `rm -rf .next` brings it back on the next cold start. Expected: 200 on every request. Bisect (each row is one cold start requesting the 8-segment route first): | Variant | Codes | Reproduces | |--------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|------------| | `cacheComponents: true`, Turbopack, Node 20.16 (as committed) | 500 500 200 200 | yes | | `cacheComponents` removed | 200 200 200 200 | no | | `next dev --webpack` | 500 200 200 200 | yes (2nd request already heals) | | Deep route with 7 segments | 200 200 200 200 | no | | Deep route with 8 segments, other folder names | 500 500 200 200 | yes | | Deep route with 9, 10 or 12 segments | 200 200 200 200 | no | | `next@canary` (16.4.0-canary.23) | 500 500 200 200 | yes | | Node 22.22.2 / 22.5.1 | 200 200 200 200 | no | | `next build && next start` | 200 | no | | No `"use client"` component in the tree | 200 200 200 200 | no | | Client component rendered by the page instead of the layout | 500 500 200 500 | yes, and never heals | Notes: - Dev only. `next build && next start` prerenders and serves the route fine. - Page content is irrelevant (`

ok

`, no imports). Static folders, no dynamic segments, no nested layouts. - Exactly 8 segments: 7 passes, 9 and deeper pass too, so this is not plain per-segment stack growth. - The terminal only prints `at ignore-listed frames`; `stack.txt` in the repo has the 50 frames from the error page. The overflow lands in React Flight `requireModule` (loading the client reference) called from Fizz `getComponentNameFromType`, under a deep `retryNode / renderNodeDestructive / renderElement / finishFunctionComponent` recursion: ``` RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at requireModule (next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-page-turbo.runtime.dev.js) at initializeModuleChunk at readChunk at getComponentNameFromType at retryNode at renderNodeDestructive at renderNode at renderChildrenArray at retryNode at renderElement ... (retryNode / renderNodeDestructive / renderElement / finishFunctionComponent repeating) ``` - Workaround: request any route with ≤ 7 segments first (or trigger any HMR recompile), or use Node 22. `--stack-size` is not applicable: Node rejects it in `NODE_OPTIONS`, which is how `next dev` passes flags to its render server. ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0 (macOS 26.6.2) Available memory (MB): 65536 Available CPU cores: 10 Binaries: Node: 20.16.0 npm: 10.8.1 Yarn: 1.22.22 pnpm: 9.9.0 Relevant Packages: next: 16.3.3 eslint-config-next: N/A react: 19.2.8 react-dom: 19.2.8 typescript: 5.9.3 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) cacheComponents, Turbopack, Partial Prerendering (PPR) ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) next dev (local) ### Additional context Also reproduced with `next@16.4.0-canary.23`. Originally hit in a real app (Next 16.3.3, `cacheComponents: true`, `proxy.ts` rewrites) with a 27-cold-start bisect showing the same pattern; the minimal repo above removes everything except the ingredients listed.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/nitipat009/next-standalone-i18next-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `git clone https://github.com/nitipat009/next-standalone-i18next-repro`
2. `cd next-standalone-i18next-repro && npm install`
3. `npm run build`
4. `ls .next/standalone/next-i18next.config.js` — file is missing
5. `node .next/standalone/server.js` then `curl http://localhost:3000/` — returns 500

### Current vs. Expected behavior

With `output: "standalone"` and next-i18next's standard setup (`appWithTranslation` in `_app`, `serverSideTranslations` in a page's `getServerSideProps`), I expected `next-i18next.config.js` to be copied into `.next/standalone/` as it is on `next@16.2.12`. Instead, on `next@16.3.0` and later it is missing, and the standalone server throws `Error: next-i18next was unable to find a user config at /app/next-i18next.config.js` on any request.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/danielcizin/next-16-3-route-handler-memory-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install && node gen.mjs` (writes 50 trivial `app/p*/page.tsx` and 34 trivial `app/api/h*/route.ts`; TypeScript 5 is pinned).
2. `node drive.mjs pages-first` — fresh `.next`, starts `next dev`, GETs every page, then GETs every route handler, printing the dev server's RSS (the process listening on the port) every 10 routes.
3. `node drive.mjs handlers-first` — the same with the handlers requested before the pages.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current (`next@16.3.4`, also `16.3.5`): after the 50 pages are compiled (~11 MB each, RSS 1.1 GB), each route handler compiled afterwards adds ~820 MB — RSS goes 1.1 → 9.2 → 17.4 → 25.7 → 29.0 GB across the 34 handlers, in 2.9 s. Requested before the pages, the same 34 handlers add ~9 MB each and the whole run ends at 1.4 GB.

The per-handler cost is linear in the number of pages already compiled: 10 pages → ~170 MB per handler, 25 → ~410 MB, 50 → ~820 MB. Removing the one shared import from the handlers (`HANDLER_IMPORT=0`) or from the pages (`PAGE_IMPORT=0`) changes nothing (28.9 GB / 27.2 GB).

Expected: a route handler's compile cost independent of how many pages were compiled before it, as in `16.2.6`, where the same pages-first run ends at 2.1 GB (handlers ~9 MB each).

Bisected in the same harness (`PAGES=10 HANDLERS=34`, pages first; good ≈ 1 GB, bad ≈ 6.3 GB): `16.2.6`, `16.3.0-canary.0/.53/.80/.93/.96/.99/.100` good; **`16.3.0-canary.101` bad**; `16.3.0` bad. That canary's release notes are four Turbopack server-HMR changes: #95546, #95795, #95661, #94948.

Where it bit: a CI browser matrix whose warmup requests 52 pages and then 33 route handlers of a real app killed 7 GB and 16 GB GitHub-hosted runners the moment the handlers were requested (dev server 5.9 → 8.9 → 11.7 → 14.3 GB across three handlers); reordering the warmup to handlers-first restored a 1.4 GB run. None of `experimental.turbopackMemoryEviction: 'full'`, `turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev: false`, `turbopackSourceMaps: false`, or `devMemoryThresholdRestart: false` changed the peak.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0: Mon Apr 27 20:41:12 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.121.6~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050
  Available memory (MB): 131072
  Available CPU cores: 18
Binaries:
  Node: 26.0.0
  npm: 11.16.0
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.4
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.4
  react-dom: 19.2.4
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, Route Handlers, Performance

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

Full measurement tables (both orders, three versions, the scaling series, and the bisect) are in the reproduction's README. Measured on macOS arm64 with 128 GB RAM so the run completes; on smaller machines the process is killed once the handlers start compiling. `turbopackMemoryLimit` (accepted by the 16.2 binding) is no longer present in 16.3's binding, so there is no bound to fall back on.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/agentHits/next.js/tree/fix/seo-monolithic-head-metadata

### To Reproduce

1. Deploy or run an App Router page with asynchronous metadata streaming in Edge SSR runtime.
2. Send an HTTP request with User-Agent `TelegramBot (like TwitterBot)`, `ChatGPT-User`, `GPTBot`, or `ClaudeBot`.
3. Read the initial HTML chunk received before the full response streams.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

- **Current:** Metadata tags (`<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, OpenGraph tags) stream in subsequent Suspense chunks. Because HTML-limited bots close the socket after the first chunk, social cards in Telegram and indexing in AI crawlers show empty/missing metadata.
- **Expected:** Next.js should recognize these user agents and emit a synchronous, monolithic `<head>` with all metadata prior to the closing `</head>` tag.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 24.2.0
Binaries:
  Node: 24.21.0
  pnpm: 10.33.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0-canary.32
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

App Router, Edge Runtime (SSR)

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (production mode)

### Additional context

Fix verified with failing/passing test in `test/e2e/app-dir/metadata-streaming/metadata-streaming.test.ts` and `test/unit/is-bot.test.ts`.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/Aabshir/next-refresh-query-repro

### To Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Aabshir/next-refresh-query-repro
cd next-refresh-query-repro
npm install
npm run build
npm start   # production build required; next dev does not exercise the cached path
```

The page renders a `#stamp` timestamp (`export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`) and a button that POSTs a mutation and then calls `router.refresh()`. The page deliberately streams (a ~12 KB filler block + a Suspense chunk that resolves after 300 ms) so the Flight response arrives in multiple chunks.

1. Open `/` (no query string), click **Mutate + refresh** several times.
2. Open `/?status=draft` (any query string; the page never reads `searchParams`), click **Mutate + refresh** several times.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Expected: the stamp updates on every click in both cases — `router.refresh()` should always discard the client cache and re-render the current URL from the server.

Actual (see version matrix below): on most Next 16 versions the stamp **never updates**. CDP network capture shows that after the mutation POST, **no `_rsc` fetch is initiated at all** for the refresh — the router silently keeps/reapplies its stale cached payload. In a real application the symptom is: the mutation persists server-side, the UI shows pre-mutation data indefinitely, and only a hard reload fixes it.

### Version matrix (same repro, production build, automated browser, 3–6 rounds per cell)

| Version | `/` (no query) | `/?status=draft` |
|---|---|---|
| 16.1.7 | ❌ stale | ❌ stale |
| **16.2.12** | ✅ fresh every time | ❌ stale every time |
| 16.3.5 (latest stable at time of writing) | ❌ stale | ❌ stale |
| 16.4.0-canary.37 (latest canary at time of writing) | ❌ stale | ❌ stale |

16.2.12 is the only tested version where refresh works at all on this page, and there the **query string alone** is the trigger: same page, same build, refresh works on `/` and never works on `/?status=draft`.

### Additional context

- Re-file of #99026 / #99027 (auto-closed by the reproduction-link validator; the repro is now a public repository containing only the minimal app).
- **Streaming is load-bearing.** If the page is shrunk (remove the filler block, shorten the Suspense chunk so the Flight response is small/fast), the same build starts passing even with a query string. The defect appears tied to the refresh committing (or failing to commit) while the response is still streaming.
- PR #94144 ("Incorrect search params stored in cache", shipped in 16.3.0-canary.31+) is present in 16.3.5 / 16.4.0-canary.37 and does **not** fix this. Possibly related to the still-open #92152 family (segment-cache keying on rendered search vs canonical URL).
- `experimental.staleTimes` makes no difference (tested with `{dynamic: 0, static: 30}` and with no config at all). `app/loading.tsx` present or absent makes no difference.
- Reproduces whether the query-string URL is reached by a fresh page load or by a client-side `router.push`.
- Real-world impact: in a large app (~144 routes) on 16.2.12 the symptom appears intermittently (~50%) on list pages whose URL carries filter params (`?status=draft`, `?q=…`, date ranges): mutate → `router.refresh()` → the list keeps showing pre-mutation rows until a hard reload. Plain-path pages in the same app are reliable. This makes mutate-then-refresh flows on filtered list views silently unreliable.

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System: Windows 11 (also reproduced on Debian 12 / Docker node:24 container)
Node: 24.x
next: see matrix above
react / react-dom: 19.3.0
Config: default (no experimental flags required to reproduce)
```

### Which area(s) are affected?

Linking and Navigating (App Router client router / segment cache)

### Which stage(s) are affected?

`next start` (production build). `next dev` does not exercise the cached path.

16.2.12 is the only tested version where refresh works at all on this page, and there the **query string alone** is the trigger: same page, same build, refresh works on `/` and never works on `/?status=draft`.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/liuxiaoxuanmmj/xoxoMeridian/tree/agent_entry

### To Reproduce

### To Reproduce

**Note up front: we could not reduce this to a standalone minimal app, and we would rather say so than link a reproduction that does not reproduce.** In a minimal app with the same shape the redirect arrives as a normal error row on a *child* chunk, so the root stays `fulfilled` and the throwing branch never runs. Below are the steps that reproduce it on the app where we hit it, the instrumentation that captured the values, and the evidence for why the minimal app fails to reproduce. If a maintainer can tell us which condition makes the **root** chunk reject rather than a child, we will turn this into a minimal fixture.

#### Steps

1. Create an App Router page whose server component does async work and *then* redirects, so the redirect lands mid-stream:

   ```tsx
   // app/chat/page.tsx
   export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

   export default async function ChatIndexPage({
     searchParams,
   }: {
     searchParams?: Promise<{ auth?: string }>;
   }) {
     const user = await requirePageUser();          // auth check
     const room = await getDefaultRoomForUser(user); // DB query
     const sp = searchParams ? await searchParams : undefined;
     redirect(chatRoomRedirectPath(room.id, sp?.auth));
   }
   ```

2. Add a link to it from another page, and open that other page in `next dev`.

3. Click the link (**a soft navigation is required** — a hard load does not hit the branch).

4. The navigation itself succeeds, but an uncaught error appears in the console and the dev overlay turns red:

   ```
   Uncaught TypeError: Failed to execute 'measure' on 'Performance':
     'ChatIndexPage' cannot have a negative time stamp.
   ```

#### Capturing the values

Wrap `performance.measure` before any navigation. In our app this fired on **every** soft navigation to that route:

```tsx
// app/perf-probe.tsx
"use client";
if (typeof window !== "undefined" && !(window as any).__perfProbe) {
  (window as any).__perfProbe = true;
  const orig = Performance.prototype.measure;
  Performance.prototype.measure = function (name: string, opts?: any) {
    if (opts && typeof opts === "object" && (opts.start < 0 || opts.end < 0)) {
      console.warn("[negative measure]", name, {
        start: opts.start,
        end: opts.end,
        tooltip: opts.detail?.devtools?.tooltipText,
      });
    }
    return orig.call(this, name, opts);
  };
}
```

Rendered from `app/layout.tsx`. Output:

```
[negative measure] "ChatIndexPage" {
  start: 0,
  end: -23583.898299109307,
  tooltip: "ChatIndexPage Errored"
}
```

`end` varies per run — we observed −5207, −13228, −20220 and −23584 ms. One captured run decomposes as `debugInfo.time` **+22.5 ms**, `response._timeOrigin` **−16490.951 ms**, `end` **−16468.436**.

#### Why the minimal app does not reproduce

Same shape, minimised, returns a working redirect; the redirect is delivered as an error row on a **child** chunk, so `root.status` never becomes `"rejected"`:

```
[200] /chat?_rsc=… (text/x-component)
  b:E{"digest":"NEXT_REDIRECT;replace;/chat/room-1;307;","name":"Error",
      "stack":[["ChatIndexPage","…/app/chat/page.tsx",11,62,9,1,false]],"env":"Server"}
```

Variants tried, all giving a working redirect and **no** negative measure:

- with and without `app/chat/loading.tsx` (the Suspense boundary moves the error row from `b:` to `14:`)
- async delays before `redirect()` of 50 / 400 / 1500 / 3000 ms
- clicking `<Link href="/chat">` vs `router.push("/chat")` from a client component
- awaiting `searchParams`
- a client component mounted in the root layout that fetches on mount

Our unverified hypothesis is that the distinguishing condition is what makes the *root* chunk reject — something about the real app's deeper async tree — but we could not isolate it, so we are not claiming it as fact.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Next.js | 16.3.3 (webpack) — **also present in 16.3.5**, verified by inspecting the published bundle |
| React | 19.2.8 (bundled `react-server-dom-webpack`) |
| Browser | Chrome (any Chromium) |
| Mode | `next dev`, App Router |

### Summary

In development, when an RSC render ends with the **root chunk rejected**, the flight client flushes
component timings and calls `performance.measure` with an `end` that is **not clamped**, while `start`
**is** clamped. Because the debug-channel timings and `response._timeOrigin` are read from two different
clock frames, `end` can be a large negative number, and Chromium throws:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Failed to execute 'measure' on 'Performance': 'ChatIndexPage' cannot have a negative time stamp.
```

The throw is uncaught and crashes the dev overlay.

### Where

`node_modules/next/dist/compiled/react-server-dom-webpack/cjs/react-server-dom-webpack-client.browser.development.js`

| line | branch | `end` guarded? |
|---|---|---|
| 1332, 1385, 1432, 4037, 4197 | normal paths | ✅ `0 < endTime` / `0 <= endTime` |
| **3907** (`end` at **3909**) | **errored** | ❌ none |
| **4165** (`end` at **4167**) | **aborted** | ❌ none |

```js
performance.measure(measureName, {
  start: 0 > startTime ? 0 : startTime,   // ← clamped
  end: childrenEndTime,                   // ← passed through unclamped
  detail: { devtools: { color: "error", tooltipText: entryName + " Errored", ... } }
});
```

Call site in our repro:

```
at Performance.measure
at flushComponentPerformance (...client.browser.development.js:3907:35)
at flushComponentPerformance (...3822:27)
at flushInitialRenderPerformance (...4268:11)
```

### Root cause: two clock frames added together

Captured by wrapping `Performance.prototype.measure` on a real app:

| quantity | observed value |
|---|---|
| `debugInfo.time` sent by the server | **22.5 ms** |
| `response._timeOrigin` | **−16490.951 ms** |
| `end` handed to `performance.measure` | **−16468.436** ← sum of the two |

The client combines them at `:3551`:

```js
"number" === typeof debugInfo.time &&
  (debugInfo = { time: debugInfo.time + response._timeOrigin });
```

and `response._timeOrigin` comes from the debug channel's `:N` row at `:4507`:

```js
case 78: response._timeOrigin = +row - performance.timeOrigin;
```

The two operands are not in the same frame:

- **every** component `time` value observed on the channel fell in `[0.8, 30.2] ms` and **restarted per
  request** — i.e. it is relative to that render, not to any absolute origin;
- the `:N` row carries an absolute-anchored origin. Four responses in one page session reported
  `1790056053565.7698`, `1790056057503.2869`, `1790056057661.7197`, `1790056057701.4707` — each
  response carries its own, all **16–28 s behind** the page's `performance.timeOrigin`.

Adding a request-relative value to a page-anchored offset therefore always yields a large negative
number. Note that the other measure sites do not crash only because they are guarded — the same
negative intermediate value is produced everywhere.

### Trigger

The errored branch requires all of:

```js
isLastComponent && "rejected" === root.status && root.reason !== response._closedReason
```

So the requirement is a **soft navigation whose render rejects the root** — in practice a `redirect()`
(and any other throw) that happens *after* the RSC response has started streaming, e.g. after an auth
check and a DB query:

```tsx
// app/chat/page.tsx
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

export default async function ChatIndexPage({
  searchParams,
}: {
  searchParams?: Promise<{ auth?: string }>;
}) {
  const user = await requirePageUser();
  const room = await getDefaultRoomForUser(user);   // async work → redirect lands mid-stream
  const sp = searchParams ? await searchParams : undefined;
  redirect(chatRoomRedirectPath(room.id, sp?.auth));
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `next dev` on an app containing the page above, and a link to it.
2. Open any authenticated page in the browser.
3. Click the link to the redirecting route.
4. The navigation succeeds, but an uncaught `TypeError` is logged and the dev overlay turns red.

### What we tried when minimising (unsuccessful — please read)

We were **not** able to reduce this to a standalone minimal app, and we would rather say so than send a
repro we cannot stand behind. In a minimal app with the same shape, the redirect is delivered as a
normal streamed error row on a **child** chunk, so the root chunk stays `fulfilled` and the errored
branch never runs:

```
[200] /chat?_rsc=… (text/x-component)
  b:E{"digest":"NEXT_REDIRECT;replace;/chat/room-1;307;","name":"Error",
      "stack":[["ChatIndexPage","…/app/chat/page.tsx",11,62,9,1,false]],"env":"Server"}
```

Variants tried, all giving a working redirect and **no** negative measure:

- with and without `app/chat/loading.tsx` (the Suspense boundary moves the error row from `b:` to `14:`);
- async delays before `redirect()` of 50 / 400 / 1500 / 3000 ms;
- clicking `<Link href="/chat">` vs `router.push("/chat")` from a client component;
- awaiting `searchParams`;
- a client component mounted in the root layout that fetches on mount.

We suspect the distinguishing condition is what makes the **root** chunk reject rather than a child, and
that it is specific to the real app's deeper async tree — but we could not isolate it. If a maintainer
can point at the condition that rejects the root, we are happy to turn this into a minimal fixture.

### Suggested fix

Clamp `end` exactly as `start` is clamped, at both unguarded sites (3909 and 4167):

```js
end: 0 > childrenEndTime ? 0 : childrenEndTime,
```

Independently, `debugInfo.time` (request-relative) and `response._timeOrigin` (page-anchored) should be
reconciled so that `time + _timeOrigin` is a valid client-relative timestamp — otherwise every measure
on the Server Components track is silently wrong, not just the two unguarded ones.

### Impact

Development only (`*.development.js`, gated on `supportsUserTiming`); production is unaffected. In dev
it produces an uncaught exception and a red error overlay, and because the throw escapes
`flushComponentPerformance` it aborts the rest of the timing flush for that response.

```bash

  Arch: x64
  Version: #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jun 18 21:54:43 UTC 2026
  Available memory (MB): 7784
  Available CPU cores: 32
Binaries:
  Node: 22.23.2

Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.3 // There is a newer version (16.3.5) available, upgrade recommended! 
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.8
  react-dom: 19.2.8
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: standalone
```

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Next.js | 16.3.3 (webpack) — **also present in 16.3.5**, verified by inspecting the published bundle |
| React | 19.2.8 (bundled `react-server-dom-webpack`) |
| Browser | Chrome (any Chromium) |

### Summary

In development, when an RSC render ends with the **root chunk rejected**, the flight client flushes
component timings and calls `performance.measure` with an `end` that is **not clamped**, while `start`
**is** clamped. Because the debug-channel timings and `response._timeOrigin` are read from two different
clock frames, `end` can be a large negative number, and Chromium throws:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Failed to execute 'measure' on 'Performance': 'ChatIndexPage' cannot have a negative time stamp.
```

The throw is uncaught and crashes the dev overlay.

### Where

`node_modules/next/dist/compiled/react-server-dom-webpack/cjs/react-server-dom-webpack-client.browser.development.js`

| line | branch | `end` guarded? |
|---|---|---|
| 1332, 1385, 1432, 4037, 4197 | normal paths | ✅ `0 < endTime` / `0 <= endTime` |
| **3907** (`end` at **3909**) | **errored** | ❌ none |
| **4165** (`end` at **4167**) | **aborted** | ❌ none |

```js
performance.measure(measureName, {
  start: 0 > startTime ? 0 : startTime,   // ← clamped
  end: childrenEndTime,                   // ← passed through unclamped
  detail: { devtools: { color: "error", tooltipText: entryName + " Errored", ... } }
});
```

Call site in our repro:

```
at Performance.measure
at flushComponentPerformance (...client.browser.development.js:3907:35)
at flushComponentPerformance (...3822:27)
at flushInitialRenderPerformance (...4268:11)
```

### Root cause: two clock frames added together

Captured by wrapping `Performance.prototype.measure` on a real app:

| quantity | observed value |
|---|---|
| `debugInfo.time` sent by the server | **22.5 ms** |
| `response._timeOrigin` | **−16490.951 ms** |
| `end` handed to `performance.measure` | **−16468.436** ← sum of the two |

The client combines them at `:3551`:

```js
"number" === typeof debugInfo.time &&
  (debugInfo = { time: debugInfo.time + response._timeOrigin });
```

and `response._timeOrigin` comes from the debug channel's `:N` row at `:4507`:

```js
case 78: response._timeOrigin = +row - performance.timeOrigin;
```

The two operands are not in the same frame:

- **every** component `time` value observed on the channel fell in `[0.8, 30.2] ms` and **restarted per
  request** — i.e. it is relative to that render, not to any absolute origin;
- the `:N` row carries an absolute-anchored origin. Four responses in one page session reported
  `1790056053565.7698`, `1790056057503.2869`, `1790056057661.7197`, `1790056057701.4707` — each
  response carries its own, all **16–28 s behind** the page's `performance.timeOrigin`.

Adding a request-relative value to a page-anchored offset therefore always yields a large negative
number. Note that the other measure sites do not crash only because they are guarded — the same
negative intermediate value is produced everywhere.

### Trigger

The errored branch requires all of:

```js
isLastComponent && "rejected" === root.status && root.reason !== response._closedReason
```

So the requirement is a **soft navigation whose render rejects the root** — in practice a `redirect()`
(and any other throw) that happens *after* the RSC response has started streaming, e.g. after an auth
check and a DB query:

```tsx
// app/chat/page.tsx
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

export default async function ChatIndexPage({
  searchParams,
}: {
  searchParams?: Promise<{ auth?: string }>;
}) {
  const user = await requirePageUser();
  const room = await getDefaultRoomForUser(user);   // async work → redirect lands mid-stream
  const sp = searchParams ? await searchParams : undefined;
  redirect(chatRoomRedirectPath(room.id, sp?.auth));
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `next dev` on an app containing the page above, and a link to it.
2. Open any authenticated page in the browser.
3. Click the link to the redirecting route.
4. The navigation succeeds, but an uncaught `TypeError` is logged and the dev overlay turns red.

### What we tried when minimising (unsuccessful — please read)

We were **not** able to reduce this to a standalone minimal app, and we would rather say so than send a
repro we cannot stand behind. In a minimal app with the same shape, the redirect is delivered as a
normal streamed error row on a **child** chunk, so the root chunk stays `fulfilled` and the errored
branch never runs:

```
[200] /chat?_rsc=… (text/x-component)
  b:E{"digest":"NEXT_REDIRECT;replace;/chat/room-1;307;","name":"Error",
      "stack":[["ChatIndexPage","…/app/chat/page.tsx",11,62,9,1,false]],"env":"Server"}
```

Variants tried, all giving a working redirect and **no** negative measure:

- with and without `app/chat/loading.tsx` (the Suspense boundary moves the error row from `b:` to `14:`);
- async delays before `redirect()` of 50 / 400 / 1500 / 3000 ms;
- clicking `<Link href="/chat">` vs `router.push("/chat")` from a client component;
- awaiting `searchParams`;
- a client component mounted in the root layout that fetches on mount.

We suspect the distinguishing condition is what makes the **root** chunk reject rather than a child, and
that it is specific to the real app's deeper async tree — but we could not isolate it. If a maintainer
can point at the condition that rejects the root, we are happy to turn this into a minimal fixture.

### Suggested fix

Clamp `end` exactly as `start` is clamped, at both unguarded sites (3909 and 4167):

```js
end: 0 > childrenEndTime ? 0 : childrenEndTime,
```

Independently, `debugInfo.time` (request-relative) and `response._timeOrigin` (page-anchored) should be
reconciled so that `time + _timeOrigin` is a valid client-relative timestamp — otherwise every measure
on the Server Components track is silently wrong, not just the two unguarded ones.

### Impact

Development only (`*.development.js`, gated on `supportsUserTiming`); production is unaffected. In dev
it produces an uncaught exception and a red error overlay, and because the throw escapes
`flushComponentPerformance` it aborts the rest of the timing flush for that response.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/lencioni/next-realm-leak-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm test`

This builds a one-page app and runs 12 identical Jest test files in one process. Each file starts a production server through the [custom server](https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/custom-server) API (`next({ dev: false })`, `prepare()`, one request, `close()`). Jest runs each test file in its own realm (a `vm` context with its own module registry), so each file loads a fresh copy of Next. A small Jest environment reports after each file:

```
[after test file 1] heap after GC: 35 MB | crypto.randomUUID wrappers: 1 | …
[after test file 2] heap after GC: 43 MB | crypto.randomUUID wrappers: 2 | …
...
[after test file 12] heap after GC: 119 MB | crypto.randomUUID wrappers: 12 | …
```


### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** every time the server starts, `node-environment-extensions/web-crypto.js` and `node-crypto.js` wrap:

- `crypto.getRandomValues` and `crypto.randomUUID`
- `randomUUID`, `randomBytes`, `randomFillSync`, `randomInt` and the `generate*Sync` functions on `require('node:crypto')`

Those objects are shared by every realm in the process, and neither module checks whether it has already wrapped them. So each realm's wrapper calls the previous realm's, and the chain keeps every realm that ever started Next alive: about 7.7 MB per realm here, and around 80 MB per test file in our app's suite.

`fast-set-immediate.external.js` has a milder version of this. It keeps its originals on `globalThis` (per realm) and replaces `setImmediate`/`clearImmediate` on the shared `node:timers`. That doesn't chain, but it leaves the most recent realm's functions on a module that outlives the realm.

**Expected:** starting Next in another realm doesn't add another wrapper to the shared functions or keep earlier realms alive.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0
  Available memory (MB): 24576
  Available CPU cores: 8
Binaries:
  Node: 22.20.0
  npm: 10.9.3
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 10.33.2
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.4 (also reproduced on 16.4.0-canary.47)
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.7
  react-dom: 19.2.7
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Runtime

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Other (Deployed), next start (local)

### Additional context

This reproduces with a plain Jest config; it doesn't need `next/jest` or Jest's ESM mode. `npm run test:workaround` puts back the replaced functions after each file, and the heap then stays at roughly 47–71 MB.

**Possible fix:** keep the "already wrapped" state on the patched object instead of in module scope or on `globalThis`. For example:

- tag each wrapper with a `Symbol.for('next.…')` property and skip wrapping if the current function already has it; or
- store the unwrapped original on the shared object and always wrap that, so a second install replaces the wrapper instead of stacking on it.

I'm happy to open a PR if either approach sounds right.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/franknoel/next-notfound-ssr

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction and run `npm install`.
2. Run `npm run build && npm run start` (`npm run dev` shows the same thing).
3. Run `./check.sh`, or fetch the pages by hand:

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:3000/missing        # page that calls notFound()
curl -s http://localhost:3000/no/such/route  # URL that matches no route
```

The app has three files: a root layout with `<html lang="en">`, an `app/not-found.tsx` that renders `NOT FOUND BOUNDARY`, and `app/[slug]/page.tsx`, which calls `notFound()` unless the slug is `known`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `/missing` answers 404, but its HTML is `<html id="__next_error__"><head></head><body>` plus scripts. The root layout does not render, so there is no `lang` and none of the `not-found.tsx` markup. That markup exists only in the RSC payload, so the page is blank until it hydrates, and stays blank without JavaScript.

An unmatched URL (`/no/such/route`) is fine: it renders `not-found.tsx` inside the root layout.

`check.sh` output, the same on 16.3.6 and 16.4.0-canary.48, in `next dev` and in `next build && next start`:

```
/known           200  <html lang="en">             boundary/page text in HTML: yes
/missing         404  <html id="__next_error__">   boundary/page text in HTML: no
/no/such/route   404  <html lang="en">             boundary/page text in HTML: yes
```

**Expected:** `/missing` renders like `/no/such/route`: the root layout with `NOT FOUND BOUNDARY` in the server HTML, and the same 404 status.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0: Tue Aug 18 17:49:13 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.161.15.700.19~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 10
Binaries:
  Node: 24.21.0
  npm: 11.19.0
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 9.15.9
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.6 // Latest available version is detected (16.3.6).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.8
  react-dom: 19.2.8
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Not Found, Error Handling

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next build (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Also reproduces on `next@16.4.0-canary.48`, dev and prod.

Same bug as #98295 and #98954, which were closed automatically for lacking a reproduction link.

Where it seems to happen: `HTTPAccessFallbackBoundary` is a client error boundary, and React does not run error boundaries during server rendering, so the `notFound()` throw escapes the Fizz shell. The catch in `app-render` (`renderToStream`, and `prerenderToStream` for ISR) sets the 404 status and renders `getErrorRSCPayload`, whose seed is the hardcoded `__next_error__` document. Because the status and the empty document come from the same catch, an app cannot get a 404 with real HTML from `notFound()`.

We hit it on a site with locale-prefixed routes: every unknown page and event URL is served without `lang` or any text.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/nigeljones84/next-image-cancel-strand-repro

### To Reproduce

Follow the README in the linked repository. It installs next@15.5.25, builds with next build, starts with next start, then requests a local image through /_next/image and cancels the request straight away. After that, every later request for that same image URL hangs until the server is restarted.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: after one cancelled request, that image URL hangs forever (6 of 6 tries on next@15.5.25). Other image sizes still load fine.

Expected: the image keeps loading normally after a cancelled request. This is already fixed on canary by #98168 (0 of 6 tries hung on 16.4.0-canary.48), but the fix is not in any stable release yet.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System: Windows 11 (win32 x64)
Node: 24.18.0
next: 15.5.25
react / react-dom: 18.3.1
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Image (next/image)

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local)

### Additional context

This replaces #99281, which was closed automatically because it had no reproduction link. I am happy to test a 15.5.x build with the fix.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/stefanprobst/next-turbopack-loader-stale-source-repro

### To Reproduce

pnpm install
node repro.mjs          # edit styles/index.css, turbopack
node repro.mjs --txt    # edit app/message.txt, turbopack
node repro.mjs --webpack
node repro.mjs --webpack --txt


see https://github.com/stefanprobst/next-turbopack-loader-stale-source-repro/blob/main/README.md

### Current vs. Expected behavior

In `next dev` with Turbopack, editing a file that goes through a loader (configured in `turbopack.rules`) runs the loader chain **twice**. The first call gets the file's **previous** content, although the file on disk already has the new content. The second call gets the current content. `next dev --webpack` runs the loader once, with the current content.

The final output is correct as long as the loader only looks at the `source` it's given. Loaders that also read the file system see a disk state that doesn't match their input. A loader that caches by the file's mtime (as `@tailwindcss/turbopack` does) rebuilds its cache from the stale content in the first call, sees an unchanged mtime in the second call, and reuses the stale result. The served output then always lags one edit behind.

This looks like the same underlying problem as #93052, which describes it for the built-in PostCSS transform and only when a PostCSS plugin reports a dependency. This repro shows it's broader:

- it happens for any loader in `turbopack.rules`, not just PostCSS;
- the loader here reports no dependencies;
- it's not CSS-specific: a `*.txt` file loaded `as: "*.js"` behaves the same.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/JesperCph/next-parallel-route-refresh-repro

### To Reproduce

###
1. Install dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
2. For the verified canary version, run `pnpm add next@16.4.0-canary.51 --save-exact`.
3. Start with `pnpm dev` and open http://127.0.0.1:4199/home.
4. Choose **Start grouped example**.
5. Open **Edit Dialog**, click **Mutate**, then **Close dialog**.
6. Soft-navigate to **About Page**.
7. Open **Edit Dialog** again, then click **Router Refresh**.
8. Repeat with **Start flat example** as the control.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

- **Expected**: About remains visible behind the dialog; refreshing does not replace the browser document.
- **Grouped example**: a full-document navigation occurs, About disappears, and the displayed performance.timeOrigin changes.
- **Flat example**: About and the existing document are preserved.
- **Additional control**: skipping the navigation from Home to About avoids the failure in both examples.

### Provide environment information

```bash

  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0: Fri Jul 31 19:19:08 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.161.14~5/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050

  typescript: 7.0.2

  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Parallel & Intercepting Routes

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

### Important reproduction details
- Both examples share the same page component, dialogs, Server Action and navigation sequence.
- The grouped pages have a (site) ancestor; the flat pages do not.
- (site) contains neither a layout nor a default.
- One root layout; defaults exist for both root slots.
- Plain parallel routes—not intercepting routes.
- No authentication, database or external services.
- Reproduced on **16.3.7** and **16.4.0-canary.51**.

### Suspected mechanism
- The grouped ancestor appears to retain /grouped-home as its refresh URL after navigation to /grouped-about.
- Opening the dialog propagates that stale URL to the retained background.
- Refresh then requests the previous background and reaches a hard-navigation fallback.
- This is the suspected explanation—not a claim that all route groups are affected.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/chirag-soni23/next-turbopack-reproduction.git

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the linked reproduction repository.
2. Install the dependencies with `npm install`.
3. Start the development server with `npm run dev`.
4. Open the application in Google Chrome.
5. Open the application in a new tab/private window.
6. On the first load, click a navigation link such as `/about` or `/contact`.
7. Observe that the first navigation does not behave normally and the destination page needs to load before navigation works normally.
8. After reloading the page once, navigation works normally.
9. Stop the development server.
10. Start the application using `next dev --webpack`.
11. Repeat the same steps. The issue does not reproduce with Webpack.
12. Also run `npm run build` followed by `npm start`. The issue does not reproduce in production mode.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Current behavior

When running the application with `next dev` using the default Turbopack development server, the first navigation after opening the application in a new Chrome tab does not work normally.

The first navigation may require the destination page to load before it becomes responsive/navigates normally.

After the page has been loaded once, subsequent navigation works normally.

I also see the following development console message:

```text
WebSocket connection to 'ws://localhost:3000/_next/hmr?...' failed:
WebSocket is closed before the connection is established

### Provide environment information

```bash
npx --no-install next info
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/heecheon92/nextjs-redirect-bug/tree/9b397509ac86f03e2557d916ca6482d4e1010851

### To Reproduce

Original reporter’s reproduction instructions from #76308:

> 1. start the dev server and then visit localhost:3000
> 2. click "Enter the evil loop"
> 3. Enjoy the infinite redirect

Assistant-assisted verification:

1. Clone the linked repository and check out commit `9b397509ac86f03e2557d916ca6482d4e1010851`. This commit already includes `return response` in `middleware.ts`.
2. Run `npm ci` and `npm run dev` (original Next 15.1.7).
3. Open `/` and click **Enter the evil loop**. Observe blank `/test/1/1` and repeated `/test/1/1?_rsc=...` requests. Navigate to `about:blank` to stop the loop.
4. Directly opening `/test/1/1` succeeds.
5. Stop dev, run `npm run build` followed by `npm run start`, and repeat the link click: production also loops.

Current canary in an independent copy:

```sh
npm install --save-exact next@16.4.0-canary.57 eslint-config-next@16.4.0-canary.57
npx next dev --turbopack
# Or: npx next dev --webpack
# Production: npx next build --turbopack && npx next start
# Or: npx next build --webpack && npx next start
```

Next 16 is invoked directly because the reproduction’s dev script first invokes the removed `next lint` command. Application and middleware source were unchanged.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** Redirect once from `/test` to `/test/1/1`, then render `You made to the second level`.

**Current:** Link navigation changes the URL to `/test/1/1`, but the page remains blank and repeatedly requests its RSC payload. Direct destination navigation succeeds.

Production network evidence from assistant-assisted verification:

```text
GET /test?_rsc=... -> HTTP 200; x-current-path: /test
RSC digest: NEXT_REDIRECT;replace;/test/1/1;307;

GET /test/1/1?_rsc=... -> HTTP 200; x-current-path: /test/1/1
RSC includes: You made to the second level
```

The target request repeats despite its expected page content and applied header. This is a client-navigation loop, not successive HTTP 307 responses. The layout logs the initial empty slugs once during link navigation; direct destination navigation logs both slugs as `1`.

Follow-up to locked #76308. The [closing explanation](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/76308#issuecomment-5482706106) attributes the problem to missing `return response`. However, [HEAD](https://github.com/heecheon92/nextjs-redirect-bug/commit/9b397509ac86f03e2557d916ca6482d4e1010851) already returns the response.

| 16.4.0-canary.57 | webpack | Loop | Loop | Works |

Builds succeeded; the failure is navigation in the running application. Observations were limited to approximately 30 destination requests to avoid leaving loops running.

The previous commit without `return` (`6b7e4cd1706ea253e228cfe38cf263f4cc4a497b`) also fails on direct destination navigation with `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`. The return fixes that missing-header/direct-load problem, but the link-navigation loop remains.

A retained shared-layout redirect result during client navigation is a hypothesis consistent with these observations, not a confirmed internal cause or proposed patch. Testing was local dev/production; no deployment behavior is claimed.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/kristoferma/turbopack-stale-cache-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Generate the app and install (see README): 100 App Router routes × 20 components; every component imports from `fake-macro`, which a Babel webpack loader expands via `turbopack.rules` + `condition.content`. `reactCompiler` + `experimental.turbopackRustReactCompiler` are on.
2. `LOADER=off next build` from an empty `.next` (cold, no loader rule).
3. `LOADER=on next build`, keeping `.next/cache` from step 2 (the loader rule is added, so every module's transform changes).
4. `LOADER=on next build` from an empty `.next` (cold, same pipeline as step 3).

Each build runs in its own `node:24-bookworm` container with `--memory=7g`; peak memory is the container's cgroup `memory.peak`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Building over the cache from a different pipeline (step 3) costs more than building with no cache at all (step 4). Two rounds each, 2,000 components:

| | Compile, cold → over old cache | Peak memory, cold → over old cache | Turbopack cache, cold → over old cache |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16.3.6 | 7.0 / 6.6 s → **11.0 / 9.2 s** | 5.16 / 5.39 → **5.41 / 5.86 GiB** | 87 → **143 MB** |
| 16.4.0-canary.57 | 7.3 / 6.4 s → **19.8 / 17.5 s** | 6.46 / 6.44 → **6.73 / 6.87 GiB** | 73 → **90 MB** |
| 16.4.0-canary.57 + `turbopackGc: true` | 6.5 / 6.5 s → **17.3 / 17.9 s** | 6.45 / 6.00 → **6.65 / 6.71 GiB** | 72 → **71 MB** |

On a real app (~1,000 modules, a Babel loader on ~265 of them), the same transition on 16.3.6 took 69 s to compile versus 29–38 s cold, spent 3.1 min in "Finished writing to filesystem cache", and grew the cache from 0.8 to 1.7 GB. On Vercel's 8 GB Standard build machine it runs out of memory (7.62 GiB when killed), while a cold build of the same commit fits (≈7.07 GiB).

**Expected:** when a pipeline change invalidates (nearly) the whole graph, a warm build should cost no more than a cold one — e.g. detect a mass invalidation and fall back to a cold start, the way a `next` version change already invalidates the whole cache. `turbopackGc` removes the stale entries afterwards but does not reduce the build's time or peak.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/kristoferma/turbopack-swc-plugin-order-repro ### To Reproduce 1. `npm install` 2. `REACT_COMPILER=0 npx next build`, then `grep -rhoE 'message:"[^"]*"' .next/static .next/server | sort -u` 3. `rm -rf .next && REACT_COMPILER=1 npx next build`, then the same grep The app has one client component with `` from `@lingui/react/macro`, compiled by `@lingui/swc-plugin` 6.6.0 through `experimental.swcPlugins` (`descriptorFields: 'all'` keeps the message text in the output). `REACT_COMPILER=1` sets `reactCompiler: true` and `experimental.turbopackRustReactCompiler: true`. ### Current vs. Expected behavior ```tsx An asterisk matches any characters.
For example s*n matches sun and season. ``` | | Message the plugin emits | |---|---| | React Compiler off | `An asterisk matches any characters.<0/>For example <1>s*n matches sun and season.` | | React Compiler on | `An asterisk matches any characters.{t2}For example <0>s*n matches sun and season.` | With the compiler on, the static `
` has already been hoisted into a memoized temporary (`t2`) when the plugin runs, so it becomes a variable placeholder and the remaining tags are renumbered. Message extraction (`lingui extract`) reads the source, so the catalog holds the first form; the compiled id matches nothing and the UI silently falls back to the source language. Which `` break depends on how the compiler splits the JSX (a child that depends on props, like `{name}`, is not hoisted and stays correct). **Expected:** a way to run SWC plugins that expand macros on the original source, before the React Compiler. In `turbopack/crates/turbopack/src/module_options/mod.rs`, `ReactCompilerRust` is appended to `ecma_preprocess` ("needs original source text"), while `swcPlugins` register at `EcmascriptTransformStage::Main`, so the compiler always runs first. Options that would fix it: - an opt-in to run `swcPlugins` in the pre-processing stage, ahead of the React Compiler; or - passing React Compiler `environment.customMacros` through from `next.config` (the Rust port has it in `environment_config.rs`), so `Trans` children are left alone. ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: linux Arch: arm64 Available memory (MB): 7838 Available CPU cores: 10 Binaries: Node: 24.21.0 npm: 11.19.0 Relevant Packages: next: 16.4.0-canary.57 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.0-canary.57). react: 19.3.0 react-dom: 19.3.0 typescript: 5.9.3 Next.js Config: output: N/A `@lingui/swc-plugin` 6.7.0 on the canary (6.6.0 does not load there); also reproduced on next 16.3.6 with plugin 6.6.0. On 16.4.0-canary.57 the client chunk carries the broken `{t2}` message while the SSR chunk carries the correct `<0/>` one, so server and client disagree about the same ``. On 16.3.6 both are broken. ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Turbopack, SWC, React ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) next build (local), next dev (local), Vercel (Deployed) ### Additional context - Lingui documents the conflict ("there's currently no way to control plugin ordering… Lingui may not work correctly with the React Compiler in SWC-based setups like Next.js") and tracks it in lingui/swc-plugin#205, where the maintainer's advice is to pick two of Lingui, Next.js and the React Compiler. - The working alternative is a `turbopack.rules` webpack loader that expands the macros before the compiler. Loaders run in Node.js worker processes; on a synthetic 2,000-component app that loader setup raised the cold-build peak from 3.4 to 5.2–5.4 GiB (Linux cgroup, 16.3.6), and on a real app it was the difference between fitting and not fitting Vercel's 8 GB build machine. Swapping Babel for the Rust `@lingui/native-tools` inside the loader did not change the peak, so the cost is the loader worker pool itself — which is why a native ordering option matters.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/artola/next-css-url-asset-repro

### To Reproduce

`next.config.ts`:

```ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  turbopack: {
    rules: {
      '*.css': {
        condition: {query: /[?&]url(?=&|$)/},
        type: 'asset',
      },
    },
  },
};
```

`app/layout.tsx` (a Server Component):

```tsx
import stylesUrl from './styles.css?url';

export default function RootLayout({children}: {children: React.ReactNode}) {
  return (
    <html>
      <head>
        <link rel="stylesheet" href={stylesUrl} precedence="default" />
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

Run `next dev` or `next build`.



### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: the build fails.

```
Module not found: Can't resolve './styles.css'
css client asset is not css chunk placeable

Debug info:
- Execution of <ModuleAssetContext as AssetContext>::process_resolve_result failed
- Execution of <NextCssClientReferenceTransition as Transition>::process failed
- css client asset is not css chunk placeable
```

Expected: the rule is respected. The file is emitted unchanged and the import returns its URL. This is what already happens for:

- the same import from a `'use client'` module
- `*.svg` with `type: 'asset'` from a Server Component

`new URL('./styles.css', import.meta.url)` fails with the same error.



### Provide environment information

```text
Next.js 16.3.8 (Turbopack)

Repro: next@16.4.0-canary.57
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

CSS, Turbopack, Module Resolution

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next build (local)

### Additional context

In the RSC context, every `.css` file is routed through `NextCssClientReferenceTransition`. The match is on the file path only (`styles_rule_condition()` → `ResourcePathEndsWith(".css")`) and happens before module rules run. The transition then applies the user rule, gets an asset module, and fails because it isn't `CssChunkPlaceable`.

Possible fixes:

- skip the transition when a user rule sets a non-CSS `type`, or
- skip it when the import has a query the user's rules match on (e.g. `?url`).

Related: #88788, which added `rules.*.type`.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/onyxdevs/next-react-482-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install && npm run build && npm start`, open http://localhost:4390
2. The counter climbs: a client component calls a server action every 100ms and each takes ~200ms, so one is always in flight. Any app with a polling or autosave server action is in this state most of the time.
3. Click **Throw during render**. It mounts a component that throws.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current (16.3.8):** `error.js` never renders. The page freezes (no commit at all; the counter stops) for ~6 seconds, then the console shows `Minified React error #482` ("An unknown Component is an async Client Component…") thrown from `trackUsedThenable` ← `use` ← `useActionQueue` ← `Router`, and the whole page is replaced by "This page couldn't load". 2 of 2 runs.

**Expected:** `error.js` renders the error, as it does on `16.4.0-canary.58` (2 of 2 runs, same app).

The #482 message is misleading here: there is no async Client Component. React's shell-suspend guard fires because error recovery keeps retrying.

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.1.119-1 (2024-11-22)
Binaries:
  Node: 22.23.1
  npm: 10.9.8
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.8 // Latest available version is detected (16.3.8).
  react: 19.2.5
  react-dom: 19.2.5
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

React, Server Actions, Error Handling

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next start (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

**Cause.** `useActionQueue` reads the router state with `use()` while an action is in flight, and nothing above `Router` is a Suspense boundary. When a render errors, React retries all pending lanes synchronously before committing the error boundary (`recoverFromConcurrentError`). The retry suspends in the shell on the in-flight action. The React bundled with 16.3.x (`19.3.0-canary-cbb046ab-20260731`) then leaves error recovery enabled, so the boundary never commits. Each new server action dispatch re-renders, errors, retries and suspends again, until `shellSuspendCounter > 100` throws #482.

**Already fixed upstream.** This is react/react#37739 (merged 2026-10-02; a regression from react/react#36911, which is in the 16.3.x React build). It reached canary via #99600 (`16.4.0-canary.58`). We confirmed it in isolation: the same harness against the React compiled into 16.3.6/16.3.8 throws #482 (production and development builds), and the same build with only #37739's change applied commits the error boundary.

**Ask.** Could #99600's React bump, or #37739 alone, be backported to a 16.3.x patch release? Every App Router app that calls server actions on a timer is exposed, and when it happens the whole page is lost.

**Seen in production** on 16.3.6 (Sentry: #482 from `useActionQueue`, after a stream of server-action POSTs on one page). We're applying #37739 as a local patch on 16.3.6 in the meantime.

**Current (16.3.8):** `error.js` never renders. ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/a-waider/turbopack-bug-report

### To Reproduce

1. Create a new Next.js application using the App Router and Turbopack: `npx create-next-app@latest`
2. Install MapLibre and the OpenLayers integration: `npm install maplibre-gl ol @geoblocks/ol-maplibre-layer`
3. Create a client component:
```ts
"use client";

import { setWorkerUrl } from "maplibre-gl";
const workerUrl = new URL(
  "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs",
  import.meta.url,
).toString();Url);
setWorkerUrl(workerUrl);
```
4. Create a MapLibre layer: `const maplibre = new MapLibreLayer({ mapLibreOptions: { style: "https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json" } });`
5. Start the application in development mode: `npm run dev --turbopack`
6. Open the page containing the map.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

The map is not rendered and the browser console reports: `Error: Worker failed to load. Check that the worker URL is correct.`

The worker URL itself resolves correctly: `/_next/static/media/maplibre-gl-worker.28o139oay2s87.mjs`.
The worker file is available and can be opened directly in the browser.
The generated build output contains:
```js
// .next/dev/static/media/maplibre-gl-worker-dev.<hash>.mjs
import { An as addProtocol, Br as EXTENT, D as clipGeometry, Dt as RGBAImage, Et as AlphaImage, F as potpack, Fn as isAbortError, G as GeoJSONVT, H as rtlWorkerPlugin, Ir as warnOnce, Ln as JSON_PREFIX, Mn as removeProtocol, N as ImageAtlas, On as makeRequest, Tn as getJSON, Ui as Point, Vt as CollisionBoxArray, _ as createStyleLayer, bt as DEMData, c as GeoJSONWrapper, d as OverscaledTileID, dn as createExpression, dr as isImageBitmap, dt as VectorTile, en as EvaluationParameters, g as Actor, gr as isWorker, i as MLTVectorTile, l as fromVectorTileJs, ln as groupByLayout, lr as getImageData, nn as register, o as DictionaryCoder, r as FeatureIndex, rr as extend, t as BoundedLRUCache, tr as ensureError, un as featureFilter, vr as mapObject, wn as getArrayBuffer, z as PbfReader } from "./maplibre-gl-shared-dev.mjs";
```
However, MapLibre fails to initialize because the worker cannot be started successfully.
The import of `maplibre-gl-shared-dev.mjs` can't be resolved because the filename does not match the generated filename `maplibre-gl-shared-dev.<hash>.mjs`.
Here is the generated files list:
```
% ls .next/dev/static/media/ 
maplibre-gl-dev.1o5nxnkjd6cnf.mjs               maplibre-gl-worker.28o139oay2s87.mjs
maplibre-gl-shared-dev.0isji-8tw1r7q.mjs        maplibre-gl.3eba20-hz30dt.css
maplibre-gl-shared.15t8rcx3psmo2.mjs            maplibre-gl.41h92-aem65b9.mjs
maplibre-gl-worker-dev.1vot6av3b_4nr.mjs
```

The same code works outside of the Next.js/Turbopack environment. It was tested with Vite.


Additionally there is an issue when importing the workerUrl directly from the `maplibre-gl` package (`import workerUrl from 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs?worker&url';` [Maplibre docs](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js/blob/v6.0.0/docs/index.md#installation)). It directly returns the worker class instead of the workerUrl.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0: Tue Aug 11 21:20:40 PDT 2026; root:xnu-13432.1.9~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6020
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 26.10.0
  npm: 11.19.1
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 12.9.1
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0-canary.60
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, Webpack, Module Resolution

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next build (local), next start (local)

### Additional context

This issue started with the migration to `@geoblock/ol-maplibre-layer` v2.0.0 and `maplibre-gl` v6. Maplibre introduced the `setWorkerUrl` as a requirement and this fails for NextJS projects.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/skurekjakub/next-rsc-swr-skew-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`, then `./scripts/deploy.sh build-a` (runs `next build` + `next start -p 3000` with `DEPLOYMENT_ID=build-a`, passed to `deploymentId`).
2. Open `http://localhost:3000/` in Chrome, DevTools → Network open, "Disable cache" unticked.
3. Click **Go to /other** (a client navigation to an ISR page, `revalidate = 3600`).
4. Stop the server, run `./scripts/deploy.sh build-b` on the same port.
5. Open a new tab at `http://localhost:3000/` (shows build-b), click **Go to /other**, watch the Network panel.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Currently, after you do repro step 5, the response is optimistically answered from the client cache and a revalidate request sent to the backend. 

This is a problem when deploying new app versions while clients have cached resources from older builds.

In my app, there is some custom code that throws in this case, giving the user a http 500 - the cause is that some resources are fetched from the fresh deployment, while others optimistically from the cache, due to the SWR headers set by Nextjs for prerendered/cached requests (or maybe the SWR fallback is browser side, not sure). After a reload, the SWR loop correctly fetches the updated payload.

But the user experience is a confusing HTTP 500 error... on some random pages that they happen to have cached locally.

**Expected**

a client navigation never fetches RSC payload from another deployment without the server being asked. The self-hosting guide says the server compares the client's deployment id with its own but currently a browser-cache hit never reaches the server. 

If this is not a bug, I'd like some recommendations/best practices for dealing with this in deployments.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Jun  5 01:12:21 UTC 2026
  Available memory (MB): 31931
  Available CPU cores: 20
Binaries:
  Node: 24.18.0
  npm: 12.0.1
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0-canary.61 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.0-canary.61).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Linking and Navigating, Headers

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

- Self-hosted, single instance, no CDN in front, so the browser is the only cache. Same behaviour on 16.3.6.
- In a production app (16.3.6, `cacheComponents`, standalone) the mixed payload did not stop at a reload: users hit client-side crashes in our own code, e.g. a context hook throwing because it found no provider, which fits a consumer and its provider coming from two deployments' module instances. With the stale payload's chunks executing first, Turbopack's first-registration-wins module factories can leave a module from the old deployment in place for the new one. The minimal repro above only shows the chunk load and the reload; the crash depends on which modules the two builds share and how they changed.
- Related: #90622 (Flight decode runs before the build-mismatch check during rolling deploys — the same ordering is why the old chunks load here before the reload), #86554 / #88457 (`CDN-Cache-Control` split, reverted).
- Workaround we ship: a proxy (middleware) that overrides `Cache-Control` on page HTML and RSC responses with `private, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. `private, no-cache` looks equivalent but breaks 304s: Next copies proxy response headers onto the request (`server/lib/router-utils/resolve-routes.js`), and `sendEtagResponse` treats a request `no-cache` as an end-to-end reload. RSC responses carry no `ETag`, so with the workaround every client navigation refetches its payload in full.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/QuachTrienHuy1107/next-ppr-rsc-restart-repro

### To Reproduce

1. npm install
2. ./repro.sh  — builds, runs `next start`, requests the pages, restarts the server and requests them again.
   `PROBE_MEM=40000 ./repro.sh evict` shows case A via in-memory cache eviction instead of a restart.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Expected: after `next start` restarts (or an entry is evicted from the in-memory cache), pages are
read back from the disk cache, and the HTML and the RSC payload carry the same data.

Actual (next@16.4.0-canary.63, also 16.3.5 / 16.3.8):
- Case A: a page outside generateStaticParams, upgraded from the fallback shell to a static page,
  is served as the fallback shell again after a restart (x-nextjs-postponed: 1) and re-rendered.
  Its `.rsc` file is never written next to `.html`. Same after eviction.
- Case B: a prerendered page regenerated at runtime returns the regenerated data in the HTML, but
  after a restart the RSC payload (client navigation) returns the build-time data labelled HIT.

It looks like file-system-cache `set()` skips the `.rsc` file for PPR routes, while `get()`
requires it whenever `postponed == null`.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 27.0.0
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 10
Binaries:
  Node: 24.7.0
  npm: 11.5.1
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0-canary.63
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

cacheComponents, Use Cache, Partial Prerendering (PPR), Runtime

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

We self-host on a single VPS (output: 'standalone'). Every restart drops the cache of pages upgraded at runtime (most of our product pages), and client-side navigation can show outdated data (e.g. old prices) next to up-to-date HTML until the next deploy. We're running a local
patch for now, but this affects anyone self-hosting with Cache Components, so we'd really appreciate it if this could be looked at soon. Thanks!
