# Linux/X11: NVIDIA EGL 595.99.02 SIGSEGV after BAD_ALLOC with front_end = 'Software'

## What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

Linux X11 — Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (Noble), x86_64.

## Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

Regolith X11 session with i3 4.23 (`i3-wm` package `4.23-1build2`).
Regolith i3 session package: `4.11.11-1regolith-noble`.

## WezTerm version

```text
wezterm 20261010-083911-e2a98e1b
```

Installed package: `wezterm-nightly 20261010-083911-e2a98e1b`.
This occurred on a nightly build; I have not verified whether a newer nightly fixes it.

## Describe the bug

My configuration had `front_end = 'Software'` during the last three crashes. WezTerm also crashed before I enabled that setting, so selecting `Software` has not prevented the crashes.

The journal excerpts below capture two of those crashes, approximately 33 seconds apart on October 13, 2026. Both were SIGSEGVs at address `0` inside `libnvidia-eglcore.so.595.99.02`, with the same reported library offset. Immediately before each of these two crashes, WezTerm logged `window::egl > make_current failed ... MakeCurrent: BAD_ALLOC`.

The first of the two logged crashes occurred at 10:57:09 CDT. WezTerm was relaunched, and the new GUI process crashed at 10:57:42 CDT. The relaunched instance accepted requests to spawn additional terminal windows before crashing.

The configured value is known: `front_end = 'Software'`. What I do not know is how WezTerm used that setting, or why the crashed processes still reached NVIDIA EGL and logged `is_opengl: true`. The logs identify the faulting library, but do not establish whether the underlying problem is in the NVIDIA driver or WezTerm's handling of an EGL failure.

## To Reproduce

I do not yet have a deterministic reproducer or a confirmed input/action that triggers the failure.

Observed sequence:

1. Configure `front_end = 'Software'` and run WezTerm in the Regolith X11 session, launched as `/usr/bin/wezterm start` (Apport records the GUI command as `/usr/bin/wezterm-gui start`).
2. An existing GUI instance crashes with an EGL `MakeCurrent: BAD_ALLOC` error followed by SIGSEGV.
3. Relaunch WezTerm. Additional launches spawn terminal windows through the existing GUI instance.
4. The relaunched instance logs further `MakeCurrent: BAD_ALLOC` errors and crashes approximately 27 seconds after its startup warning.

I have not yet reproduced this with a minimal configuration or `--skip-config`.

## Configuration

`front_end = 'Software'` was configured during the last three crashes. Earlier crashes occurred before this setting was enabled. The current configuration is included below; I can confirm the renderer setting during those three crashes, though I have not verified that every other line of this snapshot was identical at each crash.

Despite that configured value, the captured crash logs show `is_opengl: true` and a fault inside NVIDIA EGL. I do not yet know how the setting is used internally or why this code path is reached.

<details>
<summary>Current ~/.wezterm.lua</summary>

```lua
local wezterm = require 'wezterm'

-- Keep selections highlighted; copy explicitly with Ctrl+Shift+C.
local mouse_bindings = {}
for _, mods in ipairs { 'NONE', 'SHIFT', 'ALT', 'SHIFT|ALT' } do
  for streak = 1, 3 do
    table.insert(mouse_bindings, {
      event = { Up = { streak = streak, button = 'Left' } },
      mods = mods,
      action = wezterm.action.Nop,
    })
  end
end
-- Preserve clicking links when no text has been selected.
for _, mods in ipairs { 'NONE', 'SHIFT' } do
  for _, binding in ipairs(mouse_bindings) do
    if binding.mods == mods and binding.event.Up.streak == 1 then
      binding.action = wezterm.action_callback(function(window, pane)
        if window:get_selection_text_for_pane(pane) == '' then
          window:perform_action(wezterm.action.OpenLinkAtMouseCursor, pane)
        end
      end)
    end
  end
end

## Describe the bug

My configuration had `front_end = 'Software'` during the last three crashes. WezTerm also crashed before I enabled that setting, so selecting `Software` has not prevented the crashes.

The journal excerpts below capture two of those crashes, approximately 33 seconds apart on October 13, 2026. Both were SIGSEGVs at address `0` inside `libnvidia-eglcore.so.595.99.02`, with the same reported library offset. Immediately before each of these two crashes, WezTerm logged `window::egl > make_current failed ... MakeCurrent: BAD_ALLOC`.

The first of the two logged crashes occurred at 10:57:09 CDT. WezTerm was relaunched, and the new GUI process crashed at 10:57:42 CDT. The relaunched instance accepted requests to spawn additional terminal windows before crashing.

The configured value is known: `front_end = 'Software'`. What I do not know is how WezTerm used that setting, or why the crashed processes still reached NVIDIA EGL and logged `is_opengl: true`. The logs identify the faulting library, but do not establish whether the underlying problem is in the NVIDIA driver or WezTerm's handling of an EGL failure.

### What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

Windows

### Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

_No response_

### WezTerm version

20261005-054844-37254829

### Did you try the latest nightly build to see if the issue is better (or worse!) than your current version?

No, and I'll explain why below

### Describe the bug

Two panes sit side by side, and `pane_focus_follows_mouse` is at its default of `false`. When the mouse moves over the pane that does not have focus, WezTerm looks for the hovered hyperlink in the focused pane. It uses the coordinates of the pane under the mouse to do so. As a result, the pointer turns into the hand even though the cell under the mouse holds no link.

It also works the other way round: a link in an unfocused pane never shows the hand while you hover it.

I noticed this with a Neovim pane that renders OSC 8 hyperlinks, next to another pane. The steps below show the same thing with a plain shell.

### To Reproduce

1. Split a tab into a left pane and a right pane.
2. In the left pane, print a hyperlink near the left edge, e.g. in bash:
   `printf '\e]8;;https://example.com\e\\example link\e]8;;\e\\\n'`
3. Click the left pane to focus it.
4. Move the mouse over the right pane, on the same row as the link and a few cells from the right pane's left edge.

Then click the right pane and hover the link in the left pane.

### Configuration

`pane_focus_follows_mouse` is not set. The config has `mouse_bindings` for right-click paste and Ctrl+click `OpenLinkAtMouseCursor`; these only act on clicks, not on hover.

### Expected Behavior

- Step 4: the normal pointer, because the cell under the mouse has no link. Actual: the hand pointer, as if the mouse were over the link in the left pane.
- Hovering the link in the unfocused left pane: the hand. Actual: no hand.

### Logs

_No response_

### Anything else?

**Cause.** This is in `mouse_event_terminal`: https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mouseevent.rs#L670-L715

`pane` starts as the active pane ([L63](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mouseevent.rs#L63)).

- For a `Move` over another pane, `pane` is replaced only when `pane_focus_follows_mouse` is set ([L688-L697](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mouseevent.rs#L688-L697)). Even so, `column` and `row` are converted into the hovered pane's coordinates ([L707-L708](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mouseevent.rs#L707-L708)).
- The hyperlink lookup ([L788-L813](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mouseevent.rs#L788-L813)) and the cursor ([L836-L844](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mouseevent.rs#L836-L844)) then use the active pane with those coordinates.
- The same coordinates are also sent to the active pane's program as a motion report ([L991-L1036](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/e2a98e1b8af156988ad0ac778658ac27b60a55fb/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mouseevent.rs#L991-L1036)). A program in the focused pane that tracks all motion therefore receives positions from another pane, in that pane's coordinates.

**Possible fix.** For a `Move` over a pane other than the active one:
- Do the hyperlink lookup and `set_cursor` against the pane under the mouse (`pos.pane`).
- Don't send the motion report to the active pane, unless the mouse is captured.

**Nightly.** I'm on the 20261005 nightly. Current `main` (e2a98e1b) is 4 commits ahead of it, and none of them touch `mouseevent.rs`.

body_text:
### What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

Windows

### Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

_No response_

### WezTerm version

20260828-101755-27d55bef

### Did you try the latest nightly build to see if the issue is better (or worse!) than your current version?

No

### Describe the bug

A long-running `wezterm-gui` process on Windows ends up burning a whole CPU core while completely idle. A fresh process with the **identical config** sits at 0%.

Measured on the same machine, same config file, same time:

| instance | uptime | idle CPU |
|---|---|---|
| fresh process | ~0 | **0.0% – 0.8%** of one core |
| long-running process | 1.0 h | **70% – 104%** of one core |

The spin is a single thread in the `Running` state (not blocked/waiting). In my sampling one thread accounted for ~78% of the core while all other threads were idle:

```
Tid    DeltaSec  Pct   State     WaitReason
33100     11.69   77.9  Running
36080      0.27    1.8  Wait      UserRequest
50884      0.06    0.4  Wait      Executive
```

The thread count also creeps up over time while it spins — 49 threads shortly after start, 57 threads ~12 minutes later, on a process with 5 idle tabs:

```
t+ 30s  uptime 1.03h  now 69.7%  handles 730  threads 57
t+ 60s  uptime 1.04h  now 71.5%  handles 730  threads 57
t+ 90s  uptime 1.05h  now 74.2%  handles 730  threads 57
```

Handle count is *not* growing (693 → 730 over the same window), so this does **not** look like the WebGPU Event-handle leak in #8208 — this is a busy-spin, not a leak.

### What I ruled out

All of the following were measured on this machine; none of them reproduce the spin on a fresh process:

- **Config**: a minimal config and the full real config both idle at 0%. I also A/B'd a handler that does *no* work vs. the real config — no difference.
- **Background image / animations**: no background image in config; `animation_fps = 1`, `cursor_blink_rate = 0`.
- **Frame rate / redraw activity**: running a program that repaints as fast as possible (`sys.stdout.write` + `flush` in a tight loop) does not raise a fresh instance above 0%.
- **Tab count**: 1 tab = 0%, 5 tabs = 0.1% on a fresh instance.
- **Renderer fallback**: both the healthy and the spinning process load the same driver (`nvoglv64.dll`), i.e. both are on the NVIDIA GL path. `front_end` is unset (default).
- **Mux client pileup**: `wezterm cli list-clients` shows a single client. I also hammered a fresh instance with 30 abruptly-killed `wezterm cli list` calls (to force the `wezterm_mux_server_impl::local ... os error 10054` path seen in the spinning process's log) — it stayed at 0%.

### To Reproduce

Not yet reduced to a deterministic recipe, unfortunately — a freshly started instance never spins. It appears to require the process to have been running for a while; the one I captured had been up for ~1 hour with 5 tabs, one of which runs a TUI agent.

Steps that produced the measurement above:

1. Start `wezterm-gui` normally on Windows and leave it running.
2. Sample CPU: `(Get-Process wezterm-gui).TotalProcessorTime` twice, 30 s apart.
3. Compare a long-running instance against a fresh one with the same config.

### Configuration

```
local wezterm = require 'wezterm'
local config = wezterm.config_builder()

config.color_scheme = 'OneHalfDark'
config.window_decorations = "RESIZE"
config.use_fancy_tab_bar = false
config.enable_tab_bar = true
config.hide_tab_bar_if_only_one_tab = true

config.max_fps = 30
config.animation_fps = 1
config.cursor_blink_rate = 0
config.scrollback_lines = 5000

config.font = wezterm.font("CaskaydiaCove Nerd Font")
config.font_size = 14
config.default_prog = { 'nu' }
config.exit_behavior = "Hold"

config.background = {
  {
    source = { File = "D:/data/images/meinv.png" },
    repeat_x = "NoRepeat",
    repeat_y = "NoRepeat",
    vertical_align = "Middle",
    horizontal_align = "Center",
    opacity = 1.0,
    hsb = { brightness = 0.5, saturation = 1.0, hue = 1.0 },
  },
}
```

`front_end` is not set. GPU is an NVIDIA RTX 4060 (driver 32.0.15.9579); there is also an "AskLink Display Adapter (HDR)" IDD present on the system.

### Expected Behavior

An idle `wezterm-gui` should not consume a CPU core, regardless of uptime.

### Logs

### What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

Windows

### Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

N/A (Windows 10 22H2, build 19045)

### WezTerm version

20260929-043349-cab25161

### Did you try the latest nightly build to see if the issue is better (or worse!) than your current version?

No, and I'll explain why below

### Describe the bug

With any `window_decorations` value that has no native title bar (`INTEGRATED_BUTTONS|RESIZE`, `INTEGRATED_BUTTONS`, `RESIZE`), minimizing the window (e.g. clicking the taskbar button of the focused WezTerm window) breaks the GUI:

- WebGpu with an explicit Vulkan or Dx12 adapter: panic in `Surface::configure`, process exits within ~1s.
- WebGpu with default adapter selection, and `front_end = 'OpenGL'`: the window hangs ("Not Responding") and stays hung after restoring.

`TITLE|RESIZE` minimizes and restores fine on the same machine.

**Cause:** `wm_nccalcsize` (`window/src/os/windows/window.rs`) trims `frame_x + padding` from both the left and right of the proposed client rect whenever there is no native title bar. While the window is being minimized, the proposed rect is narrower than that trim, so `left > right`. `GetClientRect` then reports a negative width (-7 here), and `rect_width(&rect) as usize` in `check_and_call_resize_if_needed` wraps it to `4294967289`, which is what reaches `Surface::configure`.

Tested on the 2026-09-29 nightly rather than the newest one, but `window.rs` has not changed on `main` since 08e50ca2 (2026-08-27), so this should still apply to the current tip.

### To Reproduce

1. Use the config below.
2. Start WezTerm and run something that keeps drawing, e.g. `powershell -Command "while(1){Get-Date; Start-Sleep -m 30}"` (an idle shell also triggers it, this just makes it immediate).
3. Click WezTerm's taskbar button to minimize it (or send `WM_SYSCOMMAND`/`SC_MINIMIZE`).

### Configuration

```lua
return {
  window_decorations = 'INTEGRATED_BUTTONS|RESIZE',
}
```

Also reproduces with `'RESIZE'` and `'INTEGRATED_BUTTONS'`, with or without `use_fancy_tab_bar`. Does not reproduce with `'TITLE|RESIZE'`.

### Expected Behavior

The window minimizes and restores normally.

### Logs

With an explicit Vulkan adapter (`webgpu_preferred_adapter`):

```
thread 'main' panicked at D:\a\wezterm\wezterm\vendor\wgpu-25.0.2\src\backend\wgpu_core.rs:3561:18:
wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
  In Surface::configure
    `Surface` width and height must be within the maximum supported texture size. Requested was (4294967289, 34), maximum extent for either dimension is 32768.

ERROR  window::os::windows::window > caught Any { .. }
```

The hang variant shows up as `AppHangB1` for `wezterm-gui.exe` in the Windows event log.

### Anything else?

GPU: NVIDIA laptop GPU with hybrid graphics, driver 595.79.

Skipping the custom frame calculation while the window is iconic fixes it for me (built on top of cab25161):

```diff
--- a/window/src/os/windows/window.rs
+++ b/window/src/os/windows/window.rs
@@ unsafe fn wm_nccalcsize(hwnd: HWND, _msg: UINT, wparam: WPARAM, lparam: LPARAM) -> Option<LRESULT> {
     if !(wparam == 1 && no_native_title_bar) {
         return None;
     }
 
+    // A minimized window's rect is smaller than the frame we trim below,
+    // which inverts it into a negative width that later wraps to ~4 billion
+    // and panics wgpu's Surface::configure. Let Windows size it instead.
+    if IsIconic(hwnd) != 0 {
+        return None;
+    }
+
     if inner.saved_placement.is_none() {
```

With the patch, minimize/restore works with `INTEGRATED_BUTTONS|RESIZE` on both WebGpu and OpenGL. Clamping `rect_width`/`rect_height` to 0 before the `as usize` casts would be a reasonable extra guard.

Related: #7819 (same `Surface::configure` panic, different trigger), #2881 (earlier minimize panic with WebGpu).

@@ unsafe fn wm_nccalcsize(hwnd: HWND, _msg: UINT, wparam: WPARAM, lparam: LPARAM) -> Option<LRESULT> {
     if !(wparam == 1 && no_native_title_bar) {
         return None;
     }
 
+    // A minimized window's rect is smaller than the frame we trim below,
+    // which inverts it into a negative width that later wraps to ~4 billion
+    // and panics wgpu's Surface::configure. Let Windows size it instead.
+    if IsIconic(hwnd) != 0 {
+        return None;
+    }
+
     if inner.saved_placement.is_none() {
```

Related: #7819 (same `Surface::configure` panic, different trigger), #2881 (earlier minimize panic with WebGpu).

### What Operating System(s) are you seeing this problem on?

Windows (11 Pro, build 26200)

### Which Wayland compositor or X11 Window manager(s) are you using?

n/a (Windows)

### WezTerm version

20260914-161409-699fd77b

### Did you try the latest nightly build to see if the issue is better (or worse!) than your current version?

Yes, and I updated the version box above to show the version of the nightly that I tried

### Describe the bug

On Windows every serial connection dies on its first read. `wezterm serial COM9 --baud 115200` opens a window that terminates immediately, and the same happens when attaching a serial domain created by `config.serial_ports` (same code path: a `LocalDomain` backed by a `SerialTty` pty). It reproduces with `wezterm -n serial COM9 --baud 115200`, i.e. with no config file at all.

```
10:50:48.211  ERROR  portable_pty::serial > serial read error: 参数错误。 (os error 87)
10:50:48.212  ERROR  mux                  > read_pty failed: pane 0 Os { code: 87, kind: InvalidInput, message: "参数错误。" }
```

`os error 87` is `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`. A second spawn attempt is sometimes logged right after the failed read, which is easy to misread while triaging:

```
10:26:53.908  ERROR  wezterm_gui > spawn: openpty on serial port "COM9": 拒绝访问。 (os error 5); terminating
```

That access-denied is **not** contention: it is a retry racing the previous (failed) pty that still holds the handle. The port is free and healthy — PowerShell `System.IO.Ports.SerialPort` opens the same COM port from another process without error (its read only times out because the device sends nothing), and other serial software works with the same device.

### To Reproduce

1. On Windows, plug any USB CDC device bound to `usbser.sys` (COM9 here).
2. `wezterm -n serial COM9 --baud 115200`
3. The window appears and closes immediately; the log shows `serial read error: ... (os error 87)`.

### Analysis: the read path, not the device

1. `serial2` 0.2.38 opens the COM handle with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` (`serial2-rs/src/sys/windows/mod.rs:88`: `.custom_flags(FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED)`) and performs its own I/O as `OVERLAPPED` transfers.
2. `pty/src/serial.rs` never uses serial2's read path: `MasterPty::try_clone_reader` duplicates the raw handle into a `filedescriptor::FileDescriptor` and reads through that, and `filedescriptor/src/windows.rs` (`impl io::Read for FileDescriptor`) does:

```rust
ReadFile(
    self.handle.as_raw_handle() as *mut _,
    buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut _,
    buf.len() as _,
    &mut num_read,
    ptr::null_mut(),   // lpOverlapped == NULL, while lpNumberOfBytesRead is non-NULL
)
```

3. `ReadFile` with `lpOverlapped = NULL` on a handle opened with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` is not allowed by the I/O manager and fails with `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` (87). Minimal reproduction that involves no serial device at all — a plain file handle on Windows 11:

```c
HANDLE h = CreateFileW(L"t.txt", GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ, NULL,
                       OPEN_EXISTING, FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, NULL);
DWORD n = 0; char buf[16];
BOOL ok = ReadFile(h, buf, 16, &n, NULL);   /* lpOverlapped == NULL */
/* ok == FALSE, GetLastError() == 87 */
```

The same file opened *without* `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` reads fine through the same call, which is why this stays hidden as long as the handle is opened synchronously.

4. `pty/src/serial.rs` has not changed since the serial2 migration (`b38b5ef3`, "Use serial2 crate instead of serial (#6411)", 2024-12-05), and current `main` reads through the same duplicated handle, so the nightly does not fix it.

Writes are unaffected (they go through serial2's own `Write` impl), so a serial pane can send but can never receive.

### Configuration

None needed — `wezterm -n serial COM9 --baud 115200` fails identically. With a config, the equivalent failure happens when attaching a domain from `config.serial_ports`.

### Expected Behavior

The serial window stays open, displays output from the device, and forwards typed keys to the port.

### Logs

```
$ wezterm -n serial COM9 --baud 115200
10:50:48.211  ERROR  portable_pty::serial > serial read error: 参数错误。 (os error 87)
10:50:48.212  ERROR  mux                  > read_pty failed: pane 0 Os { code: 87, kind: InvalidInput, message: "参数错误。" }

$ wezterm serial COM9 --baud 115200        # same, plus the retry that adds the misleading second error
10:26:53.267  ERROR  portable_pty::serial > serial read error: 参数错误。 (os error 87)
10:26:53.268  ERROR  mux                  > read_pty failed: pane 0 Os { code: 87, kind: InvalidInput, message: "参数错误。" }
10:26:53.908  ERROR  wezterm_gui          > spawn: openpty on serial port "COM9": 拒绝访问。 (os error 5); terminating
```

### Anything else?

**A fix already exists: #8223** (`fix: make filedescriptor compatible with both blocking/nonblocking handles for windows`, open, by @gwangyi) — it passes a real `OVERLAPPED` to `ReadFile` and waits with `GetOverlappedResult(..., 1)`, which is the same conclusion I arrived at independently.

I verified that patch on this machine with a minimal reproducer that uses exactly the path a serial pane takes (`serial2::SerialPort::open` → `filedescriptor::FileDescriptor::dup` → `read`), plus the other two handle kinds `filedescriptor` is used with on Windows:

| case | current `main` | #8223 applied |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serial port (handle opened by serial2 with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`), COM9 with a device attached | `Err(参数错误。 (os error 87))` | `Ok(0 bytes)` — read timeout, no data |
| synchronous pipe (`filedescriptor::Pipe::new()`, i.e. `CreatePipe`), data ready | `Ok(5) "hello"` | `Ok(5) "hello"` |
| synchronous pipe, `read()` called before the writer produces data | `Ok(5) "later"` after ~300ms | `Ok(5) "later"` after ~300ms |
| synchronous file handle at position 4 of `AAAABBBBCCCC` | `Ok(4) "BBBB"` | `Ok(4) "AAAA"` (offset ignored) |

`Ok(0)` is the important part for the serial case: `pty/src/serial.rs`'s reader treats `Ok(0)` as "read timed out, no data yet" on Windows and loops again, so the blocking semantics described in #8223 are preserved and serial panes should stop dying on their first read. The pipe rows matter because `pty/src/win/conpty.rs` builds every ConPTY pane out of `Pipe::new()`, and that path — including blocking until data arrives — is unchanged. The last row is a caveat to settle before merging #8223 (the zeroed `OVERLAPPED` makes synchronous file handles read at offset 0); details in [my comment on that PR](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/pull/8223#issuecomment-6207140101). This issue can be closed once a fix for the overlapped-handle case lands.

Reproducer used for the table above:

```rust
let mut port = serial2::SerialPort::open("COM9", 115200).unwrap();
port.set_read_timeout(Duration::from_millis(200)).unwrap();
let mut fd = filedescriptor::FileDescriptor::dup(&port).unwrap();   // what try_clone_reader does
let mut buf = [0u8; 512];
println!("{:?}", fd.read(&mut buf));   // main: Err(87); with #8223: Ok(0)
```

Possibly relevant while bisecting: before #6411 `pty/Cargo.toml` depended on `serial = "0.4"`; I could not verify how that crate opened the port, but if it opened it without `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, this would be a regression introduced by #6411 — which would also fit #6969, filed against 20240203, where Windows serial echo works but is sluggish.

Related: #6969 (wezterm serial slaggish, Windows), #7241 (warning when opening a serial port while `default_prog` is set).

`Ok(0)` is the important part for the serial case: `pty/src/serial.rs`'s reader treats `Ok(0)` as "read timed out, no data yet" on Windows and loops again, so the blocking semantics described in #8223 are preserved and serial panes should stop dying on their first read. The pipe rows matter because `pty/src/win/conpty.rs` builds every ConPTY pane out of `Pipe::new()`, and that path — including blocking until data arrives — is unchanged. The last row is a caveat to settle before merging #8223 (the zeroed `OVERLAPPED` makes synchronous file handles read at offset 0); details in [my comment on that PR](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/pull/8223#issuecomment-6207140101). This issue can be closed once a fix for the overlapped-handle case lands.

Reproducer used for the table above:

```rust
let mut port = serial2::SerialPort::open("COM9", 115200).unwrap();
port.set_read_timeout(Duration::from_millis(200)).unwrap();
let mut fd = filedescriptor::FileDescriptor::dup(&port).unwrap();   // what try_clone_reader does
let mut buf = [0u8; 512];
println!("{:?}", fd.read(&mut buf));   // main: Err(87); with #8223: Ok(0)
```

Possibly relevant while bisecting: before #6411 `pty/Cargo.toml` depended on `serial = "0.4"`; I could not verify how that crate opened the port, but if it opened it without `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, this would be a regression introduced by #6411 — which would also fit #6969, filed against 20240203, where Windows serial echo works but is sluggish.

The arm64 debs on the nightly release are from January. The Cirrus arm tasks still build fine, they just can't upload any more: 401 on the encrypted `GITHUB_TOKEN` since March, #7716. And they only ever uploaded the debs, so there has never been an aarch64 tarball.

Cirrus was the only way to get arm64 when those tasks were written. It isn't any more. GitHub has had Linux arm64 runners since 2025, free and unlimited for public repos, 4 vCPU and 16 GB, which is the same size as the Cirrus arm containers. `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runs the same images, `ci/deploy.sh` already puts the arch in the filename, and every run gets its own token, so there is nothing left to re-encrypt. I can send a PR if you want one.

I run main on aarch64 anyway. This is e2a98e1b on Gentoo:

![wezterm on Gentoo aarch64](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zakkaus/wezterm/screenshots/gentoo-aarch64-wezterm.webp)

Ping me if you want something tested on arm.

### Summary

On Windows (native, ConPTY), with `enable_kitty_keyboard = true`, an **IME commit consisting of exactly one character** — a single CJK character (`我`) or a single full-width punctuation (`，` `。`) — never reaches the child process: the child reads **zero bytes**. Multi-character commits (`这是什么`) arrive fine, and plain ASCII is fine.

Setting `enable_kitty_keyboard = false` makes all of them work immediately. This matches the root cause already described in #7915 / #7944: for a `KeyCode::Composed` event `encode_kitty()` falls into the catch-all arm, `self.raw` is `None`, and an empty string is written to the pane (with the normal text fallback short-circuited).

### Summary

The admin UI assets vendored in both `org.wiremock:wiremock:3.13.2` and `org.wiremock:wiremock-standalone:3.13.2` (`assets/swagger-ui/`) embed swagger-ui-dist 5.30.2, whose bundles carry **DOMPurify 3.2.6**:

```
$ unzip -p wiremock-standalone-3.13.2.jar \
    assets/swagger-ui/swagger-ui-dist/swagger-ui-bundle.js | grep -o 'DOMPurify.version="[0-9.]*"'
DOMPurify.version="3.2.6"
```

DOMPurify ≤ 3.4.10 is affected by CVE-2026-65898 (GHSA-cmwh-pvxp-8882, fixed in **3.4.11**), among newer advisories. Security scanners (OWASP Dependency-Check / RetireJS) therefore flag every project embedding WireMock, and no released WireMock version helps:

- the stable line stops at 3.13.2;
- 4.0.0-beta.38 actually bundles an **older** DOMPurify (3.1.4, via swagger-ui 5.17.14);
- the thin `wiremock` artifact carries the same assets, so switching artifacts does not remove them.

### Ask

Please refresh the vendored swagger-ui to a release embedding DOMPurify ≥ 3.4.11 in the next 3.x patch (and in the 4.x line).

### Proposal

When an HTTP Client sends a message such as: 
```
> POST / HTTP/1.1
> Host: localhost:8082
> User-Agent: curl/8.5.0
> Accept: */*
> Connection: Upgrade, HTTP2-Settings
> Upgrade: h2c
> HTTP2-Settings: AAMAAABkAAQAoAAAAAIAAAAA
> transfer-encoding: chunked
> Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
```

Then WireMock (simply `java -jar wiremock-standalone-3.13.2.jar`) , returns an Upgrade response then kills the HTTP/2 stream instead of returning a valid HTTP response: 
```
< HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
< Upgrade: h2c
< Connection: Upgrade
* Received 101, Switching to HTTP/2
* HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly: CANCEL (err 8)
* Connection #0 to host localhost left intact
curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly: CANCEL (err 8)
```

Tested with WireMock 3.12.0 and latest (3.13.2).

FYI, I've checked the CURL command against a Vert.x server, configured as below, and the request works well: 
```
Vertx.vertx()
     .createHttpServer(new HttpServerOptions().setHttp2ClearTextEnabled(true))
     .requestHandler(request -> request.response().end("OK"))
     .listen()
     .blockingGet();
```

### Reproduction steps

Just run `curl -v --http2 -d "aaa" -H "transfer-encoding: chunked" http://localhost:8082/` with a WireMock instance running on 8082.

### Self-service

- [ ] I'd be willing to implement a fix

### Describe the bug

Since 4.18.0, `yarn version apply --prerelease=<identifier>` applies the deferred
version bump but silently ignores the prerelease identifier, and no `stableVersion`
is written back to the manifest.

Given a deferred `patch` release on `1.0.32`:

| Yarn | `version` after `apply --prerelease=alpha.0` | `stableVersion` |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| 4.12.0 – 4.17.0 | `1.0.33-alpha.0` | `1.0.32` |
| **4.18.0** | `1.0.33` | *(absent)* |

The command exits 0 with no warning, so the failure is invisible in CI. This is a
common "back to development" step in release pipelines — after tagging a release,
the next dev version is supposed to carry a prerelease suffix. On 4.18.0 the branch
is left on a plain release version instead, which then fails downstream checks that
assert the working version is a prerelease.

I bisected this to 4.18.0 exactly; 4.17.0 and every earlier 4.x I tested behave as
documented. The only version-related change in that release is #7218
("Version: Reimplement `yarn version` and `yarn version apply`"), so I assume the
regression was introduced there.

Docs for the flag: https://yarnpkg.com/cli/version/apply

> If `--prerelease` is set, the given prerelease identifier (by default `rc.%d`)
> will be used on all new versions and the version definitions will be kept as-is.

### To reproduce

Single-package repo, no workspaces, no dependencies.

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "t",
  "version": "1.0.32-alpha.0",
  "packageManager": "yarn@4.18.0"
}
```

`.yarnrc.yml`:

```yaml
nodeLinker: node-modules
```

Then:

```bash
git init -b main && git add -A && git commit -m init

# release bump
yarn version patch                        # -> 1.0.32
git commit -am release

# back to development
yarn version patch --deferred
yarn version apply --prerelease=alpha.0

node -p "require('./package.json').version"
```

Expected: `1.0.33-alpha.0`
Actual (4.18.0): `1.0.33`

Swapping `packageManager` to `yarn@4.17.0` and re-running the exact same steps
yields `1.0.33-alpha.0` plus `"stableVersion": "1.0.32"`.

Bisect results, same script, only `packageManager` changed:

```
yarn 4.12.0  ->  1.0.33-alpha.0
yarn 4.13.0  ->  1.0.33-alpha.0
yarn 4.14.0  ->  1.0.33-alpha.0
yarn 4.15.0  ->  1.0.33-alpha.0
yarn 4.16.0  ->  1.0.33-alpha.0
yarn 4.17.0  ->  1.0.33-alpha.0
yarn 4.18.0  ->  1.0.33            <-- regression
```

### Environment

```shell
System:
    OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200
    CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10850H CPU @ 2.70GHz
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.13.0
    Yarn: 4.17.0
    npm: 11.6.2

# Note: envinfo above reports 4.17.0 because the repo has since been pinned back
# to a working version. The reproduction above was run with 4.18.0 resolved via
# corepack from the `packageManager` field.
```

### Additional context

Hit this in a shared GitLab CI release template used across several repos. Every
repo on 4.12.0 produces the correct `-alpha.0` version; the one repo that had been
bumped to 4.18.0 silently produced a plain release version and broke the next
pipeline run. Pinning `packageManager` back to `yarn@4.17.0` resolved it.

<!--
  Important: These issues are for **concrete and actionable proposals**. If you just have
  a general problem that you would like to brainstorm, open a Discussion instead. We want
  our GitHub issues to be a strict project backlog.
-->

- [x] I'd be willing to implement this feature ([contributing guide](https://yarnpkg.com/advanced/contributing))
- [x] This feature is important to have in this repository; a contrib plugin wouldn't do

## Describe the user story

In a large Yarn monorepo using `nodeLinker: node-modules` with [N] workspaces, I regularly run tests from workspaces outside my main area of work.

Running `yarn workspaces focus <workspace>` removes packages from `node_modules` that are not needed by that workspace. On our repository, focusing takes a few minutes, and returning to my normal workspace setup takes a few more. I repeat this workflow a few times, so the unlink/relink cycle  can add up and be pretty painful. 

I am not sure if this issue affects repos using PnP, as I haven't had a chance to work in a large monorepo that uses it.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Ideally I want a way to _only_ ensure that all the dependencies for a workspace are present, without doing any pruning or unlinking of extraneous node modules. I'd propose adding a `--keep-existing` flag (defaults to off, so no behavior change unless the flag is passed) to the `yarn workspaces focus` command but open to other APIs.

## Describe the drawbacks of your solution

The main drawback I can see is that it may leave stale dependencies laying around, since it likely means we also wouldn't cleanup stale modules after they've been removed from package.json. To my mind this is pretty minor, since these stale dependencies mostly shouldn't hurt anybody, and it's pretty easy to get back to a clean state by just _not_ passing the new flag, though I could see it causing issues to be created here if people get themselves into a bad state by abusing the flag.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Why not make it a plugin: My understanding is that since this requires changing install behavior, not adding to it, a plugin wouldn't be able to accomplish what I'm asking without significantly duplicating the logic that exists here.

Other solutions I've considered: 
Maintaining state of which workspaces are currently "focused" and using that to allow for more custom plugin based workflows. This seems much more complex to me, as you'd need to figure out where to store that state, and how to keep it up to date as external factors change the yarn install state and edit package.json, and still only provides a partial solution because it would require a plugin built on top of it to actually improve the real behavior.

body_text: ### Self-service - [x] I'd be willing to implement a fix ### Describe the bug `yarn upgrade-interactive` silently ignores errors encountered while querying a registry for available package versions. For example, when a dependency is hosted on a private npm registry and the registry responds with `403 Forbidden`, `yarn install` correctly reports the error, but `yarn upgrade-interactive` silently behaves as if there were no upgrade available. This makes it impossible to distinguish between: * the package having no available upgrade, and * Yarn being unable to determine whether an upgrade is available. ### To reproduce 1. Configure a dependency to use a private npm registry. 2. Make the registry return `403 Forbidden` when Yarn queries package metadata (for example, due to missing/invalid credentials). 3. Run: ```text yarn install ``` Yarn reports the registry error, e.g. `403 Forbidden`. 4. Run: ```text yarn upgrade-interactive ``` The package is silently omitted from the list of upgrade candidates. No error or warning is displayed. **Expected behavior** `yarn upgrade-interactive` should indicate that it was unable to check the package. It doesn't necessarily need to abort the entire interactive command — other packages could still be displayed — but a registry error should not be indistinguishable from "no update is available." For example, it could display a warning such as: ```text Warning: failed to check @example/private-package for updates: HTTP 403 Forbidden ``` or otherwise mark the package as unavailable to check. **Actual behavior** The registry error is silently discarded and the package is omitted from the upgrade suggestions. ### Environment ```shell System: OS: Linux 7.0 Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat) CPU: (8) x64 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1135G7 @ 2.40GHz Binaries: Node: 20.20.1 - /tmp/xfs-b142f623/node Yarn: 4.12.0 - /tmp/xfs-b142f623/yarn npm: 10.8.2 - /home/juho/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.1/bin/npm ``` ### Additional context The result of running `yarn install` displays errors: But `yarn upgrade-interactive` does not: The current implementation contains: ```ts const [resolution, latest] = await Promise.all([ fetchUpdatedDescriptor(descriptor, descriptor.range, referenceRange).catch(() => null), fetchUpdatedDescriptor(descriptor, descriptor.range, `latest`).catch(() => null), ]); ``` The `catch(() => null)` means that registry errors are converted to `null`. Later, packages with no non-empty suggestions are removed: ```ts if (suggestions.filter(suggestion => suggestion.label !== ``).length <= 1) return null; ``` Therefore, an HTTP error becomes indistinguishable from a package for which no upgrade is available. Source: https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/e4e423a1eb117b5129f20ac626a03eb7a97aedff/packages/plugin-interactive-tools/sources/commands/upgrade-interactive.tsx

## Describe the user story

Being able to specify path to the home rc file can make yarn more configurable. It's often useful to isolate a tool. Maybe one don't want their home directory to be messy. Or maybe one is borrowing someone's computer and don't want to accidentally change anything, or accidentally affected by the original config. 

## Describe the solution you'd like

A method to specify the path to the home rc file when running the yarn command.

An alternative can be moving the file into `globalFolder`, and then the folder can be specified with environment variables.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Configuring with environment variables. However, one won't be able to use yarn config set. And it won't prevent yarn being affected by a rc file that's already present.

**Describe the bug**

With PnP, when the global folder (default `$HOME/.yarn/berry`) is reached through a symlinked path, `pnpapi.resolveRequest` hands Node a **realpath'd** filename for a package served from an archive, while the PnP map records that archive under the **symlinked** spelling. A **relative** `require` from inside the archive is then resolved against the realpath and fails:

```
Error: Cannot find module './dep.cjs'
Require stack:
- /volume1/homes/<user>/.yarn/berry/cache/repro-pkg-file-c28e1974f5-10c0.zip/node_modules/repro-pkg/index.js
- /tmp/repro/consumer/main.js
    at require$$0.Module._resolveFilename (.pnp.cjs:5924:54)
```

The file **is** in the archive — `unzip -l` lists `node_modules/repro-pkg/dep.cjs` — and a package **subpath** resolves fine: `require('repro-pkg/dep.cjs')` prints `dep loaded`. Only the entry's relative `require('./dep.cjs')` fails.

**To reproduce**

```sh
# $HOME here is /var/services/homes/<user>, a symlink to /volume1/homes/<user> (Synology DSM)

# a package whose entry requires a file beside it
mkdir -p /tmp/repro/stage/package /tmp/repro/consumer/.yarn/releases
cat > /tmp/repro/stage/package/package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "repro-pkg", "version": "1.0.0", "main": "index.js" }
JSON
echo "module.exports = require('./dep.cjs')" > /tmp/repro/stage/package/index.js
echo "module.exports = 'dep loaded'"         > /tmp/repro/stage/package/dep.cjs
(cd /tmp/repro/stage && tar czf /tmp/repro/repro-pkg.tgz package)

# a PnP consumer that installs it from the tarball
cp /path/to/yarn-4.18.1.cjs /tmp/repro/consumer/.yarn/releases/
printf 'nodeLinker: pnp\nyarnPath: .yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs\n' > /tmp/repro/consumer/.yarnrc.yml
cat > /tmp/repro/consumer/package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "consumer", "private": true, "dependencies": { "repro-pkg": "file:../repro-pkg.tgz" } }
JSON
echo "console.log(require('repro-pkg'))" > /tmp/repro/consumer/main.js

cd /tmp/repro/consumer
yarn install
yarn node main.js
```

**The two APIs disagree**

```
$ node -r ./.pnp.cjs -e "const p=require('pnpapi');console.log('toUnqualified:',p.resolveToUnqualified('repro-pkg',process.cwd()+'/main.js'));console.log('request:      ',p.resolveRequest('repro-pkg',process.cwd()+'/main.js'))"
toUnqualified: /var/services/homes/<user>/.yarn/berry/cache/repro-pkg-file-c28e1974f5-10c0.zip/node_modules/repro-pkg/
request:       /volume1/homes/<user>/.yarn/berry/cache/repro-pkg-file-c28e1974f5-10c0.zip/node_modules/repro-pkg/index.js
```

Adding the realpath of that same folder makes it pass, with the **same** archive file:

```yaml
# .yarnrc.yml
globalFolder: /volume1/homes/<user>/.yarn/berry   # instead of the symlinked spelling
```

```
$ yarn node main.js
dep loaded
```

**Expected behaviour**

body_text:
### Self-service

- [x] I'd be willing to implement a fix

### Describe the bug

`yarn npm publish` with provenance (`npmPublishProvenance: true`) can abort **after** its attestation has been persisted in Rekor, leaving the package unpublished and an orphan entry in the transparency log:

```
Some packages failed to publish:
prettier-plugin-toml@4.0.0
└ YN0001: gM: error creating tlog entry - (409) an equivalent entry already exists
  in the transparency log with UUID 108e9186e8c5677a54340083e014f9715fa30a9c88a599e46878bb4c5e68f8f4bdc66337dcd942d7
    at wre.createEntry (…/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs:430:90654)
    at async Bre.testify (…/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs:430:94323)
    at async Promise.all (index 0)
    at async mX.create (…/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs:400:20687)
```

Reconstructed mechanism:

1. `Rekor.createEntry` POSTs to `/api/v1/log/entries` through `fetchWithRetry`, which retries 5xx, 408, 429 and network failures.
2. If Rekor persists the entry but the response is one of those retryable outcomes (or is lost/times out), the retry re-POSTs the *identical* DSSE entry.
3. The second POST is answered with `409 an equivalent entry already exists`.
4. `TLogClient.createEntry` can recover from exactly this — it catches the conflict and fetches the existing entry — but only when `fetchOnConflict` is true, and the witness is built with it hard-coded to false:

```js
new RekorWitness({
  rekorBaseURL: t.rekorURL,
  entryType: t.legacyCompatibility ? 'intoto' : 'dsse',
  fetchOnConflict: !1,          // <-- conflict is fatal
  retry: t.retry ?? DEFAULT_RETRY,
  timeout: t.timeout ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
})
```

So the conflict surfaces as `TLOG_CREATE_ENTRY_ERROR`, the publish aborts, and the tarball is never uploaded — even though the attestation it needed is already in the log.

Evidence from the public Rekor API (`GET https://rekor.sigstore.dev/api/v1/log/entries/<uuid>`):

| attempt | entry UUID | integratedTime | error raised | payloadHash |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `108e9186…42d7` | 2026-10-16T16:45:29Z | 16:45:35 | `5ccb61f143f430544777f6df560a456e698517c0a8b4d0ff7e6fbff2dec1f936` |
| 2 | `108e9186…66f7` | 2026-10-16T16:49:53Z | 16:50:00 | `462f820fd1fddb2f5f651c06ebf83b2056cba37492bf40e4b0c8bbd82cef2ace` |

- Each error is raised ~6–7 s after the entry it names was created — the shape of a first request that was retried rather than one that simply succeeded.
- The payload hashes differ between the attempts because the statement embeds `runDetails.metadata.invocationId` (`…/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/attempts/${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}`) and `resolvedDependencies[].digest.gitCommit`. Attempt 2 therefore cannot have collided with attempt 1's entry — it collided with its own, i.e. the duplicate is generated *inside a single publish*, not by a stale log entry.
- The version never appears in the registry while its entry exists.

Expected instead, any of:

- treat a conflict as success when the entry is already logged (that is all `attest()` needs);
- or honour `fetchOnConflict` / default it to true for the publish path — the bundled sigstore client already implements the recovery;
- or at minimum, never abort the registry upload when the log entry was written by this very run.

### To reproduce

A registry publish can't be reduced to a `package.json`, so the reproduction is the two public runs plus the Rekor entries above. The essential setup:

1. GitHub Actions release workflow with `id-token: write` (here npm Trusted Publishing), `.yarnrc.yml` with `npmPublishProvenance: true`.
2. Publish a public workspace whose version is not yet in the registry, one `yarn npm publish` per package (here driven by `changeset publish`).
3. Watch for `YN0001: … error creating tlog entry - (409) an equivalent entry already exists`.

It is a race, so it is intermittent: the same repository published `prettier-plugin-sh@0.20.2` and `prettier-plugin-toml@3.0.2` with provenance successfully on 2026-09-24 (yarn 4.17.1), then failed twice in a row ~6 minutes apart on 2026-10-16. Presumably the tlog POST has to be retried for the bug to fire.

Failing runs:

- https://github.com/un-ts/prettier/actions/runs/38934371950 — job `117086020953` (attempt 1), job `117087882350` (attempt 2)

### Environment

```
GitHub Actions: ubuntu-latest (GitHub-hosted), 2026-10-16
Node: 24 (lts/*)
Yarn: 4.18.1 — /home/runner/work/prettier/prettier/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs
      (.yarnrc.yml: nodeLinker: node-modules, npmPublishProvenance: true)
Publish driver: changeset publish (@changesets/cli@3.0.3) -> yarn npm publish
Registry auth: npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC); Fulcio/OIDC signing works, the
      failure is at the Rekor write
```

### Additional context

- This is a race, not a deterministic failure, and I do not think it is caused by the yarn 4.17.1 → 4.18.1 upgrade: the publish-side code (`Rekor.createEntry`, `fetchWithRetry`, `RekorWitness` construction, the `TLogClient` conflict branch) reads the same across those bundles. What did change is the bundled sigstore client — 4.18.x also carries a `TLogV2Client` that 4.17.1 does not — so I can't rule out a changed retry/timeout policy. The symptom needs a retried POST either way.
- The last successful provenance publish in that repository was on 2026-09-24 with yarn 4.17.1; the next release with something to publish is the one that failed, so there is no counter-example in between.
- Our workaround, not yet applied: publish the blocked version once with `npmPublishProvenance: false`, then re-enable provenance.
- Other ecosystems see the same class of failure with npm's CLI and treat a Rekor 409 as already-published in CI (ChainSafe/lodestar#9703, vectorize-io/hindsight `ec384e9`, WordPress/wordpress-playground#4269).

Happy to supply the full job logs, the raw Rekor entry bodies, or to test a patch if you want one.

- [x] I'd be willing to implement a fix

### Describe the bug

`yarn npm publish` with provenance (`npmPublishProvenance: true`) can abort **after** its attestation has been persisted in Rekor, leaving the package unpublished and an orphan entry in the transparency log:

```
Some packages failed to publish:
prettier-plugin-toml@4.0.0
└ YN0001: gM: error creating tlog entry - (409) an equivalent entry already exists
  in the transparency log with UUID 108e9186e8c5677a54340083e014f9715fa30a9c88a599e46878bb4c5e68f8f4bdc66337dcd942d7
    at wre.createEntry (…/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs:430:90654)
    at async Bre.testify (…/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs:430:94323)
    at async Promise.all (index 0)
    at async mX.create (…/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs:400:20687)
```

Reconstructed mechanism:

1. `Rekor.createEntry` POSTs to `/api/v1/log/entries` through `fetchWithRetry`, which retries 5xx, 408, 429 and network failures.
2. If Rekor persists the entry but the response is one of those retryable outcomes (or is lost/times out), the retry re-POSTs the *identical* DSSE entry.
3. The second POST is answered with `409 an equivalent entry already exists`.
4. `TLogClient.createEntry` can recover from exactly this — it catches the conflict and fetches the existing entry — but only when `fetchOnConflict` is true, and the witness is built with it hard-coded to false:

```js
new RekorWitness({
  rekorBaseURL: t.rekorURL,
  entryType: t.legacyCompatibility ? 'intoto' : 'dsse',
  fetchOnConflict: !1,          // <-- conflict is fatal
  retry: t.retry ?? DEFAULT_RETRY,
  timeout: t.timeout ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
})
```

So the conflict surfaces as `TLOG_CREATE_ENTRY_ERROR`, the publish aborts, and the tarball is never uploaded — even though the attestation it needed is already in the log.

Evidence from the public Rekor API (`GET https://rekor.sigstore.dev/api/v1/log/entries/<uuid>`):

| attempt | entry UUID | integratedTime | error raised | payloadHash |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `108e9186…42d7` | 2026-10-16T16:45:29Z | 16:45:35 | `5ccb61f143f430544777f6df560a456e698517c0a8b4d0ff7e6fbff2dec1f936` |
| 2 | `108e9186…66f7` | 2026-10-16T16:49:53Z | 16:50:00 | `462f820fd1fddb2f5f651c06ebf83b2056cba37492bf40e4b0c8bbd82cef2ace` |

- Each error is raised ~6–7 s after the entry it names was created — the shape of a first request that was retried rather than one that simply succeeded.
- The payload hashes differ between the attempts because the statement embeds `runDetails.metadata.invocationId` (`…/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/attempts/${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}`) and `resolvedDependencies[].digest.gitCommit`. Attempt 2 therefore cannot have collided with attempt 1's entry — it collided with its own, i.e. the duplicate is generated *inside a single publish*, not by a stale log entry.
- The version never appears in the registry while its entry exists.

Expected instead, any of:

- treat a conflict as success when the entry is already logged (that is all `attest()` needs);
- or honour `fetchOnConflict` / default it to true for the publish path — the bundled sigstore client already implements the recovery;
- or at minimum, never abort the registry upload when the log entry was written by this very run.

### To reproduce

A registry publish can't be reduced to a `package.json`, so the reproduction is the two public runs plus the Rekor entries above. The essential setup:

1. GitHub Actions release workflow with `id-token: write` (here npm Trusted Publishing), `.yarnrc.yml` with `npmPublishProvenance: true`.
2. Publish a public workspace whose version is not yet in the registry, one `yarn npm publish` per package (here driven by `changeset publish`).
3. Watch for `YN0001: … error creating tlog entry - (409) an equivalent entry already exists`.

It is a race, so it is intermittent: the same repository published `prettier-plugin-sh@0.20.2` and `prettier-plugin-toml@3.0.2` with provenance successfully on 2026-09-24 (yarn 4.17.1), then failed twice in a row ~6 minutes apart on 2026-10-16. Presumably the tlog POST has to be retried for the bug to fire.

Failing runs:

- https://github.com/un-ts/prettier/actions/runs/38934371950 — job `117086020953` (attempt 1), job `117087882350` (attempt 2)

### Environment

```
GitHub Actions: ubuntu-latest (GitHub-hosted), 2026-10-16
Node: 24 (lts/*)
Yarn: 4.18.1 — /home/runner/work/prettier/prettier/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.18.1.cjs
      (.yarnrc.yml: nodeLinker: node-modules, npmPublishProvenance: true)
Publish driver: changeset publish (@changesets/cli@3.0.3) -> yarn npm publish
Registry auth: npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC); Fulcio/OIDC signing works, the
      failure is at the Rekor write
```

### Additional context

- This is a race, not a deterministic failure, and I do not think it is caused by the yarn 4.17.1 → 4.18.1 upgrade: the publish-side code (`Rekor.createEntry`, `fetchWithRetry`, `RekorWitness` construction, the `TLogClient` conflict branch) reads the same across those bundles. What did change is the bundled sigstore client — 4.18.x also carries a `TLogV2Client` that 4.17.1 does not — so I can't rule out a changed retry/timeout policy. The symptom needs a retried POST either way.
- The last successful provenance publish in that repository was on 2026-09-24 with yarn 4.17.1; the next release with something to publish is the one that failed, so there is no counter-example in between.
- Our workaround, not yet applied: publish the blocked version once with `npmPublishProvenance: false`, then re-enable provenance.
- Other ecosystems see the same class of failure with npm's CLI and treat a Rekor 409 as already-published in CI (ChainSafe/lodestar#9703, vectorize-io/hindsight `ec384e9`, WordPress/wordpress-playground#4269).

Happy to supply the full job logs, the raw Rekor entry bodies, or to test a patch if you want one.

### Self-service

- [ ] I'd be willing to implement a fix

### Describe the bug

If the title isn't clear, see the reproduction below.



### To reproduce

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "yarning",
  "packageManager": "yarn@4.18.1",
  "scripts": {
    "hi": "yarn --version"
  }
}
```

And you need a `.yarnrc.yml` with a `yarnPath` pointing to a different version of yarn than the one on your PATH. In the following console session, `yarn` from my `PATH` is 4.18.0, but my `yarnPath` points to 4.18.1.

Note that yarn correctly honors the configured `yarnPath`, but ignores it if `YARN_IGNORE_PATH` is set:

```console
$ yarn --version
4.18.1

$ YARN_IGNORE_PATH=true yarn --version
4.18.0
```

But if we run the script, we see the `yarnPath` is executed regardless of if `YARN_IGNORE_PATH` is set:

```console
$ yarn run hi
4.18.1

$ YARN_IGNORE_PATH=true yarn run hi
4.18.1
```

### Environment

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 6.18 cpe:/o:nixos:nixos:26.11 26.11 (Zokor)
    CPU: (16) x64 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1260P
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.21.0 - /tmp/xfs-7ca251f4/node
    Yarn: 4.18.1 - /tmp/xfs-7ca251f4/yarn
```

### Additional context

The root cause is that `yarn` deletes the `YARN_IGNORE_PATH` environment variable right before invoking the configured `yarnPath`: https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/%40yarnpkg/cli/4.18.1/packages/yarnpkg-cli/sources/lib.ts#L158.

This behavior was introduced in https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/pull/256, and seems to be understood:

> One problem is that it causes the settings to never persist - so a user manually adding YARN_IGNORE_PATH in their environment might be confused to see that the local one will still get executed in the nested scripts.

This is one user being confused by this behavior.

It seems to me like the fix is to just undo #256. The PR description has a broken link explaining that we set `YARN_IGNORE_PATH` somewhere:

> and since we set [YARN_IGNORE_PATH](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/blob/master/packages/berry-cli/sources/cli.ts#L27) the nested global instances never reexecute the local ones

I wonder if that behavior still exists and is truly necessary?

### Summary

When using Zed agent with an enterprise OpenAI-compatible API, tool calls fail with an error about empty \ parameter.

### Description

I've configured Zed to use our enterprise OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. Regular message exchange works correctly - I can send messages and receive responses. However, when the agent attempts to call tools, the request fails with the following error:

\
The error indicates that Zed is sending an empty string for the \ field in position 8 of the input array, but the API requires this to be a non-empty string.

### Model Provider Details

- **Provider**: Enterprise OpenAI-compatible API
- **Mode**: Agent Panel
- **Tool Calling**: Failing

### Expected Behavior

When the agent needs to call a tool:
1. Zed should generate a valid non-empty \ for each tool call
2. The tool call should execute successfully
3. Results should be returned to the agent

### Actual Behavior

1. Zed sends a tool call request with an empty 2. The OpenAI-compatible API rejects the request with a 400 error
3. Tool calling fails completely

### Reproduction Steps

1. Configure Zed to use an enterprise OpenAI-compatible API endpoint
2. Start a conversation with the agent
3. Request the agent to perform an action that requires tool calling
4. Observe the error in the agent panel

### Additional Context

This appears to be specific to tool calling - regular conversation works fine. The issue may be related to how Zed constructs the tool call payload for OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

### Zed Version and System Specs

(Please add your version information from Help > About Zed or \)

### Reproduction steps

## Bug Description
After modifying `.zed/debug.json`, clicking "Rerun Session" in the debugger does not 
reload the config file. The old configuration is still used. A full Zed restart 
(close and reopen) is required to pick up changes.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create `.zed/debug.json` with the following content:
```json
[
  {
    "label": "debug main",
    "adapter": "CodeLLDB",
    "request": "launch",
    "build": {
      "command": "cargo",
      "args": ["build"]
    },
    "program": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug/target/debug/main",
    "sourceLanguages": ["rust"],
    "args": [],
    "cwd": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug"
  }
]
```
2. Launch the debugger — it runs with `program: .../main`
3. Modify `debug.json`, change `program` to `.../test_debug`
4. Click "Rerun Session" in the debugger panel

## Expected Behavior
"Rerun Session" should reload `.zed/debug.json` and use the updated `program` path.

## Actual Behavior
"Rerun Session" still launches with the old `program` path (`.../main`).

Console output after rerun:
```
Console is in 'commands' mode, prefix expressions with '?'.
Loading Rust formatters from /home/somnus/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/etc
Tried to launch debugger with: {
  "request": "launch",
  "program": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug/target/debug/main",
  "cwd": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug",
  "args": [],
  "name": "debug main"
}
error: '/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug/target/debug/main' does not exist
```

Terminal output:
```
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.00s
⏵ Task `debug-build` finished successfully
⏵ Command: /usr/bin/zsh -i -c 'cargo'
```

## Workaround
Close Zed completely and reopen it. A new debug session will then use the updated config.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

current 
![](https://somnusblog.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/images/20260325135525645.png)
expected behavior

## Bug Description
After modifying `.zed/debug.json`, clicking "Rerun Session" in the debugger does not 
reload the config file. The old configuration is still used. A full Zed restart 
(close and reopen) is required to pick up changes.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create `.zed/debug.json` with the following content:
```json
[
  {
    "label": "debug main",
    "adapter": "CodeLLDB",
    "request": "launch",
    "build": {
      "command": "cargo",
      "args": ["build"]
    },
    "program": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug/target/debug/main",
    "sourceLanguages": ["rust"],
    "args": [],
    "cwd": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug"
  }
]
```
2. Launch the debugger — it runs with `program: .../main`
3. Modify `debug.json`, change `program` to `.../test_debug`
4. Click "Rerun Session" in the debugger panel

## Expected Behavior
"Rerun Session" should reload `.zed/debug.json` and use the updated `program` path.

## Actual Behavior
"Rerun Session" still launches with the old `program` path (`.../main`).

Console output after rerun:
```
Console is in 'commands' mode, prefix expressions with '?'.
Loading Rust formatters from /home/somnus/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/etc
Tried to launch debugger with: {
  "request": "launch",
  "program": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug/target/debug/main",
  "cwd": "/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug",
  "args": [],
  "name": "debug main"
}
error: '/home/somnus/code/rustStore/test_debug/target/debug/main' does not exist
```

Terminal output:
```
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.00s
⏵ Task `debug-build` finished successfully
⏵ Command: /usr/bin/zsh -i -c 'cargo'
```

## Workaround
Close Zed completely and reopen it. A new debug session will then use the updated config.

Within a React js/ts project, when `go_to_definition_fallback` is set to `find_all_references`, `Cmd + Click` on an exported definition (e.g., `export const SectionHeader`) only triggers the references view if clicked at the very beginning of the token. Clicking the middle or end of the token fails silently.

**Video:**

_(please watch the entire short clip to fully understand it. I tried showcasing both current behaviors)_ 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0db7ec9b-193a-482a-b518-86f5604f1db3

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**
Zed appears to rely on a strict cursor-movement heuristic for the fallback. 
* Clicking the start of the token: Cursor doesn't move -> Zed knows it's at the definition -> Fallback triggers correctly.
* Clicking the end of the token: Cursor jumps back to the start of the token -> Zed assumes `GoToDefinition` successfully navigated -> Fallback is swallowed.

**Expected behavior:**
The fallback check should use range-intersection (like Monaco/VS Code) rather than point-equality, so clicking anywhere within the token's bounding box correctly triggers `find_all_references` if already at the definition.

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Configure `search.include_ignored` to `false` (default)
2. `git clone --recursive https://codeberg.org/jsu/dotfiles test`
3. `zed test`
4. Expand `catppuccin/btop/` in the project panel (notice that `catppuccin/btop/LICENSE` is dimmed in the project panel)
5. Open `catppuccin/btop/LICENSE` (the file is still ignored, but it isn't dimmed in the project panel anymore)
6. Project Search for "MIT License" (it finds the file, even though it's ignored)

### Current vs. Expected behavior

The project panel conflates indexed and ignored. Once an ignored file is indexed, it seems to be no longer ignored?

What _should_ happen for gitignored files:

- Appear dimmed in the project panel
- Not appear in Project Search results if `search.include_ignored` is `false`

### Zed version and system specs

### Reproduction steps 1. Ask Agent to make change or edits to HTML. 2. Agent will perform `edit_file` tool calls. 3. If tool call fails, agent might struggle to resolve large changes in file and have with a messy dif. ### Current vs. Expected behavior ## Issue `edit_file` can mutate compact HTML even when it reports that the requested `old_text` did not match. Possibly related: - #57359 - #57041 ## Repro 1 File contents: ```html Compact

Hello

Keep this compact.

``` `edit_file` request: ```json { "edits": [ { "old_text": "Keep this compact.", "new_text": "Still compact." } ] } ``` Tool output: `Could not find matching text for edit at index 0. The old_text did not match any content in the file. Please read the file again to get the current content.` Actual file after the failed edit: ```html Compact

Hello

Keep this compact.

``` Expected: no file change if the edit fails, or only the requested text replacement if it succeeds. ## Repro 2 File contents: ```html
``` `edit_file` request: ```json { "edits": [ { "old_text": "property-card", "new_text": "property-card featured" } ] } ``` Actual file after the failed edit: ```html
``` Expected: ```html

### Reproduction steps

1. Open a remote project (WSL)

3. Add a user skill using / (e.g., /skills/...).
4. Click the generated skill link.
5. Zed opens a new tab with an incorrect path and empty content.

A new empty document opens.

```
/home/<user>/C:/Users/<user>/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md

Zed should open the actual SKILL.md file from the correct filesystem path.

body_text:
When a project contains a directory on NFS with millions of files, Zed remains responsive but stops opening files and stops expanding folders in the project panel. This is a regression, the last Zed release without this problem is 1.0.1.

In my case, the directory is a dataset with ~30M files, symlinked into the project and gitignored. If I remove that directory/symlink, Zed immediately starts working again without even needing to reload.

**Suspected cause:**

This seems related to (poll) file watching. Zed may be recursively traversing or polling the large NFS directory, and file open / project panel expansion seems to be waiting on that work.

Expected behavior: a large NFS directory should not block opening unrelated files or expanding unrelated folders. In general, it should also be possible to exclude paths from the watcher, same as VSCode.

---

### Reproduction steps

1. Create an ARM bare-metal embedded project (STM32F407VE / Cortex-M4)
2. Build with CMake to generate `compile_commands.json` at `build/Debug/`
3. Create a `.clangd` file with:

```yaml
CompileFlags:
  CompilationDatabase: build/Debug
  Add:
    - --target=arm-none-eabi
    - --gcc-toolchain=<path-to-arm-gcc-toolchain>
```

4. Open any `.cpp` file that includes standard headers (e.g., `#include <cstdint>`)
5. Observe: clangd reports `'cstdint' file not found` for all ARM GCC system headers


## Disclaimer

Please note that the above diagnosis is based on my own testing and may not be 100% precise. The core problem I've confirmed is: **clangd cannot find ARM GCC bare-metal system headers with default configuration on any platform**. The exact root cause (multilib traversal, compiler probing, resource-dir mismatch, or something else) should be verified by your team through independent reproduction. I'm reporting from the user perspective — the symptom is real, the cause analysis is my best-effort, and I trust your expertise to pinpoint the exact issue.



### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior:

clangd returns an empty include search list when `--gcc-toolchain` is used for `arm-none-eabi` targets:

```
#include <...> search starts here:
End of search list.
```

All ARM GCC system headers (`cstdint`, `c++config.h`, etc.) are reported as unresolved.

Expected behavior:

`--gcc-toolchain` should discover ARM GCC's multilib include directories, just as it does for hosted GCC targets. For Cortex-M4 with hard float, it should find:

- `arm-none-eabi/include/c++/13.3.1/`
- `arm-none-eabi/include/c++/13.3.1/arm-none-eabi/`
- `arm-none-eabi/include/c++/13.3.1/arm-none-eabi/thumb/v7e-m+fp/hard/`
- `arm-none-eabi/include/`
- `lib/gcc/arm-none-eabi/13.3.1/include/`

The same configuration works correctly for hosted GCC targets. Only bare-metal (`arm-none-eabi`) is affected.

### Reproduction steps

1. Get a machine on a service that has a banner when using ssh, like [`targon`](https://targon.com/tower), or set up a box with a banner like this yourself.
2. Try to connect to it using Zed Remote

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior
-  The ssh connection within Zed times out while trying to start the remote server

Expected behavior
- I'm connected to the remote machine

The crucial part is the banner,
output of ssh:
```
02:53:53 vaqxai@vaqxai-bwpc ~ → ssh h200_x4 -qT "echo OK"
Connecting to container wrk-saarbs2d8vmx-65c557b858-fqtt2...
OK
```
This should only print "OK" and breaks ZED's scp, because it interprets the banner as part of the handshake.
Zed needs to work around that, for example, vscode right now uses a special sequence that the client waits on, which lets it simply skip & discard banners.

### Reproduction steps

**Summary**

When a workspace contains a single-file worktree, Zed launches external agents (Claude Code via ACP) with the file's *containing directory* as `--add-dir`. Opening one file therefore grants the agent read/write access to everything in that directory — silently, with no indication in the agent panel.

**Environment**



**Reproduction**

1. Open a project (e.g. `~/code/myrepo`).
2. Open a single file from outside the project, e.g. `~/private-documents/notes.md` — it becomes a single-file worktree.
3. Start a Claude Code thread in the agent panel.
4. Inspect the spawned process (`ps aux | grep claude`):

```
claude ... --add-dir /home/user/private-documents ...
```

**Expected**
Either the agent gets access to only the single file, or — if directory granularity is unavoidable — Zed asks before widening a file-scoped worktree into directory-scoped agent access. Honestly I was surprised already that it got access to that file, just because I saved it there, but ok surprises are hard to avoid with auto config and no explanation on how it works. So some first-time hint what auto actually would be a bonus on top.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Saving a single file to some directory exposes that whole directory to agents. Expectation (by me), saving a file somewhere does not give permission at all. Reasonable expectation: Definitely should not grant access to the whole directory.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed Nightly 1.11.3

The only authentication option offered is an Anthropic API key. There is no option to sign in with a Claude.ai account / Claude Pro or Max subscription (the "Claude Code" login). 4. This means usage is billed per API call, requiring me to keep topping up API credits, instead of using my existing Claude Pro/Max subscription. 5. This used to be straightforward to set up. ### Reproduction steps ## Scenario: When working with qwen3.8-27B on Godot project, qwen is tasked with generating a texture. It generates a .PNG file and then tries to insert it into the "chat" and "send it to itself to review" (send the file to LLM API backend through standard API call). ### Current vs. Expected behavior ## Current behavior LLM Generated a "wall.png" texture for 3D Godot project, then tried to read it with "Read". This always crahes the API call with: "400 Bad Request: Invalid 'content': 'content' field must be a string or an array of objects." LLM is calling LM Studio API. Tested also with OpenAI API on LM Studio with same result (so this does not seem to be API related). ## Note: This feature (LLM uploading it's own generated image to itself for self-inspection) seems to be very new, most probably first appearing (for me) with qwen3.8; prior versions of qwen or other LLMs never tried such a call, AFAIK. This is to investigate if these types of API calls to LM Studio API are put to gether correctly on ZED side...? ## Expected behavior LLM (with image processing capability) can read and send png (and other graphical?) files on it's own to LLM API backend for it's own image inspection. ### Zed version and system specs Zed 1.15.0 Commit: e17dc4f9d50db73a458b64dcce50ecd4878b98a3 Version: 1.15.0+stable.339.e17dc4f9d50db73a458b64dcce50ecd4878b98a3 OS: Ubuntu 26.04 Memory: 32GiB Architecture: amd64 ### Attach Zed log file

### Reproduction steps

1. Use a mouse that has vertical and horizontal scrolling capabilities (Logitech MX Master 3s here).
2. Use hi-res scrolling if possible on your mouse
3. Open a page of code that produces overflow vertically and horizontally on your screen
4. Try to scroll vertically and horizontally at the same time

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behaviour : If vertical scrolling inputs started first, then the page is only following the vertical axis, ignoring horizontal inputs. Same for horizontal inputs.

Expected behaviour: Inputs for horizontal and vertical scrolling are processed independently and at the same time.

### Reproduction steps

This is a common behavior in IDEs with integrated terminals, but I believe it can be improved.

When running a process that consumes a large amount of memory in the terminal, Zed crashes because the OS kills the process. However, the system should only terminate the terminal session, not the entire IDE.

This is extremely annoying when I leave an agent running multiple tasks, only to come back and find the IDE closed, forcing me to restart both the editor and the agent from scratch.

### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions
- Closest related: #55477 (Windows specific, TSF/ALPC deadlock in text input teardown). Different root cause, different platform. Not a duplicate.

### Describe the bug / problem

Every single window close (clicking the CSD × button) on a project with multiple nested git repositories produces a **noticeable delay before Zed actually exits**, accompanied by the log error:

```
ERROR [gpui::app] timed out waiting on app_will_quit
```

This happens **100% of the time** since installation. 17 consecutive occurrences in `Zed.log` spanning Aug 30 to Sep 4, across dozens of restarts. It is not intermittent.

The root cause is the hardcoded `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` of **200ms** in GPUI:

```rust
// crates/gpui/src/app.rs:78
pub const SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(200);
```

For a workspace containing 12 nested git repositories (~13,000 tracked entries), the shutdown observers (inotify watch teardown, SQLite workspace serialization flush, session state persistence, language server disconnect) cannot complete within this 200ms budget. The `block_with_timeout` at `app.rs:~989` fires, logs the error, and forcibly proceeds.

A hang trace captured during close confirms Worker-4 was blocked for **912ms** at `crates/gpui/src/app/context.rs:861:38` (`background_spawn`):

```json
{
  "thread_name": "Worker-4",
  "timings": [{
    "location": {"file": "crates/gpui/src/app/context.rs", "line": 861, "column": 38},
    "start": 69360285468,
    "duration": 912482568
  }]
}
```

### Shutdown code path traced

1. CSD × button click: `crates/platform_title_bar/src/platform_title_bar.rs:189` emits `workspace::CloseWindow`
2. `crates/workspace/src/multi_workspace.rs:~562` `close_window()`:
   - Calls `workspace.prepare_to_close(CloseIntent::CloseWindow)` per workspace
   - Calls `flush_pending_serialization()` which does `futures::future::join_all(flush_tasks).await` (line ~593)
   - Calls `window.remove_window()` (line ~596)
3. Last window removed: `crates/gpui/src/app.rs` detects empty windows, calls `cx.quit()`
4. `crates/gpui_linux/src/linux/platform.rs:280` `quit()`: signals event loop stop, invokes `on_quit` callback
5. `crates/gpui/src/app.rs:~974` `shutdown()`: collects all `quit_observers`, joins them via `foreground_executor.block_with_timeout(SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, futures)` at line ~989. On timeout: `log::error!("timed out waiting on app_will_quit")`
6. `crates/session/src/session.rs:107-115` `app_will_quit()` spawns `store_window_stack()` as a background task doing `db.write_kvp()`, racing against the 200ms budget

### What competes for the 200ms budget

- **inotify watch teardown**: Removing 13,000+ watch descriptors. Logs show `notify::inotify unable to remove watch descriptor: Os { code: 22, kind: InvalidInput }`, indicating some watches are already stale when teardown runs (likely because inotify_rm_watch and the event loop are racing)
- **SQLite workspace serialization**: `flush_pending_serialization` joins all pending workspace DB writes. For a large worktree, this includes pane state, editor state, terminal state, and dock sizes
- **Session state persistence**: `store_window_stack()` does a `db.write_kvp()` synchronous SQLite write during shutdown
- **Language server disconnect**: 12 git repos means potentially 12 LSP connections being torn down

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a parent directory containing multiple git repositories (I have 12, with ~13,000 total entries)
2. Open that parent directory in Zed as a single worktree

### Summary

Switching between threads bound to different custom ACP agents restores the
wrong agent for a thread. The thread's agent silently "becomes" the agent of
the previously selected thread; sending a prompt in this state errors until
the agent is manually re-selected.

### Reproduction steps

1. Configure two custom ACP agents in `agent_servers` (e.g. "grok" and
   "Kimi Code CLI", both `type: "custom"`, spawned via `args: ["acp"]`).
2. Create thread A with agent grok, send a few messages.
3. Create thread B with agent Kimi Code CLI, send a few messages.
4. Switch back and forth between thread A and thread B several times
   (also observed across projects and after window reloads).
5. Observe the agent shown for thread B: it sometimes silently becomes
   grok (the agent of the previously selected thread).
6. Type and send a message in thread B while the wrong agent is shown.

### Current vs. expected behavior

Expected: each thread always restores the agent that created it; sending a
prompt works regardless of how many times threads were switched.

Actual: the agent binding is not restored per thread — the previously used
agent "sticks". If a prompt is sent in this state, it errors (the session id
does not belong to the spawned agent's process). Manually re-selecting the
correct agent in the thread restores normal behavior.

### Notes

- Related to #43378 (item 4, "Agent switches randomly when selecting
  threads"), which was closed asking for individual, focused issues with
  specific repro steps.
- The ACP agents themselves behave correctly; this looks like client-side
  per-thread agent state not being persisted/restored on thread switch.

### Zed version and system specs

macOS (exact Zed version to be added in a follow-up comment; the machine
with Zed was not the one used to file this issue).
