### Reproduction steps

## Summary

The cached Xdebug adapter had an unresolvable `../encodings` in its bundled `iconv-lite`. Because `iconv-lite` loads codec tables lazily inside `getCodec()`, the adapter passed the entire DAP handshake and then exited with an uncaught `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` the moment a real Xdebug connection needed decoding. The bad copy was reused across sessions and restarts until I deleted it manually.


## Reproduction steps

As encountered:

1. `debug.json` with a listen-mode Xdebug config on port 9003 (see Settings below)
2. Start the debug session. Adapter starts and listens on 9003, breakpoints report `verified: true`
3. Trigger a PHP request so Xdebug connects back to the listener
4. Adapter process exits, session disappears

Not reproducible on demand, since it depended on a bad cached download and a refetch fixed it. To force the same failure:

    rm -rf ~/.local/share/zed/extensions/work/php/Xdebug/Xdebug_v1.40.1/extension/node_modules/iconv-lite/encodings

then run steps 2 through 4.

## Suggestions

**Verify extension archives before caching.** An incomplete tree leaves the adapter apparently functional until it reaches a lazily-required file, and the bad copy is then reused indefinitely. A checksum, or at minimum an entry-count or size check, with a refetch on mismatch would turn a silent crash into a clear download error.

**Surface adapter stderr in the debug console.** It exists only at DEBUG level in the log file today. A crashing adapter should show its stderr where the user is looking.

### Current vs. Expected behavior


## Current behavior

The adapter exits on the first incoming DBGp packet. Zed logs `Debugger closed the connection` and the session vanishes with no error in the UI. The debug console stays empty even with `"log": true` set.

Xdebug's own log shows a successful connect and a one-sided conversation. It sends `<init>` and receives nothing:

    [Step Debug] INFO: Connected to debugging client: host.lima.internal:9003
    [Step Debug] -> <init ... fileuri="file:///srv/www/united-dqk/active/public/index.php" ...>
    Log closed


## Expected behavior

Either the session attaches and stops on the verified breakpoints, or, if the adapter install is incomplete, a visible error naming the cause.

## Why this was hard to diagnose

Every observable signal pointed at a working setup. The listener bound correctly, the guest reached it (`nc` to 192.168.5.2:9003 succeeded from inside the VM), and path mappings resolved with all three breakpoints returning `verified: true`. The failure looked like a networking or path-mapping problem for a long time before the stack trace surfaced.

### Zed version and system specs
 
- Zed 1.18.1 (bebe92f469834a287f5a57ed78e8d51a918b8ada)
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04
- PHP extension 0.5.3, adapter Xdebug_v1.40.1
- Node v24.11.0 (per adapter stderr)
- Xdebug 3.5.3 / PHP 8.3.33 running in a Lima VM, Zed listens on the host
- The same project and VM debug fine from Zed on macOS

### Attach Zed log file

<details><summary>
Zed.log

Relevant excerpt below: the DAP handshake succeeds, then stderr arrives at the moment of connection. These stderr lines are recorded only at DEBUG level and never reach the debug console.
</summary>

<!-- Paste your log inside the code block. -->
```log
    INFO  [dap::transport] Debug adapter has connected to TCP server 127.0.0.1:35207
    DEBUG [dap::client] Client 0 received response for: `setBreakpoints` sequence_id: 3
      response: ... "breakpoints": [{"verified": true, "line": 40, ...}]
    DEBUG [dap::client] Client 0 received response for: `configurationDone` sequence_id: 6
    ...
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr: Error: Cannot find module '../encodings'
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr: Require stack:
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr: - .../Xdebug_v1.40.1/extension/node_modules/iconv-lite/lib/index.js
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr: - .../Xdebug_v1.40.1/extension/out/xdebugConnection.js
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr: - .../Xdebug_v1.40.1/extension/out/phpDebug.js
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr:     at Object.getCodec (.../iconv-lite/lib/index.js:63:27)
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr:     at Object.getDecoder (.../iconv-lite/lib/index.js:125:23) {
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr:   code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr: }
    DEBUG [dap::transport] stderr: Node.js v24.11.0
    INFO  [dap::transport] Debugger closed the connection
```

</details>

        "request": "launch",
        "port": 9003,
        "log": true,
        "pathMappings": {
          "/path/on/lima": "$ZED_WORKTREE_ROOT"
        }
      }
    ]
```

    xdebug.mode = debug
    xdebug.client_host = host.lima.internal
    xdebug.client_port = 9003
</details>

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

### Disclaimer

This issue wrote by AI after I feed it with my LLAMA.CPP log and 2 full requests (I cant share here), I read the issue body and its accurate and should be valid to look to

### Summary

The Zed Agent changes its system prompt between consecutive requests, causing llama.cpp to lose the reusable prompt prefix and re-evaluate the entire ~146K-token context.

### Evidence

Request `103520` completed with:

```text
n_tokens = 146087
truncated = 0
```

Normally, subsequent requests reuse the cached prefix:

```text
selected slot by LCP similarity
f_sim_best = 0.995 ... 0.999
```

The very next request, `104401`, instead reported:

```text
selected slot by LRU
```

and then processed the entire prompt:

```text
n_tokens = 146283
```

with:

```text
prompt eval time = 79442.93 ms / 146287 tokens
```

This turned an incremental request into a ~79-second full prompt evaluation.

### Diagnosis

I compared the two request payloads sent by Zed.

The **system message is different between `103520` and `104401`**. It changes at the beginning of the serialized prompt, and the system prompt is approximately 761 characters / 196 tokens larger in `104401`.

Among the changes are additional instructions describing the current coding context, including instructions about the project's crates and generated syscall wrappers. For example, the later request contains additional instructions along the lines of:

```text
Syscall wrappers are generated, not hand-written...
sys! macro...
FreeBSD amd64...
rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8/r9...
```

These are not present in the previous request's system prompt.

The important point is **not what these particular instructions say**. The important point is that Zed changed the system prompt itself between two consecutive requests.

Because this change occurs at the beginning of the prompt:

```text
Request 103520:
[system prompt A][conversation...]
        ↓
    cached KV


Request 104401:
[system prompt B][conversation...]
^ system prompt differs
        ↓
   LCP cache cannot reuse the previous prefix
        ↓
     LRU slot selected
        ↓
full ~146K-token prompt evaluation
```

### This is not a context-limit issue

The configured context limit is ~174K tokens, while the affected request is only ~146K tokens.

llama.cpp also reports:

```text
truncated = 0
```

So there is no context overflow or context shift involved.

### Expected behavior

When the agent configuration and system instructions have not changed, consecutive requests should produce a stable, token-identical system prompt so llama.cpp can reuse the existing KV/prompt cache.

If Zed needs to add dynamic information to the agent context, it should avoid unnecessarily modifying the beginning of the cacheable prompt.

### What needs investigation

Please investigate **why the system prompt generated by Zed changes between these two consecutive requests**.

In particular, it would be useful to determine:

* What code/path adds the additional coding-context instructions to the system prompt.
* Why those instructions are present in request `104401` but not in `103520`.
* Whether the system prompt is being regenerated unnecessarily on each request.
* Whether dynamic agent context can be moved after the stable/cacheable portion of the prompt.
* Whether Zed can preserve a stable system-prompt prefix across requests.

Logging a hash/diff of the final serialized system prompt between consecutive requests would also make this type of cache invalidation easy to diagnose.

### Impact

With a ~146K-token context, changing the system prompt invalidates the existing cached prefix and causes llama.cpp to re-evaluate the entire context, adding approximately **79 seconds** of latency.

The following request returns to normal LCP-based cache reuse, indicating that the llama.cpp KV cache itself is working correctly; the problem is the changed prompt prefix.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

Cache hit, but get a huge Cache miss. this bug happens a lot. like every 7-12 request i get a cache miss.

Zed: v1.18.0+stable (Zed) 
OS: Linux Wayland cachyos
Memory: 62.7 GiB
Architecture: x86_64
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 || NVIDIA || 610.57.04

The Zed Agent changes its system prompt between consecutive requests, causing llama.cpp to lose the reusable prompt prefix and re-evaluate the entire ~146K-token context.

### Evidence

Request `103520` completed with:

```text
n_tokens = 146087

Normally, subsequent requests reuse the cached prefix:

```text
selected slot by LCP similarity
f_sim_best = 0.995 ... 0.999

The very next request, `104401`, instead reported:

```text

```

and then processed the entire prompt:

```text
n_tokens = 146283
```

with:

```text
prompt eval time = 79442.93 ms / 146287 tokens
```

This turned an incremental request into a ~79-second full prompt evaluation.

### Diagnosis

I compared the two request payloads sent by Zed.

The **system message is different between `103520` and `104401`**. It changes at the beginning of the serialized prompt, and the system prompt is approximately 761 characters / 196 tokens larger in `104401`.

Among the changes are additional instructions describing the current coding context, including instructions about the project's crates and generated syscall wrappers. For example, the later request contains additional instructions along the lines of:

```text
Syscall wrappers are generated, not hand-written...
sys! macro...
FreeBSD amd64...
rdi/rsi/rdx/r10/r8/r9...
```

These are not present in the previous request's system prompt.

The important point is **not what these particular instructions say**. The important point is that Zed changed the system prompt itself between two consecutive requests.

Because this change occurs at the beginning of the prompt:

```text
Request 103520:
[system prompt A][conversation...]
        ↓
    cached KV


Request 104401:
[system prompt B][conversation...]
^ system prompt differs
        ↓
   LCP cache cannot reuse the previous prefix
        ↓
     LRU slot selected
        ↓
full ~146K-token prompt evaluation
```

### This is not a context-limit issue

The configured context limit is ~174K tokens, while the affected request is only ~146K tokens.

llama.cpp also reports:

```text
truncated = 0
```

So there is no context overflow or context shift involved.

### Expected behavior

When the agent configuration and system instructions have not changed, consecutive requests should produce a stable, token-identical system prompt so llama.cpp can reuse the existing KV/prompt cache.

If Zed needs to add dynamic information to the agent context, it should avoid unnecessarily modifying the beginning of the cacheable prompt.

### What needs investigation

Please investigate **why the system prompt generated by Zed changes between these two consecutive requests**.

In particular, it would be useful to determine:

* What code/path adds the additional coding-context instructions to the system prompt.
* Why those instructions are present in request `104401` but not in `103520`.
* Whether the system prompt is being regenerated unnecessarily on each request.
* Whether dynamic agent context can be moved after the stable/cacheable portion of the prompt.
* Whether Zed can preserve a stable system-prompt prefix across requests.

Logging a hash/diff of the final serialized system prompt between consecutive requests would also make this type of cache invalidation easy to diagnose.

### Impact

With a ~146K-token context, changing the system prompt invalidates the existing cached prefix and causes llama.cpp to re-evaluate the entire context, adding approximately **79 seconds** of latency.

The following request returns to normal LCP-based cache reuse, indicating that the llama.cpp KV cache itself is working correctly; the problem is the changed prompt prefix.

body_text: ### Reproduction steps 1. Start Zed 2. Open Zed's integrated terminal 3. Paste and run the commands: ```printf '\033]4;16;rgb:cb/c0/ff\033\\'``` ```printf '\033[38;5;16mThis should be light purple\033[0m\n'``` 4. The output text should be light purple but is a different color ### Current vs. Expected behavior I use Hyprland with the Caelestia shell and Fish. Caelestia dynamically configures terminal colors by emitting OSC escape sequences, including OSC 4 palette redefinitions. The same Fish configuration works correctly in my external terminal and in VS Code’s integrated terminal. In Zed’s integrated terminal, applications that use the redefined extended ANSI palette entries fall back to incorrect/default colors. Zed uses the theme colors to set the ANSI colors. But not all colors are accessible through Zed's themes. There should be an option to use the terminal application’s own palette instead of Zed's theme. Or the other ANSI colors should be accessible through the themes. ### Zed version and system specs Zed 1.18.1 bebe92f469834a287f5a57ed78e8d51a918b8ada ### System NAME="CachyOS Linux" PRETTY_NAME="CachyOS" ID=cachyos ID_LIKE=arch BUILD_ID=rolling ANSI_COLOR="38;2;23;147;209" HOME_URL="https://cachyos.org/" DOCUMENTATION_URL="https://wiki.cachyos.org/" Linux 7.2.2-1-cachyos x86_64 GNU/Linux ### Session XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Hyprland XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP=Hyprland ### GPU 00:02.0 VGA compatible controller: Intel Corporation TigerLake-LP GT2 [Iris Xe Graphics] (rev 01) ### Zed integrated terminal environment TERM=xterm-kitty COLORTERM=truecolor TERM_PROGRAM= SHELL=/bin/fish ### Attach Zed log file _No response_ ### Relevant Zed settings ### Relevant Keymap _No response_ ### (for AI issues) Model provider details _No response_ ### If you are using WSL on Windows, what flavor of Linux are you using? body_text:
### Summary

On Zed 1.18 stable, a language declared by an extension with a **multi-segment (compound) `path_suffixes` entry** (e.g. `"excalidraw.svg"`) attaches to matching buffers (the status bar shows the language name), but Zed **never routes `textDocument/didOpen` for those buffers to the extension's language server**. Single-segment suffixes (e.g. `"excalidraw"`, `"svg"`) work: every open of a matching file delivers `didOpen`.

### Description

While building an extension that previews `.excalidraw` / `.excalidraw.svg` / `.excalidraw.png` files via a fake language server (`excalidraw-preview --lsp`), I interposed a logging wrapper between Zed and the language server to capture all LSP traffic.

With the language configured as:

```toml
path_suffixes = ["excalidraw", "excalidraw.svg", "excalidraw.png"]
```

…a session alternating 7 single-clicks on `lifecycle.excalidraw` and 7 single-clicks on `compose-pipeline.excalidraw.svg` produced:

- **7/7** `textDocument/didOpen` for every click on `lifecycle.excalidraw` (single-segment suffix),
- **0/7** `textDocument/didOpen` for every click on `compose-pipeline.excalidraw.svg` (compound suffix) — while the buffer demonstrably opened: each `.svg` click displaced the previously focused preview-tab buffer, recorded by the interleaved `didClose` of the `.excalidraw` buffer. No message in the entire session named the `.excalidraw.svg` URI.
- The status bar showed language `Excalidraw` for the `.excalidraw.svg` buffer, so the *language attached* — only the `didOpen` routing to the language server was missing.

### Interpretation

Single-segment suffixes route through an exact-match path (`find_by_name_or_extension` in `crates/language/src/language_registry/available_languages.rs`: `suffix == string`) which demonstrably delivers `didOpen`. The full matcher (`find_for_file`) *also* matches compound suffixes via the filename candidate — which is why the language attaches — but that match never translates into buffer registration with the language server. I did not pin the exact diverging call site (hypothesis: the buffer-subscription path uses the exact-match lookup, or the async language-load race skips `set_language_for_buffer` → `register_buffer_with_language_servers`).

### Minimal reproduction

Independent of my extension:

1. Scaffold a minimal Zed extension with two languages:
   - language `compound-repro-a`: `path_suffixes = ["repro"]`
   - language `compound-repro-b`: `path_suffixes = ["repro.svg"]`
   - a language server `[language_servers.repro-dummy]` mapped to both languages; the server can be any program that reads LSP frames on stdin and answers `initialize` with minimal capabilities (`openClose: true`).
2. Install it via `zed: install dev extension`.
3. Point the language-server command at a wrapper that tees stdin to a log (so you can see what Zed actually sends).
4. In a workspace, create `a.repro` and `b.repro.svg`. Single-click each file several times in turn.
5. **Actual:** `a.repro` clicks produce `textDocument/didOpen` every time; `b.repro.svg` clicks produce none (the buffer opens — visible via the `didClose` of the displaced preview-tab buffer — but no `didOpen` is ever sent, and no message names the `b.repro.svg` URI).
6. **Control:** repeat with single-segment suffixes for both languages — `didOpen` is delivered for both.

### Environment

- Zed: `1.18.0+stable.351` (evidence capture), still reproducing per investigation on `1.18.x`
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Extension-declared languages with compound `path_suffixes`

### Details

I worked around this by claiming only single-segment suffixes and filtering by filename inside the language server, so this is not blocking me — but either compound suffixes should deliver buffer events like single-segment ones, or declaring them should be documented/rejected, because the current behavior silently breaks extension language servers for compound-suffixed files.

{"repository": "zed-industries/zed", "task_candidate_id": 26556, "repository_id": 319, "issue_number": 63831, "github_issue_id": 5363077064, "html_url": "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/63831", "created_at": "2026-09-06T05:22:13+00:00", "author_association": null, "title": "Extension language with compound path_suffixes (e.g. "excalidraw.svg") attaches to buffers but never receives textDocument/didOpen", "body_text": "### Summary

On Zed 1.18 stable, a language declared by an extension with a **multi-segment (compound) `path_suffixes` entry** (e.g. `"excalidraw.svg"`) attaches to matching buffers (the status bar shows the language name), but Zed **never routes `textDocument/didOpen` for those buffers to the extension's language server**. Single-segment suffixes (e.g. `"excalidraw"`, `"svg"`) work: every open of a matching file delivers `didOpen`.

### Description

While building an extension that previews `.excalidraw` / `.excalidraw.svg` / `.excalidraw.png` files via a fake language server (`excalidraw-preview --lsp`), I interposed a logging wrapper between Zed and the language server to capture all LSP traffic.

With the language configured as:

```toml
path_suffixes = ["excalidraw", "excalidraw.svg", "excalidraw.png"]
```

…a session alternating 7 single-clicks on `lifecycle.excalidraw` and 7 single-clicks on `compose-pipeline.excalidraw.svg` produced:

- **7/7** `textDocument/didOpen` for every click on `lifecycle.excalidraw` (single-segment suffix),
- **0/7** `textDocument/didOpen` for every click on `compose-pipeline.excalidraw.svg` (compound suffix) — while the buffer demonstrably opened: each `.svg` click displaced the previously focused preview-tab buffer, recorded by the interleaved `didClose` of the `.excalidraw` buffer. No message in the entire session named the `.excalidraw.svg` URI.
- The status bar showed language `Excalidraw` for the `.excalidraw.svg` buffer, so the *language attached* — only the `didOpen` routing to the language server was missing.

### Interpretation

Single-segment suffixes route through an exact-match path (`find_by_name_or_extension` in `crates/language/src/language_registry/available_languages.rs`: `suffix == string`) which demonstrably delivers `didOpen`. The full matcher (`find_for_file`) *also* matches compound suffixes via the filename candidate — which is why the language attaches — but that match never translates into buffer registration with the language server. I did not pin the exact diverging call site (hypothesis: the buffer-subscription path uses the exact-match lookup, or the async language-load race skips `set_language_for_buffer` → `register_buffer_with_language_servers`).

### Minimal reproduction

Independent of my extension:

1. Scaffold a minimal Zed extension with two languages:
   - language `compound-repro-a`: `path_suffixes = ["repro"]`
   - language `compound-repro-b`: `path_suffixes = ["repro.svg"]`
   - a language server `[language_servers.repro-dummy]` mapped to both languages; the server can be any program that reads LSP frames on stdin and answers `initialize` with minimal capabilities (`openClose: true`).
2. Install it via `zed: install dev extension`.
3. Point the language-server command at a wrapper that tees stdin to a log (so you can see what Zed actually sends).
4. In a workspace, create `a.repro` and `b.repro.svg`. Single-click each file several times in turn.
5. **Actual:** `a.repro` clicks produce `textDocument/didOpen` every time; `b.repro.svg` clicks produce none (the buffer opens — visible via the `didClose` of the displaced preview-tab buffer — but no `didOpen` is ever sent, and no message names the `b.repro.svg` URI).
6. **Control:** repeat with single-segment suffixes for both languages — `didOpen` is delivered for both.

### Environment

- Zed: `1.18.0+stable.351` (evidence capture), still reproducing per investigation on `1.18.x`
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Extension-declared languages with compound `path_suffixes`

### Details

I worked around this by claiming only single-segment suffixes and filtering by filename inside the language server, so this is not blocking me — but either compound suffixes should deliver buffer events like single-segment ones, or declaring them should be documented/rejected, because the current behavior silently breaks extension language servers for compound-suffixed files.

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed (tested with Helix Mode).
2. Open a center terminal.
3. Go into Vim/Helix Mode via `Ctrl+Shift+Space`.
4. Press `:` for commands or `Space+P` for files or `Space+B` for buffers.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Current behavior

Nothing happens on Zed site.

### Expected behavior

The command/files/buffer dialog opens just as in an editor buffer.

### Additional information

I tested a bit more and it seems that the Vim mode in the terminal is really a _vim_ mode with just navigation (so no Helix behavior at all). Is that the reason that the hotkeys don't work? Although `:` is a hotkey in Vim as well as in Helix so it should work in both modes.

I would have expected that the vim mode functions like in the integrated terminal of Neovim, i.e. with this hotkey the editor sees the whole terminal window just as a "real only" file buffer, with all the possibilities of navigation and selections (e.g. pressing `space-y` (Helix) or `yy` (Vim) also seem to not pasting the current terminal line into a selection that you can insert in another editor pane, or the virtual selection mode does not work, or pasting an already made selection in the terminal with `p` also doesn't work).

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: 0.18.1
OS: Tested on Gentoo Linux and Windows

### Relevant Zed settings

Helix mode is activated.

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Install an extension that uses [a big tree-sitter grammar](https://github.com/usagi-coffee/tree-sitter-abl)
2. Zed will error out with: `ERROR [language::language_registry] failed to load language OpenEdge ABL:  Failed to instantiate Wasm module: invalid memory size 72046592`

This happens because Zed has a parser pool that reuses WasmStore instances across grammar loads. A large valid grammar can fail when loaded into the store that already contains other grammars. The failure is invalid memory size originating from [tree-sitter's fixed 128MIB WasmStore limit](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/blob/master/lib/src/wasm_store.c#L185). 

The simplest(?) solution would be to not-reuse the stores but I don't know how to approach that issue i.e is it upstream tree-sitter size limit being too small or it's Zed at fault for reusing the wasm stores.

This kind of depends on #63816 because without this patch the grammar won't compile via Install Dev Zed Extension at all - LLVM performance issue that got fixed in 23.1.

[Extension if you want to test it yourself](https://github.com/usagi-coffee/zed-openedge-abl) - keep in mind the compilation takes a very long time due to upstream issue in wasm-opt and needs `wasi-sdk` 34, you also need to have other languages installed as it's about sharing the store.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: `ERROR [language::language_registry] failed to load language OpenEdge ABL:  Failed to instantiate Wasm module: invalid memory size 72046592`.

Expected: loads the grammar successfully.

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed
2. `agent: new thread`
3. Select OpenRouter model (e.g., Gemini Flash 3.8 or Muse Spark 1.3)
4. Enter LLM command
5. Get error:



### Current vs. Expected behavior

```
Free Usage Exceeded
You reached your free usage limit. Upgrade to Zed Pro for more prompts.
```

I confirmed that the openrouter.ai model is being used. Not only does the zed interface say so, but if you look at the OpenRouter dashboard, I even occasionally (about 50% of the time) get charged even when the prompt doesn't come through. 

I also tried to disable all edit predictions in case it was pertaining to edit predictions. 

Perhaps Zed has updated its pricing policy to not include BYOK in free plans. But the various marketing pages still show Free plans include BYOK: https://zed.dev/docs/account/plans-and-pricing

Even if the policy changes, this would still be a bug because the quota should get called before and block OpenRouter billing requests. Otherwise, the request is charged to the user (by OpenRouter) but no response comes back.

### Summary

Zed 1.18.1 stable on Windows 11. Three symptoms that look like one disease family in the agent's SQLite-backed state layer:

1. **Tool-approval grants do not persist.** Choosing "Always" for a tool re-prompts after a session collapse/restart; during live agent turns the log fills with `Sqlite call failed with code 5 "database is locked"` from the agent state store.
2. **Thread-history sidebar registry drifts from the store.** `sidebar_threads` in the workspace DB holds fewer rows than the actual `threads` table; the history UI renders empty/stale even though all threads (including large ones) are intact in `threads.db`. This is ongoing drift, not a one-off: registry count increased while threads kept accumulating.
3. **Crash-handler stubs are 0-byte.** `zed-crash-handler-*` files are created but empty (no readable payload), so nothing is being captured/reported; there were also several hang miniprofiles the same day.

### Environment

- Zed **1.18.1** stable (Windows x64, `AppData\Local\Programs\Zed`), Windows 11
- Single worktree, agent panel (native agent), DeepSeek via OpenAI-compatible provider
- `agent.tool_permissions` configured (verified current against the 1.18.1 binary; migrator `crates/migrator/src/migrations/m_2025_11_20/settings.rs` present — this is not a config-shape issue)

### Receipt 1 — SQLITE_BUSY grant drops (approval amnesia)

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Zed\logs\Zed.log`, during an active agent turn (multiple repeats within the same second):

```
ERROR [crates/agent/src/agent.rs:1830] Sqlite call failed with code 5 and message: Some("database is locked")
```

The agent's per-session grant/state writes hit SQLITE_BUSY and appear to be dropped without retry. Symptom from the user's side: "Always" approvals never survive across sessions; nearly every tool call re-prompts. Correlated with the crash/hang storm the same day (Receipt 3) which also resets in-memory grant state.

Store layout (read-only inspection of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Zed\db\0-stable\db.sqlite`, WAL mode): no grant/permission table exists at the `kv_store`/`scoped_kv_store` layer, consistent with grants living in per-session agent state that is failing to persist under lock contention.

### Receipt 2 — Thread-history registry drift (61 vs 46)

- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Zed\threads\threads.db` → `threads` table: **61 rows** (id, summary, updated_at, data_type, data, parent_id, folder_paths…). Data blobs intact — including a 1.1 MB active session.
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Zed\db\0-stable\db.sqlite` → `sidebar_threads`: **46 rows / 46 distinct thread_id**.
- History UI (Ctrl+Alt+J / agent panel thread list) shows empty or stale entries while the store holds everything; earlier in the same day the registry showed 42 rows vs 57+ in the store, i.e. the gap grows as threads accumulate. Sidebar rows for new/current sessions are not being written or rendered.

### Receipt 3 — 0-byte crash-handler stubs + hang miniprofiles

All `zed-crash-handler-*` files are **0 bytes** (names carry PIDs). Eleven stubs in the last week: nine clustered **2026-08-30 21:28–22:14 local** (46-minute storm), plus 2026-09-05 16:38 and 2026-09-06 13:27. Same-day hang miniprofiles (`hang_traces\hang-2026-09-06_*.miniprof.json`, 534–802 B): 14:45, 17:54, 22:17×2.

Empty crash stubs suggest reports are not being captured or uploaded (telemetry enabled in settings), which makes these events invisible in crash telemetry.

### Expected behavior

- SQLite busy → retry/queue agent state writes (or use a dedicated connection / `busy_timeout`), never silently drop grant or registry writes.
- `sidebar_threads` registry stays in sync with `threads.db`.
- Crash handler writes a readable report payload (not 0 bytes).

### Repro notes

1. Run two agent sessions against the same worktree (or one active session under load) and watch `Zed.log` for repeated `agent.rs:1830 ... database is locked`; grant an "Always" permission, let the session crash/restart, observe the grant is gone.
2. Compare `threads.db` (`threads` table) row count vs `db/0-stable/db.sqlite` (`sidebar_threads`) row count after a day of agent sessions; open the thread-history UI and observe stale/empty rows for sessions present in the store.

Happy to attach full file listings or run any instrumented build/probe you suggest.

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

No deterministic repro. Occurred 4 times in ~3.5 hours on 2026-09-07, in one project, using the bundled Claude agent (ACP) in the agent panel.

1. Open a Claude Code thread in the agent panel.
2. Work normally (prompts, tool calls).
3. At some point the thread stops producing output entirely and never recovers.
4. Interrupting does **not** return control. After Zed's cancel floor elapses it logs `cancel floor elapsed without the SDK yielding; forcing "cancelled"` and the session is unusable — a new thread is required.

In one of the four cases the thread wedged on the **very first request of a fresh session**, before any tool call was made.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the thread silently stops. The agent panel just looks idle — there is no error, no indication anything is wrong. The only signal is a `WARN` line in `Zed.log`. In the three cases I timed, I waited 11, 25 and 31 minutes before realising the session was dead.

**Expected:** when the cancel floor elapses and the SDK has not yielded, surface it in the agent panel UI (the log already says "a new session may be required" — that message should reach the user, not just the log file).

#### Log evidence

```log
2026-09-07T11:52:59+09:00 WARN [agent_servers::acp] agent stderr: Session 470e4a12-…: cancel floor elapsed without the SDK yielding; forcing "cancelled". The underlying query may still be wedged — a new session may be required.
2026-09-07T13:23:12+09:00 WARN [agent_servers::acp] agent stderr: Session 7b5fc1d5-…: cancel floor elapsed without the SDK yielding; forcing "cancelled". …
2026-09-07T14:00:27+09:00 WARN [agent_servers::acp] agent stderr: Session f3e13657-…: cancel floor elapsed without the SDK yielding; forcing "cancelled". …
2026-09-07T14:00:46+09:00 ERROR [gpui::app] timed out waiting on app_will_quit
2026-09-07T14:03:27+09:00 INFO  [zed] ========== starting zed version 1.18.1+stable.352.bebe92f ==========
```

Zed had to be force-quit and restarted at 14:03.

#### Transcript evidence

The Claude Code session transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl`) all end mid-turn. The last record is a `user` entry (a prompt or a `tool_result`), with **no following `assistant` entry and no error record** — i.e. the request was sent and nothing ever came back:

| Session | last transcript entry | forced cancel |
|---|---|---|
| `470e4a12` | 11:41:16 — `tool_result` of a `Skill` call | 11:52:59 |
| `7b5fc1d5` | 12:57:40 — `tool_result` of an MCP call | 13:23:12 |
| `495c171b` | 13:45:21 — `tool_result` of a `Bash` call | (lost to the restart) |
| `f3e13657` | 13:29:31 — the initial user prompt, **before any tool call** | 14:00:27 |

#### What I ruled out (checked against the actual data, not assumed)

- **Not an API failure.** The only API error on this machine that day was in an unrelated non-ACP `sdk-cli` session, which *did* record `API Error: The response stopped arriving`. The wedged ACP sessions record no error at all. No 429/529 in any transcript that day.
- **Not memory pressure.** 192 GB RAM, `vm.swapusage` 0.00 MB throughout, zero jetsam/memorystatus events in `log show`. Zed sat at ~18 GB resident.
- **Not a specific MCP server or tool.** Two of the four were doing MCP work, but one wedged on a plain `Bash` result and one on a fresh session with no tool calls at all.
- **Not hooks.** Every hook attachment in the transcripts reports `exitCode: 0`.
- **Not the CLI.** The same machine ran the `claude` CLI directly (v2.1.263) the same day with 0 occurrences.

The only common factor is that all four were Zed ACP sessions.

#### Possibly relevant: the SDK version is hard-pinned

`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.75.1` pins `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` to exactly `"0.3.257"` (no range), so users cannot pick up SDK fixes by refreshing the agent registry — the pin has to be bumped in the ACP package. npm latest was `0.3.263` at the time of writing.

I manually replaced the SDK in `~/Library/Application Support/Zed/external_agents/registry/npx/claude-acp/node_modules/` with 0.3.263 and the ACP handshake still works (verified with a stdio `initialize` request, agent responds normally), but the change is reverted whenever Zed re-fetches the registry. I can't say yet whether it changes the wedge frequency.

#### Related but distinct

#62788 / #52782 / #56135 describe permission requests that Zed fails to render. Those are a different failure mode: there, interrupting the thread returns control and the tool call resolves as "denied". Here, interrupting does **not** return control — the SDK never yields, and the session stays wedged. Two of my four cases also involved no permission-eligible tool call at all.

### Zed version and system specs

- Zed: 1.18.1+stable.352.bebe92f469834a287f5a57ed78e8d51a918b8ada
- macOS, Darwin 25.6.0 (arm64), 192 GB RAM
- `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.75.1
- `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.257 (pinned)

### Attach Zed log file

<details><summary>Zed.log (relevant lines)</summary>

```log
2026-09-07T11:40:59+09:00 WARN [agent_servers::acp] agent stderr: [session/create] sessionId=470e4a12-… phase=register durationMs=0 totalMs=789
2026-09-07T11:52:59+09:00 WARN [agent_servers::acp] agent stderr: Session 470e4a12-…: cancel floor elapsed without the SDK yielding; forcing "cancelled". The underlying query may still be wedged — a new session may be required.
2026-09-07T13:23:12+09:00 WARN [agent_servers::acp] agent stderr: Session 7b5fc1d5-…: cancel floor elapsed without the SDK yielding; forcing "cancelled". The underlying query may still be wedged — a new session may be required.
2026-09-07T14:00:27+09:00 WARN [agent_servers::acp] agent stderr: Session f3e13657-…: cancel floor elapsed without the SDK yielding; forcing "cancelled". The underlying query may still be wedged — a new session may be required.
2026-09-07T14:00:46+09:00 ERROR [gpui::app] timed out waiting on app_will_quit
```

</details>

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Add an OpenAI-compatible provider named `Groq` in `settings.json` with `api_url: https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` and two models: `openai/gpt-oss-120b` and `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`.
2. Set `agent.default_model` to `openai_compatible:Groq` / `openai/gpt-oss-120b`.
3. Set `agent.inline_assistant_model` to `openai_compatible:Groq` / `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`.
4. Enter the Groq API key via Agent Settings → LLM Providers → Groq (stored in system keychain).
5. Restart Zed.
6. Open the Agent Panel and send a prompt → **works correctly**, response streams from Groq.
7. In any file, select a line of text and press `Ctrl+Enter` to invoke the Inline Assistant.
8. **Result:** the popup displays "LLM provider is not configured or does not support the configured model." No request is sent to Groq (confirmed via Zed.log — no HTTP call is made for the Inline Assistant).
9. Setting `"inline_assistant_use_streaming_tools": false` and `"enable_thinking": false` does not resolve the issue.
10. Adding `"reasoning_effort": "none"` to the model config makes Groq reject the request with: `reasoning_effort must be one of low, medium, or high` (Groq does not accept "none").

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior:**
The Agent Panel works perfectly with the `openai_compatible:Groq` provider: requests are sent and responses are received. However, the Inline Assistant (Ctrl+Enter) immediately shows "LLM provider is not configured or does not support the configured model" without making any API call. Zed.log shows no HTTP request when the Inline Assistant is triggered.

**Expected behavior:**
Per the docs ("If you have already set up an LLM provider to interact with the Agent Panel, then that will also work for the Inline Assistant"), the Inline Assistant should use the same working provider and model. Selecting text and pressing Ctrl+Enter should send a request to Groq and display the AI-generated edit inline.

**Additional context:**
- The Agent Panel successfully authenticates and communicates with Groq (log shows `Thread::send called with model: GPT-OSS 120B (Groq)`).
- No corresponding log entry appears when triggering the Inline Assistant, suggesting Zed rejects the provider/model pair before any network call.
- Occurs on Linux with Zed 1.18.1 stable.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: v1.18.1 (Zed bebe92f469834a287f5a57ed78e8d51a918b8ada)
OS: Linux (Debian, kernel 7.2.3-4-liquorix-amd64, Wayland)
Memory: N/A
Architecture: x86_64
GPU: AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR), Mesa 22.3.6, Vulkan backend

```log

2026-09-07T11:50:14+02:00 INFO  [agent::thread] Thread::send called with model: GPT-OSS 120B (Groq)
2026-09-07T11:48:05+02:00 ERROR [agent::thread] Turn execution failed: `reasoning_effort` must be one of `low`, `medium`, or `high`
```

**Note:** when triggering the Inline Assistant (Ctrl+Enter), NO log entry appears. The error is shown in the UI but nothing is logged, suggesting the provider lookup fails silently before any network call.

### Reproduction steps

1. Run Zed on Linux/Wayland.
2. Open the integrated terminal.
3. Add this keymap entry:

```json
[
  {
    "context": "Terminal",
    "bindings": {
      "super-c": "terminal::Copy",
      "super-v": "terminal::Paste"
    }
  }
]
```

4. Copy text to the clipboard from another application.
5. Focus the integrated terminal and press `Super+V`.

### Expected behavior

Zed handles `Super+V` as `terminal::Paste` and inserts the clipboard contents into the terminal.

### Actual behavior

The keybinding is not handled by Zed. `Super+V` is forwarded to the shell as `Ctrl+V`, which zsh displays as `^V` (quoted-insert). `Super+C` similarly does not copy a terminal selection.

`Ctrl+Shift+V` and `Ctrl+Shift+C` work as the Linux terminal fallback shortcuts.

### Zed version and system specs

- Zed: `1.16.2`
- OS: Arch Linux
- Session: Wayland
- Desktop: Hyprland
- Omarchy: `4.0.2-1`
- Shell: zsh
- Base keymap: JetBrains

### Relevant keymap

The complete current terminal keymap is:

```json
[
  {
    "context": "Terminal",
    "bindings": {
      "super-c": "terminal::Copy",
      "super-v": "terminal::Paste",
      "ctrl-shift-c": "terminal::Copy",
      "ctrl-shift-v": "terminal::Paste"
    }
  }
]
```

The `super-` modifier is documented as the Linux Super key modifier. Restarting Zed does not change the behavior.

body_text:
## Summary

Extension detail pages on `zed.dev` can continue showing an older release after the newer version is available through `api.zed.dev`.

Multiple extension detail pages appear affected. Stylelint  concrete example: the API contains **3.2.0**, published September 7, 2026, while its detail page still shows **3.1.0**.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Query the [Stylelint API endpoint](https://api.zed.dev/extensions/stylelint) and inspect the published 3.2.0 record:

   ```sh
   curl --fail --silent --show-error 'https://api.zed.dev/extensions/stylelint' |
     jq '.data[] | select(.version == "3.2.0") | {id, version, published_at}'
   ```

2. Open [Stylelint's extension detail page](https://zed.dev/extensions/stylelint).
3. Compare its displayed version and last-updated date with the API record.

## Current vs Expected Behavior

**Current:** The API reports Stylelint 3.2.0, but the website displays 3.1.0 and an August 28, 2026 update date.

**Expected:** Once a release is available through the extension API, the corresponding detail page should reflect its version and publication date within a defined refresh interval, without requiring a website deployment or manual intervention.

## Zed version and system specs

Not applicable to the Zed editor
## Evidence/Examples

Observed September 8, 2026:

| Field | [Extension API](https://api.zed.dev/extensions/stylelint) | [Extension detail page](https://zed.dev/extensions/stylelint) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Version | 3.2.0 | 3.1.0 |
| Publication / last-updated date | `2026-09-07T14:48:44Z` | August 28, 2026 |

The original capture also showed **61,611 downloads in the API** versus **60,262 on the detail page**. These counts are a snapshot and change over time. The mismatch across several fields is consistent with an older cached record, although it does not establish the cause.

The API response confirms that the newer version is already available from the registry. Other detail pages appear to show similar staleness. Stylelint is the documented reproduction here.

## Likely Cause / Infrastructure Clue

Missing or ineffective cache/tag/path revalidation after extension publication is a plausible explanation.  The `zed.dev` application source is private, so its cache configuration and any internal refresh hooks cannot be confirmed from the public repositories.

There is relevant precedent in [PR #59422](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/59422/files), merged June 16, 2026. It replaced a full website redeployment after Zed releases with an authenticated request to `https://zed.dev/api/revalidate?tag=releases`.

The public [extension CI workflow](https://github.com/zed-industries/extensions/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs extension packaging with publication enabled on `main` and S3 credentials, but contains no obvious explicit `zed.dev` revalidation step.  refresh logic elsewhere could be the problem though and still don't know which tag or path extension pages use.

## Related Issues/PRs

- [#59422 — ci: Revalidate zed.dev after release](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/59422): precedent for explicitly refreshing website data after publication.
- [#58837 — Hosted theme schema (zed.dev/schema/themes/v0.2.0.json) is stale](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/58837): a related stale resource on the website.
- [#43837 — Built-in extensions still appear on the website, but can't be installed and don't appear when searching for Extensions](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/43837): extension pages persisting after extensions became built-ins.
- [#43079 — Different results while searching for extensions, website vs Zed app](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/43079): another website/app inconsistency, involving search behavior rather than evidence of the same cache defect.

## Suggested Fix

- If invalidation is missing or ineffective, revalidate the appropriate extension tags or paths after the new version is available through the API. Consider a bounded refresh interval as a fallback.

### Reproduction steps

1. Run Zed on macOS.
2. Connect to a native Windows machine using Zed SSH Remote Development and open a project.
3. Start an external Codex agent through https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/codex-acp.
4. Ask Codex to edit a file and include a clickable file reference in its response.
5. Click the file reference in the response.
6. Click “Open Files” in the “Editing files” card.

Example URI, using a fictitious project path:

`file:///C:/example-project/src/example.py`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior:
Both actions do nothing. No file opens, no browser launches, and no error appears in the UI. Clicking the file link produces a “no file found at path” error in the Zed log, although the file exists on the remote Windows machine.

I tested the following comparisons:

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| macOS Zed → Windows over SSH, using Codex through ACP | File navigation fails |
| macOS Zed → the same Windows SSH project, using Zed's built-in Agent | File navigation works |
| Zed running directly on Windows, accessed through RDP, using Codex through ACP | File navigation works |

---

Expected behavior:
File references and “Open Files” should open the corresponding file in the remote project, including the referenced line when available.

---

Possibly related: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/62928
That report describes remote agent file links doing nothing and the same `agent_ui.rs:183` error. Its environment is a Linux dev container, whereas this report concerns a macOS client connected to native Windows over SSH. I have not confirmed whether the underlying cause is identical.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: 1.18.1
Commit: bebe92f469834a287f5a57ed78e8d51a918b8ada
Version: 1.18.1+stable.352.bebe92f469834a287f5a57ed78e8d51a918b8ada

Client OS: macOS
Remote OS: native Windows
Connection: SSH Remote Development

### Reproduction steps

1. Open a project in Zed with a language server enabled, such as TypeScript.
2. Disable the TypeScript language server using the language server menu, or set `"enable_language_server": false` for TypeScript in `.zed/settings.json`.
3. Open the language server menu again.
4. Observe that TypeScript is no longer available to select or re-enable.
5. Open the Command Palette and search for a command to start or enable the TypeScript language server.
6. Observe that there is no command to start that specific language server.
7. Run "Restart Language Servers".
8. Observe that all language servers are restarted, rather than only TypeScript.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Current behaviour

When a language server is disabled, it disappears from the language server menu and cannot be started individually.

### Reproduction steps

1. Open a terminal in Zed.
2. Run a program that turns on mouse reporting and shows a path, for example:
   `echo /etc/hosts > /tmp/zed-link.txt && vim -c 'set mouse=a' /tmp/zed-link.txt`
   (I hit this in Claude Code, a TUI that turns on mouse reporting. The vim command is a minimal equivalent derived from the code path below; htop should behave the same way.)
3. Hold ⌘, then move the pointer onto `/etc/hosts`.
4. Leave the pointer on `/etc/hosts`, release ⌘, and press it again.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** in step 3 the path is not underlined and the pointer stays an I-beam. In step 4, pressing ⌘ while already hovering underlines the path. ⌘-click opens the link in both cases, because `open_links_in_mouse_mode` defaults to `true`. In a plain shell without mouse reporting, ⌘-hover underlines links as expected.

**Expected:** moving onto a link with ⌘ held highlights it in mouse mode too, the same as pressing ⌘ while hovering, and consistent with ⌘-click, which already opens links in mouse mode.

**Cause (from reading the v1.19.2 source):**
- [`Terminal::mouse_move`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/df181c6f58d02677b385fa947d6bfde6d3530078/crates/terminal/src/terminal.rs#L2481-L2514) forwards motion to the PTY when `mouse_mode()` is true, and calls `schedule_find_hyperlink` only in the `else` branch. Motion never triggers a link lookup while the app has mouse reporting on.
- [`Terminal::try_modifiers_change`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/df181c6f58d02677b385fa947d6bfde6d3530078/crates/terminal/src/terminal.rs#L2391-L2398), called from the `ModifiersChangedEvent` listener in [`terminal_element.rs`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/df181c6f58d02677b385fa947d6bfde6d3530078/crates/terminal_view/src/terminal_element.rs#L1665-L1675), calls `schedule_find_hyperlink` without checking `mouse_mode()`.

So whether the link highlights depends on whether the last event was a modifier change or a mouse move.

A possible fix: in the mouse-mode branch of `mouse_move`, also call `schedule_find_hyperlink` when `modifiers.secondary()` is held and `open_links_in_mouse_mode` is enabled.

**Workaround:** hold ⌘⇧ instead of ⌘. Shift bypasses mouse mode, so the link highlights on hover.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: v1.19.2 (Zed)
OS: macOS 26.6.2
Memory: 32 GiB
Architecture: aarch64 (Apple M1 Max)

### Relevant Zed settings

Terminal link settings are at their defaults (`open_links_in_mouse_mode: true`).

body_text:
It seems Zed advertises deleted files to rust-analyzer, breaking its module resolution logic.

### Reproduction steps

1. Create a Rust crate whose `src/lib.rs` contains `mod ast;`, with the module in `src/ast.rs`.
   For example, clone https://github.com/stephanemagnenat/ra-ghost-module and run
   `mv src/ast/mod.rs src/ast.rs && rmdir src/ast`.
2. Open the crate folder in Zed and open `src/ast.rs` and `src/lib.rs` in tabs.
   rust-analyzer reports no diagnostics for `src/lib.rs`.
3. Close the Zed window with these tabs still open.
4. While the window is closed, move the module into a directory:
   `mkdir src/ast && mv src/ast.rs src/ast/mod.rs`.
   This is what refactors, `git checkout`, or coding agents commonly do.
5. Reopen the folder in Zed.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the tab for the no-longer-existing `src/ast.rs` is restored, and Zed sends `textDocument/didOpen` for it to the language servers with empty text, as if an empty file existed at that path. rust-analyzer then resolves `mod ast;` to that empty buffer instead of `src/ast/mod.rs`, so the module disappears: `src/lib.rs` shows "Variable `Error` should have snake_case name", although `cargo check` passes. In bigger projects this causes false diagnostics everywhere (`{unknown}` types, false `E0308` mismatches). Restarting the language server does not help, since the restored tab is announced again.

These tabs accumulate. In a real project, the persisted workspace had 250 Rust editor tabs across three panes, 56 of which pointed to files that no longer exist. On restore, Zed sent `didOpen` with empty text for the missing files (captured with a proxy logging all LSP traffic). Opening only one of them (an empty `src/ast.rs`) reproduced all the false diagnostics; opening all real files without the missing ones gave none.

**Expected:** tabs for files that no longer exist on disk are not restored, or at least they are not announced to language servers as existing documents.

rust-analyzer side of the problem: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#23366 and probably rust-lang/rust-analyzer/issues/19709

### Reproduction steps

1. Create a Rust crate whose `src/lib.rs` contains `mod ast;`, with the module in `src/ast.rs`.
   For example, clone https://github.com/stephanemagnenat/ra-ghost-module and run
   `mv src/ast/mod.rs src/ast.rs && rmdir src/ast`.
2. Open the crate folder in Zed and open `src/ast.rs` and `src/lib.rs` in tabs.
   rust-analyzer reports no diagnostics for `src/lib.rs`.
3. Close the Zed window with these tabs still open.
4. While the window is closed, move the module into a directory:
   `mkdir src/ast && mv src/ast.rs src/ast/mod.rs`.
   This is what refactors, `git checkout`, or coding agents commonly do.
5. Reopen the folder in Zed.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the tab for the no-longer-existing `src/ast.rs` is restored, and Zed sends `textDocument/didOpen` for it to the language servers with empty text, as if an empty file existed at that path. rust-analyzer then resolves `mod ast;` to that empty buffer instead of `src/ast/mod.rs`, so the module disappears: `src/lib.rs` shows "Variable `Error` should have snake_case name", although `cargo check` passes. In bigger projects this causes false diagnostics everywhere (`{unknown}` types, false `E0308` mismatches). Restarting the language server does not help, since the restored tab is announced again.

These tabs accumulate. In a real project, the persisted workspace had 250 Rust editor tabs across three panes, 56 of which pointed to files that no longer exist. On restore, Zed sent `didOpen` with empty text for the missing files (captured with a proxy logging all LSP traffic). Opening only one of them (an empty `src/ast.rs`) reproduced all the false diagnostics; opening all real files without the missing ones gave none.

**Expected:** tabs for files that no longer exist on disk are not restored, or at least they are not announced to language servers as existing documents.

rust-analyzer side of the problem: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#23366 and probably rust-lang/rust-analyzer/issues/19709

### Reproduction steps

1. Install the Tera language extension
2. Open a process monitor (e.g. `btop`)
3. Create a file and set the language to Tera HTML
4. Start typing `{% extends foobar.html %}` (foobar.html does not need to exist to trigger this bug)
5. Observe the memory and CPU use

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behaviour: Zed enters an infinite loop, a CPU core runs at 100%, and memory is continuously allocated until the editor is closed. The syntax highlighting fails to update.

Expected behaviour: Zed would not enter an infinite loop and the syntax highlighting would update properly.

I am uncertain whether this is a flaw with the extension or with Zed itself.

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed with a clean installation/configuration.
2. Open any project.
3. Open the Project Panel.
4. Make sure there is a file or folder near the bottom of the visible Project Panel.
5. Right-click the file or folder.
6. Observe the context menu.
7. The context menu extends beyond the bottom edge of the Zed window, causing some menu items to be clipped and not fully visible.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior:**

When right-clicking a file or folder near the bottom of the Project Panel, the context menu can extend beyond the bottom edge of the Zed window. As a result, the lower menu items are partially or completely clipped and cannot be properly viewed.

This also occurs with a clean Zed configuration.

**Expected behavior:**

The context menu should automatically reposition itself so that the entire menu remains visible within the Zed window, even when the selected file or folder is near the bottom of the Project Panel.

For comparison, VS Code repositions the context menu when there is not enough space below the selected item, keeping the complete menu visible.

**Screenshots / screen recordings:**

A screen recording comparing the behavior in Zed and VS Code is attached.

Everything works fine when not going through ACP in Zed.

### Reproduction steps

> **AI-assisted diagnostic context**
>
> Source corruption occurred twice while OpenCode 2.0.6 was editing a Python file through Zed’s external-agent integration. This has not yet been reproduced from a clean installation.
>
> A candidate regression sequence, derived from the source:
>
> 1. Cache a buffer snapshot through an ACP read or resolved tool location.
> 2. Replace a word in the live buffer while retaining the earlier snapshot—for example, through an external file change and reload.
> 3. Call `write_text_file` with content containing that replacement.
> 4. Verify that the replacement is not inserted a second time.
>
> The sequence was examined using a reduced in-memory model, not Zed’s test runner.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

> **Observed:** valid patch output was followed by duplicated tokens outside the latest patch’s requested changes, including `unlink_ownedunlink_owned`, `selfself`, and `ifif`. One occurrence added 45 bytes across four lines. The preceding clean checkpoint passed 171 tests; replaying the next recorded patch against that checkpoint produced valid Python, unlike the resulting file.
>
> **Expected:** synchronizing updated file content must not replay replacements already present in the buffer.
>
> **Suspected mechanism:** [`write_text_file`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/49448afcab82f219b0ef4c58471cf81d23412475/crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs#L4308-L4326) prefers a cached `shared_buffers` snapshot, computes a diff against it, and anchors replacements inside the old text. It then [applies those edits and saves](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/49448afcab82f219b0ef4c58471cf81d23412475/crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs#L4343-L4383), without advancing the cached snapshot.
>
> For already-deleted original text, [`offset_for_anchor`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/49448afcab82f219b0ef4c58471cf81d23412475/crates/text/src/text.rs#L2529-L2541) collapses the old replacement range. body_text:
This is about GPUI (not the Zed app), the X11 backend.

### What happens

`Event::ConfigureNotify` takes `event.x` / `event.y` as the window's position on screen (`crates/gpui_linux/src/linux/x11/client.rs:966-982`). An X server generated `ConfigureNotify` carries the window's position **inside its parent**, and under a reparenting window manager that parent is the window manager's frame. Root coordinates come only from the *synthetic* `ConfigureNotify` the window manager sends alongside (ICCCM 4.2.3), or from asking with `TranslateCoordinates(window -> root)`.

Measured on GNOME Shell 46 / mutter, one 2560x1440 screen:

| | x | y |
|---|---|---|
| client window (`xwininfo -root -tree`) | 66 | 69 |
| frame | 52 | 20 |
| what gpui reports as `window_bounds().origin` | **14** | **49** |

14 = 66 - 52, 49 = 69 - 20. The reported origin is the inset into the frame.

Two consequences:

- Dragging the window does not change `origin` at all, because the window does not move inside its frame. An application that saves its window position saves the inset and restores the window somewhere else.
- The value is not even stable: gpui consumes both kinds of `ConfigureNotify`, so whichever arrived last decides whether `origin` is the inset or the real position.

### This is already in the tree twice, as workarounds

- `set_bounds` throws the origin away on a resize, with the comment *"we ignore `bounds.origin` because it contains wrong values"*. That came from #12604, fixing #11236. Its author wrote: *"In my case it would **always** contain x:14/y:49, which I think might map to the origin of the top bar in GNOME"* and *"I also tried the X11 `TranslateCoordinates` call but couldn't get meaningful results back"*. Those 14/49 are the frame inset in the table above. A side effect: a window dragged and resized in one gesture reports the position it had before the gesture.
- `X11Window::new` adds two pixels to the requested x, and nudges the window two pixels further when `GetGeometry` says it was placed at the origin, *"to work around a bug where our rendered content appears outside the window bounds when opened at the default position (14px, 49px on X + Gnome + Ubuntu 22)"*. That "default position" is this bug. Once an application really does restore a saved position, the two pixels are added on every run and the window walks right across the screen, two pixels at a time.

### Expected

`window_bounds().origin` is where the window is on the screen, so an application can save it and open there next time.

### A fix that works here

Tell the two kinds of event apart by the top bit of `response_type` (set for anything delivered by `SendEvent`), trust the synthetic one, and translate the server-generated one:

```rust
const SENT_BY_A_CLIENT: u8 = 0x80;
let origin = if event.response_type & SENT_BY_A_CLIENT != 0 {
    Point { x: event.x.into(), y: event.y.into() }
} else {
    // release the client-state borrow before this round trip
    xcb.translate_coordinates(event.window, root, 0, 0)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|cookie| cookie.reply().ok())
        .map_or(
            Point { x: event.x.into(), y: event.y.into() },
            |reply| Point { x: reply.dst_x.into(), y: reply.dst_y.into() },
        )
};
```

With this in, both workarounds above can go: `set_bounds` can keep the origin on a resize, and the two-pixel nudge in `X11Window::new` is unnecessary (it has to go, or it keeps walking the window).

Measured after the change: a dragged window reports where it actually is, and a saved position opens in the same place across restarts.

Full patch, on top of 0.2.2: https://github.com/Yahook/gpui/commit/15a2891 (see `PANEFOLD.md` in that repository for the measurements).

### Zed version and system specs

Not the Zed app: GPUI. The numbers were measured on `gpui` 0.2.2 from crates.io (published 2025-10-22, still the newest release) and on a fork of it with the fix applied. The code quoted from `zed-industries/zed` `main` @ `74a6468` was read, not run — the lines quoted are unchanged from 0.2.2 apart from the move into `crates/gpui_linux/`.

OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Linux 6.8.0, GNOME Shell 46.0 / mutter, X11 session (compositing), one 2560x1440 screen, `_NET_WORKAREA = 66, 32, 2494x1408`
Rust: 1.96.1

Only tried on GNOME Shell / mutter. Not tried on any other window manager, and not on Wayland.

`Event::ConfigureNotify` takes `event.x` / `event.y` as the window's position on screen (`crates/gpui_linux/src/linux/x11/client.rs:966-982`). An X server generated `ConfigureNotify` carries the window's position **inside its parent**, and under a reparenting window manager that parent is the window manager's frame. Root coordinates come only from the *synthetic* `ConfigureNotify` the window manager sends alongside (ICCCM 4.2.3), or from asking with `TranslateCoordinates(window -> root)`.

Measured on GNOME Shell 46 / mutter, one 2560x1440 screen:

| | x | y |
|---|---|---|
| client window (`xwininfo -root -tree`) | 66 | 69 |
| frame | 52 | 20 |
| what gpui reports as `window_bounds().origin` | **14** | **49** |

14 = 66 - 52, 49 = 69 - 20. The reported origin is the inset into the frame.

Two consequences:

- Dragging the window does not change `origin` at all, because the window does not move inside its frame. An application that saves its window position saves the inset and restores the window somewhere else.
- The value is not even stable: gpui consumes both kinds of `ConfigureNotify`, so whichever arrived last decides whether `origin` is the inset or the real position.

### This is already in the tree twice, as workarounds

- `set_bounds` throws the origin away on a resize, with the comment *"we ignore `bounds.origin` because it contains wrong values"*. That came from #12604, fixing #11236. Its author wrote: *"In my case it would **always** contain x:14/y:49, which I think might map to the origin of the top bar in GNOME"* and *"I also tried the X11 `TranslateCoordinates` call but couldn't get meaningful results back"*. Those 14/49 are the frame inset in the table above. A side effect: a window dragged and resized in one gesture reports the position it had before the gesture.
- `X11Window::new` adds two pixels to the requested x, and nudges the window two pixels further when `GetGeometry` says it was placed at the origin, *"to work around a bug where our rendered content appears outside the window bounds when opened at the default position (14px, 49px on X + Gnome + Ubuntu 22)"*. That "default position" is this bug. Once an application really does restore a saved position, the two pixels are added on every run and the window walks right across the screen, two pixels at a time.

### Expected

`window_bounds().origin` is where the window is on the screen, so an application can save it and open there next time.

### A fix that works here

Tell the two kinds of event apart by the top bit of `response_type` (set for anything delivered by `SendEvent`), trust the synthetic one, and translate the server-generated one:

```rust
const SENT_BY_A_CLIENT: u8 = 0x80;
let origin = if event.response_type & SENT_BY_A_CLIENT != 0 {
    Point { x: event.x.into(), y: event.y.into() }
} else {
    // release the client-state borrow before this round trip
    xcb.translate_coordinates(event.window, root, 0, 0)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|cookie| cookie.reply().ok())
        .map_or(
            Point { x: event.x.into(), y: event.y.into() },
            |reply| Point { x: reply.dst_x.into(), y: reply.dst_y.into() },
        )
};
```

With this in, both workarounds above can go: `set_bounds` can keep the origin on a resize, and the two-pixel nudge in `X11Window::new` is unnecessary (it has to go, or it keeps walking the window).

Measured after the change: a dragged window reports where it actually is, and a saved position opens in the same place across restarts.

Full patch, on top of 0.2.2: https://github.com/Yahook/gpui/commit/15a2891 (see `PANEFOLD.md` in that repository for the measurements).

body_text:
This is about GPUI (not the Zed app), the X11 backend.

### What happens

Whatever position is put in `WindowOptions { window_bounds: Some(WindowBounds::Windowed(bounds)), .. }`, mutter places the window where it likes.

Measured on GNOME Shell 46 / mutter: asked for `+300+650`, the window opens at mutter's own `+116+119`. Sampling the position every few milliseconds through a start shows a single placement at mutter's spot; nothing later moves it.

### Why

`crates/gpui_linux/src/linux/x11/window.rs:541-551` passes the position to `create_window`, which is only a *request*. `WM_NORMAL_HINTS` is where a client says the position is deliberate, and gpui writes only sizes into it (`window.rs:779-793`: `min_size` when `window_min_size` was given, plus `max_size` from the GPU's maximum texture size). There is no `USPosition` / `PPosition` flag.

ICCCM 4.1.2.3 leaves a window manager free to place a window that does not claim its position is meant, and mutter takes that freedom.

### Expected

A position given in `WindowOptions` is the position the window opens at — otherwise an application cannot restore its window where the user left it.

### A fix that works here

Always write the hints, with a user-specified position and static gravity:

```rust
let mut size_hints = WmSizeHints::new();
size_hints.position = Some((
    WmSizeHintsSpecification::UserSpecified,
    bounds.origin.x.0,
    bounds.origin.y.0,
));
size_hints.win_gravity = Some(xproto::Gravity::STATIC);
size_hints.min_size = params.window_min_size.map(|s| (s.width.0 as i32, s.height.0 as i32));
size_hints.set_normal_hints(xcb, x_window)?;
```

The gravity is not optional: without `STATIC` the position is taken as the frame's, and the window opens one title bar lower than asked, every single time.

Note this bug and #64445 interact — with the position honoured but the reported origin wrong, an application that saves and restores its window still drifts. Both have to be fixed for saving a window position to work on X11.

Measured after the change: asked for `+300+650`, the window opens at `+300+650`, and there is exactly one placement during startup instead of mutter's spot followed by a correction.

Full patch, on top of 0.2.2: https://github.com/Yahook/gpui/commit/15a2891

### Zed version and system specs

Not the Zed app: GPUI. The numbers were measured on `gpui` 0.2.2 from crates.io (published 2025-10-22, still the newest release) and on a fork of it with the fix applied. The code quoted from `zed-industries/zed` `main` @ `74a6468` was read, not run — the lines quoted are unchanged from 0.2.2 apart from the move into `crates/gpui_linux/`.

body_text:
This is about GPUI (not the Zed app), the X11 backend.

There is an open PR for this, #59570, and the measurements below say its X11 half does not work on mutter. Filing the bug separately so it is tracked, and so the measurement is somewhere the PR author can find it.

### What happens

A window opened with `WindowBounds::Maximized(bounds)` opens at `bounds`, plain. Measured on GNOME Shell 46 / mutter: asked for `900x600` maximized, the window opens `900x600` with an empty `_NET_WM_STATE` — not one maximized atom on it.

Check this at a size **unlike** `_NET_WORKAREA`, or it proves nothing: mutter maximizes a window of its own accord when the size asked for matches the work area, and the saved size of a maximized window always does. That is how the bug stayed hidden here for a while.

### Why

`crates/gpui/src/window.rs:1602` answers `WindowBounds::Maximized` with `platform_window.zoom()`, about two hundred lines before `map_window()` is called. Two things then go wrong at once:

1. `zoom()` on X11 (`crates/gpui_linux/src/linux/x11/window.rs:1670-1679`) sends a `_NET_WM_STATE` **client message**, and a window manager does not act on a state message about a window it has not been given yet. EWMH is explicit: a mapped window's state is changed by the message, an unmapped window's by the property.
2. The action it sends is `Toggle` — the only variant left in the enum, `Remove` and `Add` being commented out (`window.rs:914-918`). `Toggle` is the wrong verb when opening: if mutter has already maximized the window of its own accord (see above), a toggle undoes it.

### What I measured, in the order I tried it

| what | result on mutter |
|---|---|
| `_NET_WM_STATE = [_MAXIMIZED_VERT, _MAXIMIZED_HORZ]` set as a **property before `MapWindow`** — what EWMH prescribes, and what #59570 does | **ignored**: window stays at the requested size, and mutter replaces the property with its own, empty |
| `_NET_WM_STATE` **message right after `MapWindow`** | ignored — the window manager has not taken the window yet |
| `_NET_WM_STATE` message with action `Add`, sent from the **`MapNotify` handler** | works |

The first row is not a gpui measurement. It is a bare 40-line `xcffib` client that creates two 900x600 windows, sets the property on one before mapping it, maps both and looks at them 2.5 s later:

```
workarea: (66, 32, 2494, 1408)
no property before map:            size=900x600  _NET_WM_STATE=[]
property set before map:           size=900x600  _NET_WM_STATE=[]
```

So the property route is a correct reading of EWMH that mutter does not honour. I have not tried it on any other window manager, and it may well work on some.

### Expected

`WindowBounds::Maximized` opens a maximized window.

### A fix that works here

Give `PlatformWindow` a `set_maximized(bool)` with a default body of the old `zoom()`, so no other backend changes, and have `Window::new` call it instead of `zoom()` for `WindowBounds::Maximized`. X11 remembers a maximize asked for before the map and sends it, as an **add**, from the `MapNotify` handler:

```rust
// in the Event::MapNotify arm, after the client-state borrow is released
if let Some(window) = self.get_window(event.window) {
    window.maximize_if_asked();
}
```

`Remove = 0` and `Add = 1` have to come back into `WmHintPropertyState` for this.

Measured after the change: a window saved `900x600 maximized` opens maximized, and unmaximizes back to `900x600` where it was left.

Full patch, on top of 0.2.2: https://github.com/Yahook/gpui/commit/15a2891

### Zed version and system specs

Not the Zed app: GPUI. The numbers were measured on `gpui` 0.2.2 from crates.io (published 2025-10-22, still the newest release) and on a fork of it with the fix applied. The code quoted from `zed-industries/zed` `main` @ `74a6468` was read, not run — the lines quoted are unchanged from 0.2.2 apart from the move into `crates/gpui_linux/`.

OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Linux 6.8.0, GNOME Shell 46.0 / mutter, X11 session (compositing), one 2560x1440 screen, `_NET_WORKAREA = 66, 32, 2494x1408`
Rust: 1.96.1

Only tried on GNOME Shell / mutter. Not tried on any other window manager, and not on Wayland.

body_text:
This is about GPUI (not the Zed app), the X11 backend.

### What happens

Minimizing a maximized window makes gpui report it as a plain window the size of the screen. `window_bounds()` turns from `WindowBounds::Maximized(..)` into `WindowBounds::Windowed(..)` around the same rectangle, so an application that saves its window on the way out saves a maximized window as a windowed one and opens it that way next time.

### Why

`crates/gpui_linux/src/linux/x11/window.rs:1387-1392`:

```rust
fn is_maximized(&self) -> bool {
    let state = self.0.state.borrow();

    // A maximized window that gets minimized will still retain its maximized state.
    !state.hidden && state.maximized_vertical && state.maximized_horizontal
}
```

### Reproduction steps

### Reproduction steps
1. Open Zed on GNOME Wayland, 1366x768 builtin display
2. Resize to 3/4 screen manually (don't maximize)
3. Click minimize `-` in titlebar, restore from dock
4. Window is now larger than screen / overflows, can't reach borders. Repeats every time.
5. Fresh start after deleting `db.sqlite-wal/shm` opens maximized and same overflow happens on next minimize/restore cycle.

### Expected vs actual
Expected: restore to pre-minimize size fitting inside 1366x768.
Actual: window larger than screen, overflows edges.

### System specs
Zed Stable: v1.20.2+stable.360.7c451e694f3c52ee0aeb01d7e28b5fa18cd0ad2f
Zed Preview: v1.21.0+preview.358.808200ff7cc78214bb9a6040b52a4d6b35e80c78
OS: Linux Wayland fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.4
Memory: 7.6 GiB, x86_64
Monitor: eDP-1 BOE 1366x768@60.012 scale 1.0
GPU: Intel HD Graphics 520, Mesa 26.1.8 (vulkaninfo fails in --system-specs, but Zed.log shows `Using GPU: Intel HD Graphics 520 Vulkan`)

GNOME:
- `auto-maximize`: tested `true` -> `false`, still reproduces (currently `false`)
- `text-scaling-factor`: 0.82 (tested 1.0 temporarily, still reproduces, reverted to 0.82)
- `button-layout`: `:minimize,maximize,close`
- extensions: aqua-dock-pro, gsconnect, blur-my-shell, show-desktop-plus, caffeine (tested with dock/blur/show-desktop disabled + logout/in, still reproduces, re-enabled)

Backend:
- Initially ran via XWayland: `x11::window / Using scale factor from Xft.dpi: 0.8229167`
- Now native Wayland: `wayland::client activation token received with no pending activation` x3, still reproduces

### Tried, no fix
- Zed Preview same as Stable
- Native Wayland vs XWayland
- `gsettings set org.gnome.mutter auto-maximize false`
- `text-scaling 1.0` temporarily
- Extensions off temporarily
- `rm db.sqlite-wal db.sqlite-shm` (backed up `db.sqlite`) for 0-preview, also tested 0-stable path

### Zed.log snippet
2026-09-18T16:01:52+01:00 ERROR gpui_linux::linux::wayland::client activation token received with no pending activation
2026-09-18T16:05:18+01:00 ERROR gpui_linux::linux::wayland::client activation token received with no pending activation
2026-09-18T16:05:31+01:00 ERROR gpui_linux::linux::wayland::client activation token received with no pending activation

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behaviour:
Minimize via titlebar - then restore from dock → Zed window comes back larger than the 1366x768 display, overflowing past screen edges. Can't grab borders to resize. After db.sqlite reset it opens maximized and the next minimize/restore overflows again. Happens on stable 1.20.2 and preview 1.21.0, native Wayland, auto-maximize false.
Expected behaviour:
Restore to pre-minimize size/position inside the work area. Maximized should fit exactly inside 1366x768 minus top bar/dock, never overflow.

### Reproduction steps

1. Install Zed on Windows (clean install, default settings) and have a WSL2 distro (Ubuntu 24.04 here).
2. In a WSL shell, run the `zed` CLI that the Windows installer puts on the PATH (`C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Programs\Zed\bin\zed`) with an SSH URL. The host doesn't have to exist, because it fails before connecting:
   ```sh
   zed ssh://user@example.com/tmp
   # also fails:
   zed --new ssh://user@example.com/tmp
   zed zed://ssh/example.com/tmp
   ```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior: the CLI prints the following and exits with code 1. No window opens and nothing is written to Zed.log:

```
cannot open multiple different remote connections
```

Expected behavior: Zed opens the SSH remote project, the same as it does from PowerShell/cmd. Calling `zed.exe` directly from the same WSL shell works:

```sh
/mnt/c/Users/<you>/AppData/Local/Programs/Zed/bin/zed.exe --new ssh://host/path   # works
```

AI-generated root-cause analysis (Claude Code), pasted as-is:

> Cause: the WSL wrapper script `crates/zed/resources/windows/zed.sh` always adds `--wsl "$USER@$WSL_DISTRO_NAME"` when `$WSL_DISTRO_NAME` is set. `OpenRequest::parse` in `crates/zed/src/zed/open_listener.rs` then sets `remote_connection` to a WSL connection before it reads the URLs. `parse_ssh_file_path` sees an existing remote connection that is not the SSH one and fails with `cannot open multiple different remote connections`. With `ZED_WSL_DEBUG_INFO=true`, the wrapper shows the command it runs:
>
> ```
> + /mnt/c/Users/<you>/AppData/Local/Programs/Zed/bin/zed.exe --wsl darren@Ubuntu-24.04 --new ssh://host/path
> cannot open multiple different remote connections
> ```
>
> A possible fix is for `zed.sh` to skip `--wsl` when the arguments contain `ssh://` / `zed://ssh` URLs, or for the CLI to ignore the injected `--wsl` for SSH URLs.

It's pretty obvious that --wsl conflicts with the --new flag. You can't assume ever invocation of zed is intended for a local directory.

### Zed version and system specs

OS: Windows 10.0.26200
Memory: 59.6 GiB
Architecture: x86_64
WSL version: 2.9.10.0 (kernel 6.18.40.1-1), distro Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS

Nothing is logged. The error goes back to the CLI before the app handles the request.
